links: Simulee (ICSE 2020) Table 2 lists this revision as a known data-race bug (arXiv 1905.01833)
kernel: scan_nonfinal_kernel (scan_first_by_key_impl.hpp) and the dim variant in scan_dim_by_key_impl.hpp
location_buggy: scan_first_by_key_impl.hpp:L143-L158 (read s_ftmp[tidy] at L145 vs write s_ftmp[tidy] at L157); scan_dim_by_key_impl.hpp:L162-L177 (read s_ftmp[tidx] L164 vs write L176), all at buggy_commit
race_description: After the segmented-scan loop, thread tidx==0 reads s_ftmp[tidy] to decide the segment boundary while the last thread of the row (isLast) overwrites s_ftmp[tidy] (and s_tmp[tidy]) a few lines later with no __syncthreads in between. For DIMX>32 (and in the dim variant, tidy==0 vs tidy==DIMY-1) the two threads are in different warps, so the write can land before the read. Same for the by-key dim kernel.
fix_summary: Insert one __syncthreads() after the 'Identify segment boundary' block in both CUDA scan-by-key kernels (OpenCL kernels were fixed in the same commit).
evidence: Commit title 'BUGFIX: Add missing syncthreads to scan_by_key'. Listed by Simulee as a known data race (test_arrayfire_scan_nofinal_kernel / scan_dim_nofinal in its repo).
driver: The first-dim variant needs out.dims[0] >= 8193 (blocks_x = divup(dims0, threads_x*REPEAT) with REPEAT=32 and threads_x=256), not 'a few thousand'. The dim variant (scanByKey with scanDim=1) needs only dims[1] >= 257 (threads_y=8, REPEAT=32), e.g. dims (32, 300), and is much cheaper. test/scan.cpp's ScanByKey tests (16*1024 x 1024, scanDim 0) already exercise the first-dim path but have 16M elements.
build_notes: 2016 ArrayFire needs CMake + boost + old CUDA APIs (texture references were removed in CUDA 12), so the whole library will probably not build with CUDA 13. Recommended: extract scan_nonfinal_kernel plus its headers (Param/CParam, Binary, Transform) into a standalone .cu and launch it with DIMX=64/128; the kernel needs only math helpers.
dispute_points: For DIMX<=32 the two threads share a warp and pre-Volta lock-step hides the race; the cross-warp case (DIMX>=64) is the unambiguous one. Whether racecheck reports the s_ftmp hazard depends on the launch config.

verify.notes: Commit title 'BUGFIX: Add missing syncthreads to scan_by_key' (Pavan Yalamanchili, 2016-06-16); the diff has one added barrier in each CUDA file and also changes the OpenCL kernels. The Simulee repo's README lists test_arrayfire_scan_nofinal_kernel and test_arrayfire_scan_dim_nofinal_kernel and its log contains the commit title, so that part of the evidence checks out. The read of s_ftmp is unconditional for the tidx==0 thread, so any input with at least two blocks triggers the pair. location_buggy: csrc/kernels.cu:L653-L664 at 344e8516 (init loop `temp_storage.smem_qidx[j] = -1` L654-655 for all 512 threads, then `if (threadIdx.x < 256) temp_storage.smem_qidx[local_idx] = threadIdx.x;` L657-662, first __syncthreads after both at L664); smem_qidx[4096] is a union member aliasing the CUB sort/load temp storage
race_description: After the block radix sort, all 512 threads fill smem_qidx[0..4095] with -1 in a strided loop (thread t clears t, t+512, ...), and threads 0..255 immediately scatter their index into smem_qidx[local_idx] where local_idx is the rank of the t-th quantile. Nothing separates the clear loop from the scatter, so a warp that clears late (e.g. warps 8-15 clear slots owned by warps 0-7's quantile positions) can overwrite a freshly scattered index with -1, dropping that quantile's contribution to the global atomicAdd accumulation.
fix_summary: Adds one __syncthreads() between the smem_qidx clear loop and the quantile scatter.
evidence: PR/commit title 'Fix race condition in kEstimateQuantiles (#1061)'; two-line diff adding a barrier. No sanitizer output in the commit message.
driver: tests/test_functional.py::test_estimate_quantiles (torch.rand(1024,1024) fp32/fp16 -> F.estimate_quantiles(A)); smaller: F.estimate_quantiles(torch.randn(16384, device='cuda')) (needs numel >= 4096 per block to avoid the half-block skip; 4 blocks x 512 threads; BlockRadixSort dominates the access count, ~1e7 thread accesses). Launches kEstimateQuantiles via lib.cestimate_quantiles_fp32 / _fp16.

kernel: cms::cuda::multiBlockPrefixScan<T> (global kernel; per-block scan, then last-block-done combines partial sums)
location_buggy: HeterogeneousCore/CUDAUtilities/interface/prefixScan.h: writes co[i] at L22 (warpPrefixScan) and L77 (`co[i] += ws[warpId-1]`); counter atomicAdd at L155; last-block read `psum[i] = co[j]` at L172; last-block write `co[i] += psum[k]` at L179
race_description: Each block writes its partial scan into co[], then thread 0 bumps the global block counter pc with atomicAdd. The block that sees count == gridDim.x-1 reads co[blockDim.x*i + blockDim.x-1] written by all other blocks. There is no __threadfence() between the block's co[] writes and the counter increment, so the writes are not ordered before the counter (no release) and the last block's reads are not ordered after it (no acquire); co/ci were also plain (cacheable) loads.
fix_summary: Adds __threadfence() before the atomicAdd on the block counter and accesses ci/co through volatile pointers in the kernel; also adds a host-side atomicCAS shim and a templated blockPrefixScan signature.
evidence: Commit title 'Fix a possible data race in the prefix scan' (V. Innocente, Aug 2020). Wording 'possible' suggests it was found by review rather than reproduced.
driver: HeterogeneousCore/CUDAUtilities/test/prefixScan_t.cu (exists at the parent): main() loops multiBlockPrefixScan over num_items = 2000, 20000, 200000 with 1024 threads/block (2, 20, 196 blocks) and uint32 data, then verify(); total well under 1e7 accesses. The same file also launches the block- and warp-level scans (testPrefixScan, testWarpPrefixScan) which are useful extra targets.
build_notes: No CMSSW build needed: compile prefixScan_t.cu with nvcc -arch=sm_89 -I<repo root at 37a05c6b> plus a tiny shim for FWCore/Utilities/interface/Likely.h (included by cudaCheck.h) and requireDevices.cc (cudaGetDeviceCount check). Needs headers cudaCompat.h, cuda_assert.h, cudaCheck.h, requireDevices.h from the same tree. CUDA 13 compatibility of 2020 headers: probably fine for these small headers (unverified). Fetch blobs with git show <sha>:<path>.
already_reported_check: Not searched on GitHub issues/PRs; cmssw PR number is unverified (merge commit not inspected).
dispute_points: Fence-based hand-off: the race only exists in the formal memory model; on real hardware the missing fence rarely misorders. The fix mixes a fence with volatile, so fix_is_sync_only is false. A detector that does not model atomic+fence happens-before will keep reporting the fixed version too.

verify.strong_accesses: none at the buggy sha (the fix makes ci/co volatile)

location_buggy: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmid.cu:L95-L106 at 9e0e2205 (store[] written at L96, read at L106 by different lanes; only shfl/warp_reduce between)
race_description: Lanes of the single warp write compacted records into the dynamic shared array `store` (store[it_compact + it_compact_add_lower]) and, after the loop, a different lane mapping (itc = threadIdx.x; itc += warp_size) reads store[itc]. Only __shfl_*_sync / warp_reduce_sum separate the two phases, which CUDA does not define as a memory barrier, so on Volta+ (independent thread scheduling) the read is unordered w.r.t. the write.
fix_summary: Added ggml_cuda_syncwarp() (= __syncwarp() on NVIDIA, no-op on HIP) after the nex_prev warp_reduce_sum.
evidence: PR 28475 body only says 'Fixes races reported --tool=racecheck when running test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT_ID'. It does not attribute a hazard to mm_ids_helper; the same commit adds many __syncwarp in mmf.cuh and only wraps the existing one in fattn-vec.cuh. Issue 28376 (code reading, no log) names exactly this pair and proposes __syncwarp before warp_reduce_sum.
driver: The proposed case (f16, n_mats=16, n_used=16, m=32, n=1024, k=16) does NOT reach mm_ids_helper. should_use_mmf() rejects it because src0_ne[0]=16 % (32*(4/2)) != 0, and f16 is not an mmq type, so it falls to the host-sorted generic path. Use a case that reaches the helper: quantized type with n>8, e.g. -p 'type_a=q4_0,type_b=f32,n_mats=8,n_used=4,b=0,m=512,n=32,k=256' (mmq.cu:200), or f16 with k multiple of 64 and ncols>16, e.g. 'type_a=f16,type_b=f32,n_mats=8,n_used=4,b=0,m=512,n=32,k=256' (mmf.cu:87). All appear in the test list at 9e0e2205. 'tiny' is optimistic: one 32-thread block per expert, up to n/(32/neu_padded) loop iterations.
dispute_points: Skeptic: a full-mask __shfl_sync converges the warp so the compiler/hardware ordering holds in practice; the report is a sanitizer/spec-level hazard. Maintainers accepted it and fixed it, and racecheck reported it.

kernel: block_reduce<> as used by soft_max_f32 (and group_norm_f32, soft_max_f32_parallelize_cols_single_row)
location_buggy: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/common.cuh:L630-L649 (shared_vals[warp_id] = val at L638, shared_vals[lane_id] read at L643); softmax.cu:L102 and L120 call block_reduce twice with the same buf_iw
race_description: block_reduce writes one partial per warp into shared_vals, __syncthreads, then lanes read shared_vals[lane_id]. soft_max_f32 calls it twice (max, then sum) with the same buf_iw and no barrier in between, so a fast warp starts the second reduction and overwrites shared_vals[warp_id] while a slower warp is still reading the max partials from the first call.
fix_summary: Added `__syncthreads()` before the second block_reduce in soft_max_f32 (block_size > WARP_SIZE); double-buffered the shared array in the single-row cooperative-groups softmax; used s_sum + 32 in group_norm_f32; documented that callers must not reuse shared_vals.

kernel: ssm_scan_f32<splitD, N, L_template> (Mamba-1 selective scan, USE_CUB path and smemB/smemC)
location_buggy: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ssm-scan.cu:L69-L70 (two BlockLoad calls reuse cub_temp_storage.load_temp with no barrier) and L83-L108 (smemB/smemC rewritten at L87-L88 of iteration i+1 while other threads still read them at L103-L104 of iteration i; only one barrier per iteration at L90)
race_description: Two shared-memory reuse hazards in one kernel: (1) cub::BlockLoad's TempStorage is reused by the second Load without the __syncthreads CUB requires between uses; (2) in the L-loop threads < N write smemB/smemC for token i+1 right after the barrier of iteration i, but slower threads may still be inside the n-loop of token i reading smemB[n]/smemC[n] -- a missing trailing barrier.
fix_summary: Added __syncthreads() between the two BlockLoad calls and at the end of each loop iteration; removed unused dynamic smem.
evidence: PR 24360: 'Add required __syncthreads() to avoid data-races in ssm_scan_f32'; says it should resolve sporadic CUDA CI failures (verified on DGX Spark). Commit messages cite the CUB BlockLoad docs on TempStorage reuse. No racecheck log pasted.

kernel: cub::detail::topk::AgentTopK::finalize_pass (called from invoke_filter_and_histogram / the one-block-per-pass kernels launched by dispatch_topk.cuh)
location_buggy: cub/cub/agent/agent_topk.cuh:L431-L450 (merge_histograms atomicAdd to global histogram), L642-L684 (finalize_pass: __threadfence at L652, thread 0 atomicInc of finished_block_cnt at L656-L660, then last block reads global histogram in compute_bin_offsets L584-L596) at buggy_commit
race_description: All threads of a block atomicAdd their histogram bins into the global histogram (merge_histograms), execute __threadfence(), and then thread 0 does atomicInc(&counter->finished_block_cnt) to announce that the block is done. There was no __syncthreads() between the per-thread fence/atomics and thread 0's atomicInc, so thread 0 can retire the block while other threads of the same block have not yet issued their histogram atomicAdds. The block that observes the last retirement then reads the global histogram (plain volatile loads in compute_bin_offsets) and may miss those contributions: unordered atomicAdd (other block, other thread) vs plain read (last block).
fix_summary: Add __syncthreads() after the __threadfence() and before thread 0's atomicInc in finalize_pass (comment: wait for all threads to finish merge_histograms before thread 0 signals completion).
evidence: The fix commit message is only the title. The PR #10627 page (WebFetch) shows no sanitizer output; the backport-label claim could not be verified from the page text and is unverified.
driver: cub/examples/device/example_device_topk_keys.cu or cub/test/catch2_test_device_topk_keys.cu; needs a multi-block launch, i.e. enough items that DeviceTopK::MinKeys/MaxKeys uses gridDim.x > 1 (try 1e5 to 1e6 int/float keys, k small). A 30-line program calling cub::DeviceTopK::MaxKeys on 1M floats suffices.
build_notes: Header-only; check out buggy_commit of NVIDIA/cccl and compile with nvcc -std=c++17 -arch=sm_89 -I cub -I thrust -I libcudacxx/include; DeviceTopK needs CUDA >= 12 and a C++17 host compiler. Not compiled here. Alternatively the CCCL bundled in CUDA 13.x toolkits (3.0-3.2 era) contains the same code if DeviceTopK is present in that version (unverified).
dispute_points: Race window is one thread's atomic vs the retirement signal, so the failure is rare at runtime (no failing test cited); a happens-before based detector should still flag the lack of ordering between thread t's global atomicAdd and the last block's plain read. Reviewer may ask whether the post-fix __threadfence-then-__syncthreads order is itself sufficient (the fix as merged is __threadfence then __syncthreads, then atomicInc); not our concern for the buggy-version ground truth.

location_buggy: modules/gpu/src/cuda/canny.cu:L278-L298 at ce42593f (unrolled k<16 loop: neighbour reads of volatile smem[18][18] at L282-L293, own-cell write at L296-L297, no barrier in loop; the pull-in barrier is only at L270)
race_description: 16x16 block (8 warps, each warp = two rows of the tile) does a 16-step flood fill on an 18x18 shared tile smem (declared volatile). In every step thread (tx,ty) reads its 8 neighbours smem[ty..ty+2][tx..tx+2] and, if any was 2, writes smem[ty+1][tx+1]=2. A thread in the last row of warp w and a thread in the first row of warp w+1 are neighbours: one writes the cell the other reads in the same barrier interval, and the 16 unrolled iterations contain no __syncthreads, so the propagation distance a cell sees depends on warp scheduling. volatile gives no inter-warp ordering.
fix_summary: Two __syncthreads() added inside the loop: one between the neighbour-read phase and the write (WAR) and one after the write (RAW for the next iteration). 4 added lines.
evidence: Bug #3562 'Missing __syncthreads in CUDA Canny (edgesHysteresisLocalKernel)' by Julien Demouth (NVIDIA), 2014-02-19, for 2.4.8: loop works on shared memory with no barrier, RAW/WAR hazards across warps, volatile does not guarantee anything. Fixed by Vladislav Vinogradov in PR #2380 (commit 7fd21d21) on 2.4, later merged forward. No racecheck output; found by inspection.
driver: cv::cuda::Canny (opencv_contrib modules/cudaimgproc, class CannyEdgeDetector, test modules/cudaimgproc/test/test_canny.cpp) on e.g. a 512x512 CV_8UC1 GpuMat; kernel launched with 16x16 blocks, grid = divUp(cols,16) x divUp(rows,16) (1024 blocks at 512x512, ~0.26M threads x 16 iterations x ~10 smem accesses ~ 4e7 accesses). The old modules/gpu/ path (cv::gpu::Canny, OpenCV 2.4.x) is the literal buggy code.

Extract edgesHysteresisLocalKernel from opencv_contrib modules/cudaimgproc/src/cuda/canny.cu (HEAD, L225-L307), delete the two __syncthreads() at L274 and L279 to recreate the buggy loop, and provide a 20-line PtrStepSzi (data, step, rows, cols, operator()(y,x)) stand-in. Input: int map filled with 0/1/2 (e.g. random, 2 sparse seeds) of 512x512; launch <<<(32,32),(16,16)>>>. Full build alternative: opencv_contrib with -DBUILD_LIST=core,imgproc,cudev,cudaarithm,cudaimgproc -DWITH_CUDA=ON.
dispute_points: Race is monotone (cells only go 1->2, 8-neighbour), so the end state after a later pass of edgesHysteresisGlobalKernel is mostly the same; at worst the local kernel under-propagates and the global kernel fixes it, so wrong output is unlikely to be observable (the reporter only claims no guarantee). Barrier placed after the 'if (x>=cols||y>=rows) return' in partial edge blocks (barrier with exited threads, accepted on sm_70+). At HEAD the fix is present, so the buggy code needs the barriers removed or a pre-2014 tree.

location_buggy: aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Embedding.cu:L44-L127 at 5b6caa6b (racing accesses: store L66 indices_batch[tid]=... in batch k+1 vs load L99 indices_batch[chunk_start-batch_start+threadIdx.x] in the last chunk of batch k)
race_description: The block loops over batches of blockDim.x*blockDim.y indices. At the top of each batch every thread stores its index into the shared array indices_batch[tid] with no preceding barrier. Warps still finishing the previous batch's last chunk read indices_batch[chunk_start-batch_start+threadIdx.x] (the match-mask compare after the chunk's second __syncthreads) so a fast warp's store for batch k+1 can overwrite what a slow warp of batch k is about to read. Needs a following batch large enough to re-store the last chunk: 2017..3072 indices on CUDA (block 32x32).
fix_summary: One __syncthreads() added at the top of the batch loop (5 added lines incl. comment).
evidence: Commit message (written by AI-assisted author, reviewed by a PyTorch maintainer) describes the shared indices_batch overwrite before any barrier; reproduced as run-to-run gradient changes when a co-tenant process shares the GPU (ROCm gfx1100/gfx950); no racecheck output quoted; commit says no unit test is possible.
driver: torch.nn.Embedding(V, D)(idx).sum().backward() or torch.ops.aten.embedding_dense_backward(grad[N,D], idx[N], V, -1, False) with 2017<=N<=3072, scale_grad_by_freq=False (dispatch at Embedding.cu L277: num_indices<=3072 && !scale_grad_by_freq). D=32 gives grid=1 block of 32x32. Roughly 10^5-10^6 thread accesses. Race is a happens-before violation so a detector should flag it even when it never manifests (bug is timing dependent at runtime).
build_notes: Kernel is in every released wheel up to v2.14.1 (verified v2.5.0 and v2.8.0 contain it; no release tag contains the fix yet): pip install torch (CUDA 12.x/13 wheel) is enough. Alternatively extract lines 44-127 (needs only C10_WARP_SIZE=32, WARP_BALLOT=__ballot_sync(0xffffffff,..), acc_type<float,true>=float) into a ~60-line .cu harness launched <<<ceil(D/32), dim3(32,32), 32*32*(4+4)>>>.
dispute_points: Race only matters when N in 2017..3072; the fix commit's own authors only saw wrong results under GPU time-slicing, so a skeptic may call it theoretical, but it is a textbook missing WAR barrier.

kernel: nearest_kernel<scalar_t> (THREADS=1024, one block per query point)
location_buggy: csrc/cuda/nearest_cuda.cu:L47-L57 at 817b767e (reduction loop; racing accesses: read of best_dist[thread_idx+i] / best_dist_idx[thread_idx+i] at L53-L55 vs write of best_dist[thread_idx]/best_dist_idx[thread_idx] at L54-L55 by thread thread_idx+i in the same iteration)
race_description: Block-wide arg-min over best_dist[1024] in shared memory is done in place with a stride-doubling loop whose only barrier is at the top of each iteration. In iteration i thread t reads best_dist[t+i]/best_dist_idx[t+i] while thread t+i may be writing its own best_dist[t+i]/best_dist_idx[t+i] (it executes the same 'compare with t+2i, copy if smaller' body in that iteration). Reads and writes of the same shared slot are therefore unordered within one barrier interval (cross-warp for i>=32, intra-warp for i<32), and the winner (value, index) pair can be torn or stale.
fix_summary: Replaced the in-place sliding reduction by a proper tree reduction: in step u only threads < THREADS>>(u+1) are active, thread t compares best_dist[(2t)<<u] with best_dist[(2t+1)<<u] and writes only to its own even slot, so reads and writes of one barrier interval are disjoint. Also fixes continue->break in the batch lookup (unrelated, perf/semantics).
evidence: Commit message is only 'fix nearest parallel reduction' (rusty1s, no issue/PR link, no sanitizer output). Diff shows the reduction loop rewritten from a stride loop reading idx+i to a disjoint-pair tree reduction; the barrier placement stays at the top of the loop.
driver: torch_cluster.nearest(x, y, batch_x, batch_y) -> nearest_cuda (x: [N,3] float32 cuda, y: [M,3]); any N,M, e.g. N=64, M=2000 (grid = N blocks of 1024 threads; all 1024 threads run the reduction regardless of M). Test file test/test_nearest.py in the repo.
build_notes: Kernel is self-contained apart from CHECK_CUDA macros in utils.cuh: extract nearest_kernel (L9-L63) into a ~40-line .cu harness launched <<<N,1024>>> with float x,y and int64 ptr_x/ptr_y = {0,N}/{0,M}. Release tags (git tag --contains on the fix): the fix is first in tag 1.5.9, so tag 1.5.8 or earlier is buggy; a source build against torch/CUDA 13 would be needed, so the standalone harness is preferred.
dispute_points: Commit message is terse and does not name a race; one could read it as a pure correctness fix of a wrong-result bug. The in-place stride loop is, however, objectively unordered (read of best_dist[t+i] vs write by thread t+i inside one barrier interval). Whether wrong results manifest on a given GPU is timing dependent; for i<32 old-GPU lockstep would hide it, for i>=32 it cannot.

kernel: gko::kernels::cuda::generic_kernel_col_reduction_2d_blocked (column reduction launched by run_kernel_col_reduction / run_kernel_col_reduction_cached when cols > warp_size)
location_buggy: common/cuda_hip/base/kernel_launch_reduction.hpp:L283-L324 at e0d4d6e0 (the for(block_col...) loop, block_partial store at ~L303, warp-0 read loop at ~L308-L318)
race_description: Each iteration of the grid-stride loop over column blocks writes block_partial[threadIdx.x] (256-entry __shared__ array), calls block.sync(), then warp 0 (threadIdx.x < 32) reads all 256 entries. There is no barrier after the warp-0 reads, so threads of warps 1..7 (and warp 0 itself) that finish their per-thread accumulation early can store block_partial[threadIdx.x] for the next block_col while warp 0 is still reading the previous iteration's values. Only happens when gridDim.y*32 < cols, i.e. cols > 65535*32 (grid y capped at 65535).
fix_summary: Introduces col_step = gridDim.y*warp_size and adds 'if (block_col + col_step < cols) block.sync();' at the end of the loop body so block_partial is not overwritten while still being read.
evidence: Commit message is only 'fix: synchronization for multiple iterations'; the in-code comment 'only sync if block_partial will be reused by another iteration' is the sole rationale. No racecheck output.
driver: Running run_kernel_col_reduction with cols just over 65535*32 works but launches 65535 blocks x 256 threads (16.8M threads), and the in-tree ReductionCol2D test (cols=65535*128+1, rows 0..10000) launches the same 16.8M-thread grid with 4 column-block iterations. Cheaper and equivalent: generic_kernel_col_reduction_2d_blocked is a plain template in gko::kernels::cuda (before the anonymous namespace at L346 of kernel_launch_reduction.hpp), so a stand-alone driver can launch it directly with gridDim=(1,1), 256 threads, cols=64, rows=8, which gives 2 loop iterations (col_step=32) and ~512 thread-accesses.

race_description: block_argmin and the superblock argmin tables are bit-packed arrays: several consecutive entries share one 32/64-bit word. Each thread calls set(i, v) which does a plain read-modify-write ('data_[w] &= ~mask; data_[w] |= v<<shift') on the shared word, so threads handling neighbouring blocks (same warp, or adjacent warps/blocks at word boundaries) lose each other's bits. kernel: Kokkos::Impl::CudaReductionsFunctor<FunctorType,ArgTag,false,false>::scalar_intra_warp_reduction (tail 'broadcast' of the warp result; used by every shuffle-free scalar parallel_reduce on Cuda)
location_buggy: core/src/Cuda/Kokkos_Cuda_ReduceScan.hpp:L551 at the buggy commit ('*value = *(value - lane_id);' right after the tree loop in scalar_intra_warp_reduction, which starts at L529); racecheck in the commit message reports the read/write pair at this line
race_description: After the warp tree reduction every lane executes '*value = *(value - lane_id)' to broadcast lane 0's result. Lane 0 therefore stores into slot value[0] (a self-assignment of the same value) while lanes 1..31 load from that same slot; the reads and the write are unordered (no __syncwarp between them), a read/write conflict on one shared address between two lanes of a warp.
fix_summary: Wraps the broadcast in 'if (lane_id != 0)' so lane 0 no longer writes the slot all other lanes read.
evidence: Commit message (Phil Miller, 2022-03-08) quotes compute-sanitizer --tool=racecheck output on a tiny reduction (./redtest 1): before the change a Read vs Write race at ReduceScan.hpp:551 in scalar_intra_warp_reduction with 144 hazards, after the change that pair is gone and one hazard (scalar_intra_block_reduction write vs a read in Parallel_Range.hpp:321) remains.
driver: Any scalar Kokkos::parallel_reduce on Cuda, e.g. a 20-line program 'Kokkos::parallel_reduce(Kokkos::RangePolicy<Kokkos::Cuda>(0,n), KOKKOS_LAMBDA(int i,double& u){u+=i;}, s)' with n=1..1000; the commit's own repro used n=1. Also core/unit_test TestReduce.hpp on Cuda.
build_notes: Same as kokkos-1: cmake -DKokkos_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DKokkos_ARCH_ADA89=ON (nvcc_wrapper or nvcc as CXX), build libkokkoscore, then a small program. Check out the parent of the fix commit (that is 87415792f, the kokkos-1 fix), so this race is present together with the later-fixed ones (kokkos-2/-3/-4).
already_reported_check: Reported by the author in the commit message itself with racecheck output; PR #4855 (not fetched).
dispute_points: Benign in practice: lane 0 writes back the value it already holds, so results are always right; it is only a formal read/write conflict, which racecheck reports. Overlaps with kokkos-1 (same PR, same function family, adjacent lines).

location_buggy: cpp/include/raft/matrix/detail/select_radix.cuh at 32df870d: histogram merge atomicAdd(histogram + i, histogram_smem[i]) at L322 (inside filter_and_histogram, L226-L325), then __threadfence() L750 and thread 0 atomicInc(&counter->finished_block_cnt) L754 with no __syncthreads in between; last block reads histogram in scan<>() L767 / choose_bucket L769 and out/out_buf in last_filter
race_description: Last-block-done pattern. Each thread merges its shared-memory histogram into the global per-row histogram with atomicAdd (and, in the early_stop path, writes out/out_buf), then executes __threadfence(); only thread 0 then does atomicInc on finished_block_cnt. Without a __syncthreads between the per-thread fence and thread 0's atomicInc, thread 0 can signal block completion before other warps of the same block have issued their histogram atomicAdds/writes, so the 'last block' reads an incomplete histogram (scan/choose_bucket) or misses output writes: the lagging thread's global write is not ordered before the last block's plain read.
fix_summary: Inserts __syncthreads() after the __threadfence() and before the thread-0 atomicInc, so all threads of the block have finished their writes and fences before the block publishes completion.
evidence: Commit message is just 'SelectK-race-condition-fix'; the explanation is the added code comment. PR 3041 (fetched) has no sanitizer output; it says the author reproduced it, it fixes the flaky test in issue 2997 (SelectKCsrTest/SelectKCsrTest_float_int.Result/39), and it merged 2026-05-27.
driver: The multi-block radix_kernel is used only when len > BlockSize*32 = 16384 (BlockSize is 512 for both 8- and 11-bit passes) and calc_grid_dim > 1; otherwise radix_topk_one_block is used and the race cannot occur. '10^4 columns' is therefore too small: use len >= ~50000 (the issue-2997 flaky test is SelectKCsrTest, CSR layout), a few rows, SelectAlgo kRadix8bits or kRadix11bits.
build_notes: Header-only kernel file; RAFT tests build via ./build.sh tests --limit-tests=MATRIX_TEST (needs rmm, cccl via CPM) or compile a tiny main including raft/matrix/select_k.cuh with raft::resources. Racing values: histogram array in global memory (counter/histograms workspace).
dispute_points: Maintainer-approved. The conflicting pair is atomic-vs-plain across blocks mediated by the counter; a detector that only models thread-0's atomicInc as the release must see that other warps' earlier accesses are not ordered before it (no barrier).

race_description: MoE top-K routing reduces candidates in stages through shared arrays. In each stage warp w first reads its 32-wide window sh_key[32w..32w+31] (and sh_payload/sh_idx) and then writes its K best into sh_key[w*K..w*K+K-1]; for K=8 and 256 experts (8 warps, 64 candidates > 32) warp 1 writes [8..15], which lies inside warp 0's read window [0..31], and nothing orders the two warps inside the stage (the only barrier is after the whole if-block). A fast warp can therefore overwrite entries a slower warp has not yet read, producing wrong top-K. routing_std_kernel has the same WAR through the alias max_red == sh_v: slow warps are still reading max_red[lane_id] while a fast warp starts writing its top-K into sh_v.
fix_summary: routing_*_topk_kernel: every thread loads its candidate (key/payload/idx) into registers and the block does __syncthreads() before any warp enters the K-iteration write phase; routing_std_kernel: adds __syncthreads() after the max-logit reduction because max_red aliases sh_v.

race_description: The kernel runs with exactly 32 threads (one warp) and stages a 4x16x18 byte tile in `__shared__ uint8_t block`. In the unpack phase lane t (block_idx=t/8, block_offset=t%8) writes columns block_offset and block_offset+8 of rows 0..15 of tile t/8. In the repack phase lane t reads block[i][srow..][scol..] with srow=(t%4)*2 and scol=t/4, i.e. elements written by a different lane (e.g. lane 0 reads block[1][0][0], written by lane 8). There is no __syncwarp or __syncthreads between the two phases, so the cross-lane store->load pair is unordered under the PTX memory model; it only works if the warp stays in lockstep.
fix_summary: Insert __syncwarp() (or __syncthreads()) between the unpack loop and the repack loop.
evidence: Code reading only: the whole kernel contains no __syncthreads/__syncwarp/shuffle. The project's test tests/test_repacking.py L106 calls autogptq_marlin_cuda.gptq_repack, so the kernel is exercised upstream, and results are checked for equality, but nothing was observed to fail.

location_buggy: src/colmap/mvs/patch_match_cuda.cu: shared reads in PhotoConsistencyCostComputer::Compute L488-L490 and L502 (local_ref_image.data[...]) vs shared writes in LocalRefImage::Read L360-L367 (row shift) and L371-L381 (new bottom row); the only barrier is the __syncthreads at L459 AFTER those writes. Row loops: ComputeInitialCost row loop L866-L884 (Read L869, Compute L881), SweepFromTopToBottom row loop L1003-L1255 (Read L1006, Compute L1133/L1168, early `continue` L1008-L1009); pinned HEAD 6db3867f (shallow clone, 2026-10-13)
race_description: The kernels run with 32-thread blocks (THREADS_PER_BLOCK=32, L25: 'do not change'), one block = one warp, and keep a sliding window of the reference image in a single __shared__ array of kNumRows x 96 floats. In each row iteration every lane first runs LocalRefImage::Read(row), which shifts the window up one row and writes a new bottom row, but only into its own columns (t, t+32, t+64); a __syncthreads (L459) then publishes these writes. Compute() reads the window at columns 32-R+t .. 32+R+t, i.e. columns owned by up to 2R other lanes. Nothing orders lane t's Compute reads of iteration r before lane t' writing the same column in Read(r+1) at the top of the next iteration: the barrier in Read(r+1) comes after its writes, and the loop back-edge has no __syncwarp/__syncthreads. In SweepFromTopToBottom the tail block also lets lanes with col >= width `continue` straight into the next Read while the other lanes are still in Compute (divergent).
fix_summary: Add __syncwarp() (or __syncthreads()) before the shift/write part of LocalRefImage::Read, or at the end of each row iteration (and make the `continue` path reach it). Cost is negligible.
evidence: Code reading only. grep finds no __syncwarp anywhere in src/colmap/mvs (only in generated third-party code). Possibly related but UNVERIFIED and speculative: colmap issue #3514 (open at fetch time; PatchMatch output is noise/empty on sm_100/sm_120 GPUs, compute_89/90 unaffected) and the NOTE at the top of patch_match_cuda.cu (L3-L8) that blames an nvcc miscompile of SweepFromTopToBottom; that thread contains no racecheck/synccheck/__syncwarp analysis and nobody has tied it to a race.
driver: `colmap patch_match_stereo --workspace_path <ws> --PatchMatchStereo.max_image_size 96 --PatchMatchStereo.window_radius 3 --PatchMatchStereo.num_iterations 1 --PatchMatchStereo.num_samples 5 --PatchMatchStereo.geom_consistency 0` on a tiny undistorted dense workspace (3 images, <=96 px; make with feature_extractor/exhaustive_matcher/mapper/image_undistorter). The kernels are launched <<<ceil(W/32),32>>> (L1375, L1434); ~1e7-1e8 shared accesses at this size (estimate, not measured). No unit test launches these kernels.

Cheaper alternative that still exercises the same code: copy LocalRefImage (L317-L383) and the Compute() window loop (L462-L545) into a standalone .cu, launch <<<ceil(W/32),32>>> over H rows with a plain texture or global array in place of tex2D; this reproduces the hazard but is not the original kernel. location_buggy: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/fattn-common.cuh:L332-L373 at master 1b70350c (unconditional `yq32[threadIdx.x] = q32;` at L365 vs `((float2 *) yds)[threadIdx.x/QI8_1] = make_float2(d, sum);` at L370); caller fattn-vec.cuh:L181 passes ni = nthreads_quantize = D/sizeof(int) = 16 for head size 64
race_description: When ni < WARP_SIZE (head size 64: ni == 16) lanes 16..31 still execute yq32[threadIdx.x] = q32 (zero padding) and so write yq32[16..31]. The caller lays yds = yq32 + D/4 = yq32 + 16, so yq32[16..19] alias yds[0..1], which lanes 0 and 8 write with make_float2(d, sum) in the same warp with no sync and different control-flow paths: write/write conflict on the same shared words, with the final value (d,sum or zero) depending on ordering; the __restrict__ qualifiers additionally let the compiler order the padding store last, silently zeroing Q_ds.
fix_summary: Proposed (PR 28358, unmerged): predicate the yq32 store with `(ni == WARP_SIZE || threadIdx.x < ni)`, mirroring the yds guard.
evidence: PR 28358 body: 'racecheck flags this in every flash_attn_ext_vec instantiation pairing head size 64 with quantized K (q8_0, q4_0)'; environment sm_120, `test-backend-ops -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT` under `--tool racecheck`; full FLASH_ATTN_EXT sweep 50 -> 0 hazard records after both fixes in the PR. Maintainer asked for logs (ORippler) and did not get them; PR closed by JohannesGaessler citing the AI usage policy. I verified the unconditional store is still present at master 1b70350c (2026-10-13).
driver: The vec kernel is only selected when K->ne[1] % FATTN_KQ_STRIDE(256) == 0 (can_use_vector_kernel). kv=113 in the proposed pattern is routed to the MMA kernel and never runs quantize_q8_1_to_shared. location_buggy: llmc/layernorm.cuh at f1e2ace6: partial stores L371-L372 (store128 to scratch_dbias/scratch_dweight + 2*C*blockIdx.x), atomicInc L378, last-block loads L391-L392 (load128). Record's L370-373 / L377-379 / L388-394 are within 1-3 lines.
race_description: Every block stores its per-block dbias/dweight partials into the global `scratch` buffer with plain 128-bit stores (store128), executes __syncthreads, then thread 0 does `atomicInc(scratchFlag, gridDim.x)`. The block that observes gridDim.x-1 reads all other blocks' partials with plain loads (load128). There is no __threadfence() (release) before the atomicInc and none (acquire) after it, so block A's stores to scratch and block B's loads are not ordered by happens-before under the PTX model: __syncthreads only orders within the CTA and a relaxed atomicInc to a different address does not publish prior stores.
evidence: The earlier kernel5 in dev/cuda/layernorm_backward.cu (the original last-block version, L527-L541) has `__threadfence();` between the scratch stores and the flag atomicAdd, i.e. the author knew the idiom; the later, faster kernels 9/10 (and the production llmc version) dropped it. grep for threadfence in the repo finds only that one occurrence. Matches the canonical CUDA threadFenceReduction sample, which has the fence.
driver: (a) dev/cuda/layernorm_backward.cu: `nvcc -O3 -lcublas layernorm_backward.cu -o lb; ./lb 10` (or 9, 8, 7, 6). main() hard-codes B=8,T=1024,C=1600 (~13M elements) so recompile with small B,T (e.g. B=2,T=64,C=768) to stay under 1e7 accesses; it checks results against a CPU reference. (b) production path: llmc/layernorm.cuh layernorm_backward() called from train_gpt2.cu gpt2_backward and test_gpt2cu.cu; much heavier. Grid is 2*numSMs blocks of 512 threads, so there are many blocks and the hand-off is exercised.
build_notes: dev/cuda is self-contained: `cd dev/cuda && make layernorm_backward` (needs nvcc, cublas; Makefile auto-detects capability). For kernels 9/10 the build uses floatX=float by default (add -DENABLE_BF16 for bf16).

dispute_points: (1) On real hardware this essentially always works because atomics execute at L2 after earlier stores from the same SM have drained; a skeptic will say 'not observable'. The detector follows PTX happens-before, under which it IS a race (message-passing without release/acquire), and the author's own earlier kernel5 includes the fence. (2) The detector must model atomicInc as relaxed (not acq_rel) and not treat the CTA-level __syncthreads as a GPU-scope fence; if it treats any atomic as a full fence it will miss this. race_description: Identical code shape to the reduction fixed upstream in nearest_cuda.cu (commit a5abfee). In step i thread t reads best_dist[t+i] and best_dist_idx[t+i] (three separate reads: compare, value copy, index copy) while thread t+i, in the same barrier interval, may overwrite exactly those two slots from slots t+2i. The (value,index) pair read by thread t can therefore be torn (value from the old, index from the new write or vice versa), which makes `out[m]` point to a point that is not the arg-max. Cross-warp for i>=32, intra-warp for i<32.
evidence: The author already rewrote the same loop as a disjoint-pair tree reduction in nearest_cuda.cu (a5abfee, 2020-12-07, 'fix nearest parallel reduction') but fps_cuda.cu kept the in-place form (git log of fps_cuda.cu since: only dtype/ratio/tensor-creation changes).

dispute_points: Maintainer might argue that the max-reduction is monotone so reading a newer value is harmless; but value and index are copied by separate loads, so a torn pair is possible. Disputable but formally a data race.

race_description: Each warp stages data in a shared buffer 'buf' (warp-size V elements): lanes store source elements into bufT[shmPos...], then lanes copy buf out to global memory and reset shmPos so the next loop pass stores into the same buffer. dispute_points: Race needs a cell reached by two different merge neighbourhoods (nrs>1) at a coarse-fine boundary; with flag_as_crse/levmsk all zero the branches are not taken. Floating point atomics make the fixed code order-nondeterministic.

location_buggy: src/operator/tensor/cast_storage-inl.cuh:L413-L458 at f75138fa (last thread stores block_nnz L440 vs all threads read block_nnz at k += block_nnz L454 of the previous iteration)

In iteration i every thread reads the __shared__ volatile block_nnz (k += block_nnz, L454) after a barrier; in iteration i+1 thread kBaseThreadNum-1 immediately stores block_nnz = nnz (L440) before any new barrier, while slower warps may not yet have read the value of iteration i. The k offsets (and hence write positions into val[]/col_idx[]) become wrong.

Extract the kernel (cub::BlockScan + __shared__ volatile block_nnz; ~45 lines) into a .cu harness with 256 threads per block and one block per row; kBaseThreadNum from mshadow (3rdparty/mshadow/mshadow/cuda/tensor_gpu-inl.cuh) -- value unverified.
dispute_points: Project is archived/retired; kernel uses cub::BlockScan whose internal barriers partially order things (the race is on the extra volatile variable only). Behaviour depends on warp scheduling.

location_buggy: src/backend/cuda/kernel/scan_dim.hpp:L86-L111 at buggy_commit: s_tmp[tidx] read at L105, rewritten by the isLast thread at L88 of the next iteration
race_description: All threads of a column read s_tmp[tidx] (carry from the previous chunk) at L105; in the next loop iteration the thread with tidy==DIMY-1 overwrites s_tmp[tidx] at L88 before any barrier that orders it after the slower readers (the first barrier of the next iteration is after L88). A reader in a different warp can therefore see the new carry (or the writer clobbers the value being read).
fix_summary: Add one __syncthreads() immediately after 'val = binop(val, s_tmp[tidx])' so all reads of s_tmp finish before the next iteration's write.
evidence: Commit message 'BUGFIX: for accum along non-first dimension' (one-line __syncthreads insertion in scan_dim.hpp). Matches a Simulee known data-race bug.
driver: af::accum(in, dim=1) (CUDA backend) on an array whose scan dimension is long enough that lim>1 (multiple chunks per block): e.g. 64x4096 floats; ArrayFire test/scan.cpp (accum tests along dim 1) exists at the buggy commit.

dispute_points: Needs lim>1 and DIMY>1; the race window is narrow so a happens-before detector is preferable to hoping for a wrong result.

location_buggy: src/backend/cuda/kernel/hamming.hpp at buggy_commit: unroll kernel L137-L143 (out_dist/out_idx read s_dist[0]/s_idx[0]) vs next-iteration L63 (s_dist[tid]=max_dist) and L88-89; same shape in hamming_matcher

With no trailing barrier, a fast thread (in particular thread 0) proceeds to iteration j+1 and overwrites s_dist[0]/s_idx[0] (s_dist[tid]=max_dist, s_dist[tid]=dist, s_idx[tid]=f) while threads in other warps are still reading them.

kernel: hamming_matcher_unroll and hamming_matcher (final min-reduction over s_dist/s_idx)
location_buggy: src/backend/cuda/kernel/hamming.hpp:L109-L134 (unroll) and L230-L255 (hamming_matcher) at buggy_commit
race_description: The last six reduction steps (offsets 32,16,8,4,2,1) run inside a single 'if (tid < 32)' block on plain (non-volatile) __shared__ arrays with no barrier or __syncwarp between steps: thread t reads s_dist[t+16] that lane t+16 wrote in the previous step. This is the legacy warp-synchronous idiom; the compiler may cache s_dist in registers and on Volta+ independent thread scheduling gives no lock-step guarantee.
fix_summary: Split the warp tail into separate 'if (tid < N)' steps each followed by __syncthreads().
evidence: Commit 'Added more syncs to hamming_matcher()'. Simulee flags it as a data race (test_arrayfire_hamming_matcher_*).

dispute_points: Pure intra-warp; on pre-Volta lock-step hardware the original is arguably correct (modulo missing volatile). A detector that models __syncwarp-less intra-warp accesses as unordered will flag it; one that assumes warp lock-step will not. Good ITS-sensitivity probe, not a clean 'maintainer-accepted real bug'.

location_buggy: catboost/cuda/targets/kernel/yeti_rank_pointwise.cu:L131-L159 at e0dda61c (loop over k<N=4; `weightDst[idx1] += ..; targetDst[idx1] += ll;` at L149-L152, __syncthreads at L153, `weightDst[idx2] += ..; targetDst[idx2] += -ll;` at L155-L158, NO barrier before the next k iteration)
race_description: In each k-iteration, thread with sorted position o does a plain read-modify-write on dst[idx1] (idx1 = indices[o-1]) and then on dst[idx2] (idx2 = indices[o]). Neighbouring positions share indices (thread o's idx2 == thread o+1's idx1), which is why a barrier separates the idx1 and idx2 phases. The barrier after the idx2 phase was missing: thread B-1 in iteration k (idx2 = indices[(k+1)B-1]) and thread 0 in iteration k+1 (idx1 = indices[(k+1)B-1]) update the same weightDst/targetDst element from different warps with no ordering -> lost update. The same commit makes the dst pointers volatile.
fix_summary: Adds __syncthreads() after the idx2 update (end of each k iteration) and makes targetDst/weightDst volatile so the compiler does not cache the RMW across the barrier.
evidence: Commit message 'fix possible race' (Vasily Ershov, Yandex, 2018) for the YetiRank pointwise gradient kernel; diff adds the missing barrier. No test or sanitizer output attached.
driver: CatBoost GPU training with loss_function='YetiRank' (or 'YetiRankPairwise'), task_type='GPU', tiny dataset (e.g. 2000 docs, 50 queries, <=1024 docs per query) - each boosting iteration launches YetiRankGradientImpl; Python: CatBoostRanker(loss_function='YetiRank', task_type='GPU', iterations=2). Same kernel remains at HEAD (L151-L163 contain the 'fixed' barriers).
build_notes: catboost builds with ya/ymake (or cmake generated files in catboost/cmake) - heavy. Practical: pip install catboost (GPU-enabled wheel; includes the FIXED kernel) is not useful for the buggy variant; for the buggy variant lift yeti_rank_pointwise.cu (needs catboost/cuda/cuda_util/{kernel_helpers,fill,sort...}.cuh headers and RadixSortSingleBlock4) into a standalone nvcc harness, or build catboost at the parent with the cmake build (README: build/build_native.py --targets _catboost with CUDA, 30+ min).
dispute_points: The authors hedge with 'possible race'. Whether neighbouring blocks processing disjoint queries can conflict: no, only within one query (one block). The conflict needs a query with > BLOCK_SIZE docs spanning multiple k iterations and the shared index at the iteration boundary. 2018-era code; sorting helper headers needed for a standalone build.

kernel: gpuClustering::findClus<isPhase2> via pixelStatus::promote() (shared-memory 2-bit pixel status words)
location_buggy: RecoLocalTracker/SiPixelClusterizer/plugins/gpuClustering.h:L44-L54 (promote) and L170-L185 (call sites) at ce8a57bd; status[] is __shared__ at ~L98
race_description: promote() reads the 2-bit status of a pixel with a plain load of the packed shared word, decides the target state (kFound or kDuplicate), then atomicOr's it. Two threads handling the same (x,y) pixel can both read kEmpty and both OR kFound, so the duplicate is never recorded; neighbouring pixels sharing the word also make the plain read race with the other threads' atomicOr. Plain read versus atomic write on the same word.
fix_summary: Replaces read + atomicOr with an atomicCAS retry loop on the packed word so the check and the update are one atomic step.
evidence: Commit title 'Fix a race condition in the pixel duplicate detection' (A. Bocci, Aug 2022); the diff is only the promote() function.
driver: RecoLocalTracker/SiPixelClusterizer/test/gpuClustering_t.cu (+ gpuClustering_t.h) launches countModules and findClus on synthetic digis. At the parent the generator (checked: no 'dupl' hits) does not feed duplicate pixels, so the driver must be modified to repeat some (x,y) entries in one module. Small (<= 1000 pixels per module).
build_notes: Standalone compile like cmssw-1: gpuClustering_t.h needs CUDADataFormats/SiPixelCluster/interface/gpuClusteringConstants.h, Geometry/CommonTopologies/interface/SimplePixelTopology.h, HistoContainer.h, cudaCompat.h, launch.h, device_unique_ptr.h, requireDevices.h and gpuClusterChargeCut.h; several of these pull more CUDAUtilities headers (allocators, FWCore Likely.h). Expect to vendor ~15 headers by git show; no scram needed.
already_reported_check: Not searched on GitHub issues/PRs; PR number unverified.
dispute_points: After the fix, the first 'status[index]' load of the CAS loop is still a plain read racing with other threads' atomicCAS, so a strict detector may still flag the fixed code (benign by construction). Needs duplicate-pixel input to trigger a wrong result.

kernel: vertexFinder::SplitVerticesKernel -> splitVertices (alpaka kernel, one vertex per block; compiles to CUDA with the alpaka CUDA backend)
location_buggy: RecoTracker/PixelVertexFinding/plugins/alpaka/splitVertices.h:L36-L125 at f6e0fc42 (shared nq/it/zz/newV/ww reset and refilled at the top of each vertex iteration; newV[k]/it[k] read in the last loop of the body)
race_description: Loop over vertices with shared buffers (nq, zz, newV, ww, it, igv). The last statement of an iteration reads igv, newV[k], it[k] in a uniform_elements loop; the next iteration begins with thread 0 resetting nq and then refilling zz/newV/ww/it. With no barrier at the end of the loop body, a fast thread overwrites the shared state while others still read it.
fix_summary: Adds alpaka::syncBlockThreads(acc) at the end of the loop on vertices (before the shared memory is reset); the rest is refactoring to SoA accessors.
evidence: Commit title 'Fix a race condition in splitVertices'; message says the barrier is added at the end of the vertex loop 'before resetting the shared memory'.
driver: Vertex-finder tests inside CMSSW (RecoTracker/PixelVertexFinding/test, alpaka variants); exact test name unverified. Needs vertices with chi2/ndof above maxChi2 and ndof >= 4 so the loop body runs more than once per block.
build_notes: Alpaka-CUDA build inside CMSSW (scram, alpaka headers, Eigen, SoA data formats). Not practical standalone without vendoring a large part of the alpaka tools; rank low.
already_reported_check: Not searched on GitHub issues/PRs.
dispute_points: The commit bundles the fix with a refactor, so the buggy parent differs textually in many places; a skeptic can say the missing barrier was benign only when each block handles at most one vertex. Practicality is low.

links: related earlier cleanup 'grid: Clean up GPU backend and fix race condition (#5338)' efe242d354f5092fb465bfc4887d87132df56df7
location_buggy: src/grid/gpu/grid_gpu_collocate.cu:L94-L113 (task loop: `__shared__ smem_task<T> task` refilled by fill_smem_task_coef L99 / compute_alpha L103 at the top of the next iteration while cab_to_cxyz L112 of the previous iteration may still be reading task/smem_alpha/smem_cab); src/grid/gpu/grid_gpu_integrate.cu:L78-L115 (compute_hab_v4: same task-loop reuse, no barrier after the ico/jco loops L92-L114), L152-L234 (compute_hab_v2: shared_forces_a/b/virial written at L176-L189 aliasing smem_alpha = shared_memory[0..] while the previous iteration still reads them at L221-L227), L574-L620 (integrate_kernel: sum[] written L612, read L617-L619, rewritten next batch) at buggy_commit
race_description: The grid kernels run with __launch_bounds__(64), i.e. two warps per block, and loop over the tasks assigned to the block while keeping per-task data (`task`, smem_alpha, smem_cab, shared_forces_*, sum[]) in shared memory. At the end of an iteration/batch there is no barrier, so a fast warp starts the next iteration and overwrites these shared objects (fill_smem_task_coef, compute_alpha, shared_forces_a[tid] = ..., sum[i] = val) while the other warp is still reading the previous values (WAR; also WAW on the aliased region at the start of shared_memory).
fix_summary: Adds __syncthreads() at the end of each task-loop iteration in calculate_coefficients, compute_hab_v4, compute_hab_v2 and after each batch in integrate_kernel, plus one before the force/virial staging in compute_hab_v2 (and a trailing one after the loop) and removes a redundant barrier.
evidence: Commit title 'Fix a race condition in the grid backend (#5437)' (Mathieu Taillefumier, 2026-06-23). Added comments in the diff: 'all warps need to be synchronized here before modifying the task information' and 'Important to synchronize the warps'. Preceded one day earlier by #5338 'grid: Clean up GPU backend and fix race condition'.

kernel: stack_mm_r / stack_mm_d / stack_mm_c / stack_mm_z (DBCSR small-matrix-multiply stack kernels)
location_buggy: cuda_tools/dbcsr_cuda_calc_r.cu:L97-L118 (thread 0 spins `lock_owner = atomicCAS(&c_locks[c_id], 0, sp_one)` L103-L104; `c_data[our_params[5]-1+tn] += myc;` L109-L111; unlock `c_locks[c_id] = 0; //threadfence();` L113-L118) at buggy_commit; the same block in the _d/_c/_z variants
race_description: Thread blocks multiply small blocks and add the product into a shared C block c_data[...] guarded by a spin lock (c_locks[c_id]): thread 0 acquires with atomicCAS, all threads do a plain `c_data[...] += myc`, thread 0 releases with a plain store `c_locks[c_id] = 0`. The unlock has no __threadfence (the call is commented out) and the acquire has no fence either, so the C updates of one block are not guaranteed visible to the next lock holder (and the plain += races formally with the next block's += as far as the memory model is concerned): lost updates / stale C reads between thread blocks.
fix_summary: Drops the lock: each thread now does atomicAdd directly on c_data (a CAS-loop atomicAdd(double*) is added to dbcsr_cuda.h because CUDA 5.0 lacks it); the c_locks arguments become unused.
evidence: Commit message: 'Fix a long standing bug in the cuda kernels. Locking of the C-block is not enough, a threadfence or an atomic update is needed to make this updated C available (via global memory) to all other CUDA blocks ... Here we go with an atomic update. (Ole)' (Joost VandeVondele, 2013-02-06, svn-origin-rev 12689).
driver: Extract stack_mm_r from cuda_tools/dbcsr_cuda_calc_r.cu and write a 50-line harness: param stack of e.g. 256 entries of 7 ints {m,n,k,a_off,b_off,c_off,c_id} that all target the same C block (c_id=1), m=n=k=8, blockDim=64, grid=stack_size, dynamic smem = (m*k+k*n)*sizeof(float) (see dbcsr_cuda_calc.cu L131 for the real launch). 256 blocks x 64 threads, a few 1e5 accesses.
build_notes: Kernels use the pre-CUDA-9 spellings `syncthreads()` and `threadfence()` which modern nvcc rejects: add `#define syncthreads() __syncthreads()` and `#define threadfence() __threadfence()`. The kernel is self-contained apart from dbcsr_cuda.h. On Volta+ the intra-warp spin loop (thread 0 only) is fine under ITS.
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream 2013).
dispute_points: Very old code; the DBCSR library later moved to its own repository (cp2k/dbcsr is on the skip list) and was rewritten. The data hazard here is a plain store used as lock release plus a missing fence; on current GPUs lock-free hardware behaviour often masks it, so a detector must model release/acquire to flag it. Single-precision variant used as the example; the double variant has an extra 170 changed lines.

location_buggy: csrc/flash_attn/src/flash_bwd_kernel.h:L1013-L1028 at a4e5d1ed (sdK aliases sK `make_tensor(sK.data(), SmemLayoutdKV)` L1013, sdV = sdK + size(sdK) L1014; guard `if (Kernel_traits::Is_V_in_regs && !Is_last) __syncthreads();` L1025; then `copy(smem_thr_copy_dKV, taccdKrdK, taccdKsdK)` L1027) vs the last-iteration dQ GEMM reading sK/sKt at L926 `flash::gemm(acc_dq, tdQrdS, tdQrKt, tdQsdS, tdQsKt, ...)`
race_description: In the backward kernel's epilogue every thread writes its dK/dV accumulators into shared memory at the location that holds sK and sV. For Is_last == false (sequence-parallel mode: Is_first=false, Is_last=false) the m_block loop ends without a __syncthreads (the loop-end barrier is only inside `if (Is_last)`), and the barrier before the epilogue write was only taken when Is_V_in_regs. A fast warp can therefore overwrite sK while a slow warp is still reading it in the final iteration's dQ GEMM (tdQsKt).
fix_summary: Make the pre-epilogue barrier unconditional for !Is_last: `if (!Is_last) { __syncthreads(); }` (was `Is_V_in_regs && !Is_last`). The commit also tightens test_flash_attn_race_condition (batch_size 60, d=128, seqlen=128, fp16, non-causal).
evidence: Fix commit title 'Fix race condition in bwd (overwriting sK)'; added comment: 'Without syncthreads, some thread might modify the location of sK while another thread is reading it for dQ gemm, leading to a race condition.' The same commit edits tests/test_flash_attn.py::test_flash_attn_race_condition to batch_size=60 with comment 'Sometimes we need large batch size for the race conditions to trigger'.

location_buggy: src/graph/transform/cuda/knn.cu:L327-L391 at c51cc82e (tile loop: smem stores data_buff[threadIdx.x*feature_size+i] at L331-L337 vs reads data_buff[d_idx*feature_size+dim_idx] at L349-L374 of the previous tile; no barrier at the end of the loop body)

No racecheck output quoted. Bundle of fixes: the barrier is only one of several causes of the instability.
driver: dgl.knn_graph(x, k, algorithm='bruteforce-sharemem') with x a CUDA float32 tensor [N, D] (e.g. N=4096, D=3, k=8) or dgl.segmented_knn_graph; unit test tests/compute/test_knn.py::test_knn_cuda. Block size = FindNumThreads(max_smem/single_smem) up to 1024 threads, one block per 'block_size' queries; each thread loops over all data points: with N=4096 about 4096*4096*(2*3) ~1e8 smem accesses, use N<=2048 to stay below 4e7.

kernel: ReduceX / Reduce1D / Reduce1DNotAlign device helpers, used by MapReduceKeepLowestKernel, MapReduceKeepDim1Kernel, SoftmaxKernel (tensor_gpu-inl.cuh)
location_buggy: mshadow/cuda/reduce.cuh:L62-L86 (in-warp tail of ReduceX: `if (tid < 16) Reducer::Reduce(buf[tid], buf[tid+16]);` ... `if (tid < 1) ...` on a `volatile DType buf[]`, separated only by the empty macro __MSHADOW_EMUSYNC__ L34-L38) at buggy_commit; callers tensor_gpu-inl.cuh L143 (MapReduceKeepLowestKernel, 32x32 block), L191 (MapReduceKeepDim1Kernel, 256 threads), L297/L315 (SoftmaxKernel)
race_description: The last five steps of the shared-memory tree reduction (strides 16,8,4,2,1) are executed by the lanes of one warp through a `volatile` buffer with no barrier between steps (the EMUSYNC macro expands to nothing outside device emulation). Lane tid reads buf[tid+stride] that another lane wrote in the previous step; this is only ordered by lock-step execution, which independent thread scheduling (Volta/sm_70+, including sm_89) no longer guarantees, so the reads can see stale values (and writes of step k+1 can overtake reads of step k).
fix_summary: Replaces __MSHADOW_EMUSYNC__ with __syncwarp() (defined to nothing for CUDA < 9) after every in-warp reduction step.
evidence: Commit title 'Adding __syncwarp() from CUDA 9 to unsafe warp-synchronous code (#263)' by Przemyslaw Tredak (NVIDIA), 2017-06-19. The title itself calls the code 'unsafe warp-synchronous'.
driver: mshadow GPU tensor ops, e.g. `Softmax(Tensor<gpu,2> dst, Tensor<gpu,2> src)` (SoftmaxKernel, 256 threads/row) or `dst = sumall_except_dim<1>(src)` (MapReduceKeepDim1Kernel) on a 128 x 256 float tensor; or test/test.cu. A few tens of thousands of elements.
build_notes: Header-only; compile a 40-line main with nvcc -arch=sm_89 -DMSHADOW_USE_CUDA=1 -DMSHADOW_USE_CBLAS=0 -DMSHADOW_USE_MKL=0 -DMSHADOW_USE_CUDNN=0 -I<repo> at buggy_commit. Library is archived (2020) but header-only code still compiles with some warnings.
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream; dmlc/mshadow is also vendored by Apache MXNet - the ml-frameworks slice covers MXNet itself).
dispute_points: Fix was proactive for CUDA 9 / Volta (the author explicitly flags code as unsafe) rather than a reported wrong result. MXNet vendored mshadow so downstream copies also carry the fix. Intra-warp RAW/WAR is only a 'race' for tools that model ITS.

location_buggy: src/tree/constraints.cu:L271-L298 at e9f1abc1 (node |= feature at L281; feature.Clear(tid) at L283-L285); src/common/bitfield.h:L109-L114 (operator|=) and L154 (Clear = atomicAnd loop)
race_description: In one launch (n_grids x 256 threads) thread t first does `node |= feature`, i.e. a plain read of the 64-bit word feature.Data()[t]; then every thread t<feature.Capacity() clears BIT t of `feature` via an atomicCAS loop on word t/64. Thread t' = t/64 therefore reads a word that up to 64 other threads (in several warps, and with larger feature counts other blocks) concurrently modify with atomic AND. Plain read vs atomic write on the same address with no barrier: the OR may or may not see the cleared bits, so the resulting node constraint is non-deterministic.
fix_summary: Removed the in-kernel `feature.Clear(tid)`; the feature buffer is now zeroed after the kernel by thrust::fill_n in FeatureInteractionConstraintDevice::Split (a kernel boundary orders it). operator|=/&= were also rewritten to be bit-wise via Check/Set.
evidence: Title 'Fix potential race in feature constraint' (PR #10719, Jiaming Yuan). No sanitizer output in the commit; the maintainer fixed it by moving the clear out of the kernel.
driver: C++ gtest tests/cpp/tree/test_constraints.cu: GPUFeatureInteractionConstraint.Split / .QueryNode / .Query (call constraints.Split(node,feature,left,right) on 4-5 features, tiny). Python alternative: xgboost<=2.1.x built with CUDA, xgb.train({'device':'cuda','tree_method':'hist','interaction_constraints':[[0,1],[2,3]]}, small DMatrix) launches the kernel on every split (first fixed in v3.0.0; pip wheels 2.1.x are 'buggy' - unverified that wheels contain sm_89 SASS/PTX).
build_notes: cmake -DUSE_CUDA=ON -DGOOGLE_TEST=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89 then make testxgboost, run ./testxgboost --gtest_filter='GPUFeatureInteractionConstraint*'. Buggy commit is Aug 2024 (CUDA 12.x era) - may need small patches for CUDA 13 (CCCL changes: thrust::device_vector/cub). Lighter: lift constraints.cu + bitfield.h + test into a standalone nvcc test (needs xgboost/span.h, device_helpers.cuh).
dispute_points: Author calls it 'potential' race. The bitfield test inputs are tiny so in a single warp the read of thread 0 happens before the other lanes' atomics only by luck of scheduling; a detector that models happens-before by barriers will flag it, a lockstep-assuming one will not. Fix also bundled a semantic change in operator|=/&=, so the commit is not a pure race fix.

location_buggy: src/tree/constraints.cu:L202-L215 at 221e1631 (Set at L208, L212; `result_buffer_output &= result_buffer_input` at L214); BitField in src/tree/constraints.cuh (operator&= plain RMW on bits_[tid], Set = atomicCAS loop)
race_description: One kernel first sets bits (atomicCAS loop) in result_buffer_input/result_buffer_output at positions taken from feature_list_input[tid]/node_feature_list[tid], then in the same kernel every thread does `output.bits_[tid] &= input.bits_[tid]` (plain read of input word tid and plain RMW of output word tid). Words are written by other threads' Set() calls (different tid) with no grid-wide sync, so the AND consumes partially-built bitfields (cross-warp within the block, cross-block for >256 features/threads).
fix_summary: Splits it into two kernels (SetInputBufferKernel, then QueryFeatureListKernel) so the writes are complete (kernel boundary) before the AND; also ClearBuffers() added before.
evidence: Commit/PR #4587 'Fix race condition in interaction constraint': 'Split up the kernel to sync write.'
driver: tests/cpp/tree/test_constraints.cu GPUFeatureInteractionConstraint.Query (and tests/python-gpu/test_gpu_interaction_constraints.py via gpu_hist with interaction_constraints). Tiny sizes.
build_notes: 2019 xgboost (CUDA 9/10 era, old dmlc-core, thrust) will not build with CUDA 13 as is; use standalone lift of constraints.cu/.cuh. Ranked below xgboost-1.
dispute_points: Cross-block part would be an inter-block race but the detector scope is a single launch so fine. Older code; building is hard. In test inputs the number of features is small so one block does everything.

location_buggy: src/tree/updater_gpu_hist.cu:L36-L42 at e1f57b44 (loop calling cub::BlockReduce::Reduce on temp_storage->sum_reduce each iteration, L41); shared TempStorage union declared at L134-L142
race_description: ReduceFeature walks the histogram bins of one feature in chunks of BLOCK_THREADS=256 and, in every chunk, calls cub::BlockReduce<GradientPairPrecise,256>::Reduce on the SAME shared TempStorage (temp_storage->sum_reduce) without a __syncthreads() between consecutive uses. CUB's BlockReduce stages warp aggregates in that storage and thread 0 reads them back; in the next chunk the other warps already overwrite the staging area while thread 0 (or a slow warp) is still reading the previous chunk's partial sums. Only manifests when a feature has more than 256 bins (max_bin>256, e.g. 1024) so the loop runs >1 time.
fix_summary: Accumulate each thread's bins into a per-thread local_sum inside the loop and call the block reduction exactly once after the loop, so TempStorage is used once per call (the trailing shared_sum/__syncthreads stays). 2 added, 2 removed lines.
evidence: Issue #3264 'Problems with k80 GPUs on AWS': gpu_hist accuracy worse than CPU hist and non-deterministic on Tesla K80 only; a maintainer (teju85) traced it to ReduceFeature: a cub Reduce uses shared temp storage inside a loop with no barrier so it can be overwritten between iterations - a race condition. Fixed by PR #3293 ('Fix issue #3264, accuracy issues on k80 GPUs').
driver: Python (xgboost 0.71/0.72-era, buggy): xgb.train({'tree_method':'gpu_hist','max_bin':1024,'max_depth':4}, DMatrix(X[~10^4 x 10 float32], y)); or C++ gtest tests/cpp/tree/test_gpu_hist.cu-era (not verified to exist at that commit). Each split-eval launches evaluate_split_kernel with one 256-thread block per feature column: tiny (<10^6 shared accesses).
build_notes: Cheapest: standalone harness. Copy ReduceFeature (L28-L50) + the BlockReduce typedef; replace GradientPairPrecise with a 2-double struct with operator+=; kernel <<<ncols,256>>> where each block reduces a 1024-4096-element histogram segment with cub::BlockReduce<Pair,256>, shared TempStorage; compile with nvcc -arch=sm_89 (CUDA 13 ships cub inside CCCL, cub::Sum is still available). Building the full xgboost 0.71 tree with CUDA 13 is NOT recommended (thrust/cub API drift).
dispute_points: Cause of Kepler-only manifestation is not established in the issue (the maintainers noted they could not explain why Pascal passes); on Pascal+ the actual cub implementation may happen to keep thread 0 ahead so the overwrite window is tiny. A skeptic may argue the race lives inside cub internals (documented requirement: barrier between reuses of TempStorage) but the call site clearly violates the documented contract. Fix is a restructure, not a pure barrier insertion.

kernel: AttentionKernel<KernelInfo, ArchTag>::MM1::compute_dot_product_att_value (cutlass mem-efficient attention forward, loop over blockN output tiles)
location_buggy: xformers/components/attention/csrc/cuda/mem_eff_attention/attention_forward_generic.cu:L246-L339 at cc68a6c9 (`for blockN < nBlockN`: mma(...) L280, then the pipelined Epilogue L331-L336 on shared_storage_mm.epilogue; SharedStorageMM1 is `union { Mma::SharedStorage mm; DefaultEpilogue::SharedStorage epilogue; }` L209-L216)
race_description: When the head dimension K exceeds one threadblock tile (K>128 for fp16 sm80, K>64 otherwise, i.e. nBlockN > 1) the kernel runs the attn@V mma and the output epilogue several times in a loop. The mma's operand staging (mm) and the epilogue's smem tile (epilogue) are members of one union, so the epilogue of tile blockN (smem reads by some warps) can overlap with the mma of tile blockN+1 (smem writes by others), and within one iteration the epilogue's first smem stores can overlap with slower warps still reading mm.
fix_summary: Brackets mma() with __syncthreads() before and after (comments: 'we share shmem between mma and epilogue').
evidence: Commit title 'Fix race condition when K>128|64 in attention forward (#381)'; the added barrier comment says the shared memory is shared between mma and epilogue. No sanitizer log.
driver: tests/test_mem_eff_attention.py (xformers.ops.memory_efficient_attention forward with K=256, e.g. q,k,v of shape (B=1..4, M=128..512, K=256) fp16 on sm80); run under racecheck. Tiny (a few 1e6 accesses).
build_notes: git clone --recursive https://github.com/facebookresearch/xformers && git checkout <buggy_commit> && git submodule update --init --recursive (third_party/cutlass pinned by the commit); TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.0 (sm_80 SASS runs on sm_89; or 8.9) pip install -e . --no-build-isolation; MAX_JOBS limited because every dtype/K/arch instantiation is a separate .cu file. RISK (unverified): this old source with a CUDA 13 toolchain and a modern torch (extension API, CCCL 3) may not compile; prefer a CUDA 11.8/12.x toolkit and the torch version contemporary with the commit. Note that the C++ extension was removed from the open-source xformers tree on 2026-09-22 (commit 0568e0d), so only historic commits are buildable; PyTorch ships a copy of the same cutlass kernels (aten/src/ATen/native/transformers/cuda/mem_eff_attention) with later history.

location_buggy: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/fattn-mma-f16.cuh:L1652-L1778 at 2bbca8f2 (tile_Q written at L1656-L1712, read at L1722-L1771; trailing barrier at L1775 is only `if (np > 1)`)
race_description: At the end of a tile the kernel stages the VKQ accumulators (and meta data) in the tile_Q shared buffer (the same buffer that held Q) and then reads them back with a different warp->row mapping. The trailing __syncthreads after the k00 write-out loop was only executed when np > 1, on the assumption that for np == 1 each location is touched by a single thread. That is false when nbatch_combine != DKQ/2: the next k00 iteration (or the next tile's Q load into tile_Q) overwrites rows that other warps are still reading from the previous iteration.
fix_summary: Barrier condition changed from `if (np > 1)` to `if (np > 1 || nbatch_combine != DKQ/2)`.
evidence: Issue 29314: test-backend-ops FLASH_ATTN_EXT failed flakily on gfx1201 (AMD); 'always one tile getting trashed'. Maintainer (JohannesGaessler) diagnosed missing sync when nbatch_combine != DKQ/2; reporter confirmed the patch fixes it. No compute-sanitizer output in the thread, but am17an commented on PR 30103 that racecheck on FLASH_ATTN_EXT 'fails quite reliably' (without this PR).
driver: tests/test-backend-ops.cpp: `test-backend-ops test -b CUDA0 -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT -p '<regex>'`. Need a config with np == 1 and nbatch_combine != DKQ/2. By reading the ampere config table (used for sm_80/sm_89): hsk=192,hsv=128 with ncols=64 (nthreads 128, nbatch_combine 64 vs DKQ/2 96). On Turing sm_75: hsk=hsv=256 ncols>=64. Example filter (unverified that it selects ncols=64): -p 'hsk=192,hsv=128,nh=4,nr23=\[16,1\],kv=512,nb=75'. Tiny: kv=512, nb=75 -> well below 1e8 accesses per case.

kernel: mul_mat_f<...> and mul_mat_f_ids<...> (tile_xy per-warp staging buffer; slot_map)
location_buggy: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmf.cuh:L143-L146 (slot_map[j] = -1 by lane 0, read by other lanes), L170-L224 (tile_xy[...] = ... by all lanes then load_ldmatrix reading other lanes' elements) at 9e0e2205; same pattern in mul_mat_f_ids
race_description: Each warp stages A/B tiles in its private tile_xy region: every lane stores one column element (tile_xy[i*tile_k_padded + threadIdx.x]) and then ldmatrix (load_ldmatrix) reads the tile across lanes. There was no __syncwarp between store and ldmatrix, and none between the ldmatrix reads of one itA/itB iteration and the stores of the next (WAR). Also slot_map[j] reset by lane 0 and read by other lanes without sync, and the single-warp (nwarps == 1) case skipped the __syncthreads before/after the buf_iw reduction buffer reuse.
fix_summary: Inserted ggml_cuda_syncwarp() before/after each tile_xy store/ldmatrix phase, after slot_map reset, and in the else branch of `if (nwarps > 1) __syncthreads();`.
evidence: Same PR 28475: 'fixes races reported --tool=racecheck when running test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT_ID'. Author measured <0.5% slowdown on RTX 5090 / DGX Spark.
driver: `compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck build/bin/test-backend-ops test -b CUDA0 -o MUL_MAT_ID` (mul_mat_f_ids) and `-o MUL_MAT -p 'type_a=f16'` (mul_mat_f, used for small ncols). Tiny example: -p 'type_a=f16,type_b=f32,n_mats=16,n_used=16,b=0,m=32,n=1024,k=16'.

location_buggy: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/cpy.cu:L59-L88 at 3b439504 (shared tile[][] written L74, barrier L78, read L84; next matrix iteration of the i-loop writes tile again with no trailing barrier)
race_description: The transpose kernel loops over CUDA_CPY_BLOCK_NM matrices per block using one 32x33 shared tile. There is a barrier between the tile write and tile read, but not between the tile read of matrix i and the tile write of matrix i+1, so a warp that finished reading can overwrite rows of the tile that another warp still has to read.

kernel: cumsum_kernel<T> (fallback, shared s_carry) and cumsum_cub_kernel<T,BLOCK_SIZE> (shared block_carry)
location_buggy: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/cumsum.cu:L167-L182 (cumsum_kernel: carry = *s_carry read by all threads at L167, then tid 0 does *s_carry += *s_chunk_total at L180, barrier only after at L182) and L63/L73-L76 (cub kernel: block_carry read at L63, updated by tid 0 at L74, barrier after at L76)
race_description: Thread 0 updates the carry (`*s_carry += *s_chunk_total` / `block_carry += block_total`) immediately after its own write-back phase, before a barrier. Other warps may not yet have executed `float carry = *s_carry` (resp. `thread_offset = ... + block_carry`) for the current chunk, so they can read the already-updated carry: read/write conflict on one shared word with no barrier between.
fix_summary: Moved the __syncthreads() so it sits between the write-back and the carry update (and removed the trailing one).
evidence: PR title 'cuda: fix race condition in cumsum' (am17an); no sanitizer log or description in the PR body.
driver: `compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck build/bin/test-backend-ops test -b CUDA0 -o CUMSUM` (test_cumsum exists at the buggy commit: ne={128,128,4,4}, {2048,16,5,4}, {1024,5,4,3}, ...). Use -p 'ne=\[128,128,4,4\]' (fallback kernel, ne0 < 1024) and -p 'ne=\[2048,16,5,4\]' (CUB kernel, needs ne00 >= 1024 and GGML_CUDA_USE_CUB). <1e6 accesses.
build_notes: As in other llama.cpp entries; CUMSUM op exists since Dec 2025 so buggy commit must be 382808c1 or later and before 5fa66c6e.
dispute_points: Benign-looking in practice (carry read vs update window is tiny) but it is a genuine unsynchronized shared read/write per iteration; no log from maintainers.

kernel: flash_attn_vec_ext_f32 / flash_attn_vec_ext_f16 (maskf_shared, fully-masked KV slice skip)
location_buggy: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/fattn-vec-f32.cuh:L194-L300 at b775345d (maskf_shared written L200, __syncthreads L203, read L216, `continue` at L219-L221 skips the loop's final __syncthreads at L299); same in fattn-vec-f16.cuh near L212-L215
race_description: When all mask entries of the KV slice are -inf each warp independently decides to `continue` (skip) without executing the end-of-iteration __syncthreads. A warp that skips immediately starts the next k_VKQ_0 iteration and overwrites maskf_shared (L200) while another warp is still reading maskf_shared of the previous iteration in the skip test (L216), so warps drift apart and later barriers pair up wrongly.
fix_summary: Added `__syncthreads();` before the `continue` in the skip branch of both kernels.
evidence: PR 13742: 'I accidentally introduced a race condition' (added in PR 13584); warps are not guaranteed to execute the continue at the same time and then write new maskf_shared values. User-visible symptom (issue 13733): garbage/repetitive output with -np > 1 from build b5434 onward.
driver: Needs a mask in which an entire D-wide KV slice is -inf for all ncols (multi-sequence batch). `test-backend-ops -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT` at the buggy commit builds the mask from random finite values, so it probably never reaches the skip path (unverified) -- patch test_flash_attn_ext::initialize_tensors to set -INFINITY over kv[0:256) of the mask for the F16/F32 vec kernel cases (hsk=hsv=64/128, nb=1..8, prec F32 -> vec_f32 kernel), or run llama-server -np 2 -fa with a small model. kv=512 case is tiny.
dispute_points: Skip path needs fully masked slices, which the stock unit test likely does not produce; the dynamic hazard may only be detected with a custom mask. The fix adds a barrier before `continue` that pairs with a different __syncthreads instruction at loop end (technically still 'misaligned' but accepted).
