kernel: gko::kernels::cuda::lu_factorization::factorize<full_fillin,...> (sync-free sparse LU, one warp per row, syncfree_scheduler)
location_buggy: common/cuda_hip/factorization/lu_kernels.cpp:L113-L146 at 1afe8df0 (early 'const auto val = vals[lower_nz];' at ~L119, update loop 'vals[output_pos] -= scale*upper_val' at ~L137-L142)
race_description: Within a warp, lanes update row entries (vals[row_begin+pos] -= scale*upper_val) for dependency dep_k; in the next iteration every lane reads vals[lower_nz+1] BEFORE scheduler.wait(dep), whose internal warp sync is the only warp-level ordering. If the dependency row has an entry in the column of the next lower_nz, the lane that wrote that entry and the lanes that read it early are unordered (no __syncwarp between the update loop and the next iteration's load).
fix_summary: Moves 'val = vals[lower_nz]' after scheduler.wait(dep) (the wait contains the warp sync) and adds an explicit warp.sync() before computing scale = val / diag.
evidence: Commit title 'fix the race condition in lu factorization'; code comment says the next lower_nz might be modified if the dep row has the same column. Fix is a reordering plus warp.sync(); no sanitizer output quoted.
driver: test/factorization/lu_kernels.cpp TYPED_TEST(Lu, KernelFactorizeIsEquivalentToRef) (matrices ani1, ani1_amd; ani4 unless GINKGO_FAST_TESTS): small sparse matrices, tens to hundreds of rows, well under 1e8 accesses.
build_notes: Same Ginkgo CUDA configure as ginkgo-1; build the generic 'test/factorization/lu_kernels' test for the CUDA executor (exact target name unverified) with -DGINKGO_BUILD_CUDA=ON, sm_89. The parent is from May 2025; it should build with CUDA 12/13 but this is unverified; fallback is build HEAD and re-apply the buggy ordering by hand.
already_reported_check: Not searched on GitHub issues.
dispute_points: The conflicting accesses are intra-warp and between lanes of the same warp running the same code, so a detector that treats a warp as lockstep will not flag it; under the ITS model it is a formal race. A skeptic can note that real hardware very likely reconverges there. The racing value feeds scale, so a wrong result is possible only if the compiler splits the update from the next load.

location_buggy: common/solver/idr_kernels.hpp.inc:L53-L105 at 1c2276f3 (reduction_helper[tidx] = dot at ~L74; reduction_helper_real[tidx] = norm at ~L93; reads reduction_helper[0] at ~L82 and ~L100)
race_description: A single __shared__ reduction_helper buffer (reinterpreted as real for the norm) is reused across loop iterations. After the reduce and the barrier every thread reads reduction_helper[0] and then does a long update loop; a fast thread (e.g. thread 0) can reach the next iteration's 'reduction_helper[tidx] = dot' (or the norm store) and overwrite element 0 or others while a slower warp has not yet read reduction_helper[0]. No barrier between the read of the result and the next store.
fix_summary: Moves the __syncthreads() so it comes BEFORE the store ('Ensure already finish reading this shared memory'), for both the dot and the norm buffers.
evidence: Commit 'fix idr race condition', co-authored by T. Ribizel; in-code comment about finishing reading shared memory before writing. No sanitizer output quoted.
driver: cuda/test/solver/idr_kernels.cpp TEST_F(Idr, IdrInitializeIsEquivalentToRef) and the IdrIteration*IsEquivalentToRef tests; orthonormalize_subspace_vectors is called from the initialize path with a small subspace_dim x n random matrix (single block of 512 threads at HEAD default_block_size, check at build time). Tiny.

kernel: csr::extract_transposed_diag_blocks (device function used by the block-Jacobi generate kernels jacobi_generate_kernel.cu)
location_buggy: cuda/components/diagonal_block_manipulation.cuh:L76-L108 at 986f7047 (workspace[threadIdx.x] = zero at ~L85; workspace[col] = values[j] at ~L96; read workspace[threadIdx.x] at ~L102)
race_description: Per-warp shared workspace is zero-initialised by lanes with threadIdx.y == b, then all lanes scatter values into workspace[col], then lanes with threadIdx.y == b read workspace[threadIdx.x] into block_row, in a loop over rows. Between the zero store and the scatter, and between the read-back and the next iteration's zero store, there was no warp-level synchronization, so lanes can disagree about the workspace contents (RAW/WAW/WAR within a warp).
fix_summary: Adds warp.sync() after the zeroing and after the read-back (2 lines).
evidence: Commit title is just fix racecheck problem (Oct 2019), which implies cuda-memcheck racecheck flagged the workspace accesses; the actual report text is not in the commit. Fix adds two warp.sync() calls.
driver: cuda/test/preconditioner/jacobi_kernels.cpp (generate tests e.g. GeneratesCorrectBlockJacobi with block sizes up to 32); small matrices.
build_notes: Buggy parent is Oct 2019 and will not build with CUDA 13. Build HEAD (common/cuda_hip/components/diagonal_block_manipulation.hpp already has the warp.sync() calls) and delete the two sync lines to reproduce; Jacobi generate kernel tests are quick to run.
already_reported_check: Not searched on GitHub issues.
dispute_points: Intra-warp with the formal ITS model; pre-Volta lockstep hardware made it benign, racecheck flagged it anyway. A detector with a strict lockstep warp model will not report it.

location_buggy: common/unified/solver/bicgstab_kernels.cpp:L162-L182 at c13dac2e (lambda reads stop[col].has_stopped()/is_finalized(), updates x, then calls stop[col].finalize())
race_description: The kernel launches one thread per (row, col). All threads of a column test 'stopped && !finalized' on the same 1-byte stopping_status and the first thread to finish then calls finalize(), a plain 'data_ |= finalized_mask_' on that byte. Threads of the same column (in other warps and blocks) that read the flag later see 'finalized' and skip the x update. Conflict: write of stop[col] against reads of stop[col] (and WAW between writers), no ordering within one launch. Class: check-then-act on a shared flag (plain write vs plain reads).
fix_summary: Splits the work into two kernels: the first updates x for all rows (flag only read), the second (one thread per column) calls finalize(). The race disappears because the writer is in a different launch.
evidence: The repo's own unit test BicgstabFinalizeIsEquivalentToRefWithoutRaceCondition (test/solver/bicgstab_kernels.cpp, already present at the parent) has a long comment describing exactly this failure: threads see the stop status partly finalized and skip the update. The test uses m=1e6 rows, n=2 columns 'to trigger this race more easily'.
driver: test/solver/bicgstab_kernels.cpp TEST_F(Bicgstab, BicgstabFinalizeIsEquivalentToRefWithoutRaceCondition): x,y are 1e6x2, a few global accesses per element, about 1e7 thread-accesses.
build_notes: Ginkgo CUDA configure (see ginkgo-1); the Sept 2024 parent should build with CUDA 12.x; CUDA 13 is unverified. Fallback: build HEAD and merge the two run_kernel calls back into one (move stop[col].finalize() into the 2D lambda).
already_reported_check: GMRES multi_axpy at HEAD uses the safe two-kernel structure; the bicgstab fix is the only commit touching this pattern; no GitHub issue search done.
dispute_points: The conflict is a flag, not data, so a skeptic may call it benign; but the unit test documents a wrong-result outcome (x not updated). Byte-sized flag accesses: detector must track 1-byte granularity.

location_buggy: hoomd/md/AnisoPotentialPairGPU.cuh:L160-L212: cooperative copy of s_params/s_shape_params L172-L200, __syncthreads L200, then load_shared() calls L205-L210 (ManagedArray::load_shared in hoomd/ManagedArray.h:L239-L270 copies array data cooperatively and writes the redirected 'data' pointer from every thread) and no barrier before the force loop starting L212 at buggy_commit
race_description: Each thread calls s_params[i].load_shared / s_shape_params[t].load_shared, which cooperatively copies the nested ManagedArray payloads (e.g. ALJ vertices/faces) into dynamic shared memory with a block-strided loop and then stores the new 'data' pointer into the shared struct (all threads write the same value to the same address). The force loop that follows reads those arrays through s_params[...]/s_shape_params[...] written by other threads, with no __syncthreads between load_shared and first use.
fix_summary: Adds __syncthreads() after the load_shared() loops (and a cosmetic blank line before the earlier barrier).
evidence: Commit message: anisotropic pair kernel has several ManagedArray::load_shared() calls but no thread synchronization after them, creating a race; 'Before this commit, cuda racecheck reported race conditions at this point in the code. racecheck reports no races after this commit.' (author Tim Moore).
driver: pytest hoomd/md/pytest/test_alj.py (ALJ potentials with polyhedron vertices/faces as ManagedArray) and hoomd/md/pytest/test_aniso_pair.py, on a GPU device; tests use tens to hundreds of particles.
dispute_points: Only evaluators whose param/shape types contain ManagedArray (ALJ) make load_shared do real work; for Dipole/GayBerne it is a no-op, so the race is evaluator dependent. The pointer-redirect write is a same-value WAW that some detectors may call benign.

build_notes: cmake -S hoomd-blue -B build -DENABLE_GPU=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89 -DBUILD_MD=ON -DBUILD_HPMC=OFF -DBUILD_MPCD=OFF -DBUILD_METAL=OFF -DBUILD_TESTING=ON -DENABLE_MPI=OFF (needs Python3+numpy, pybind11, Eigen3, cereal; clone with submodules); build the _md target only and put build/ on PYTHONPATH; run pytest on the file named in 'driver' with the GPU device (hoomd.device.GPU()). links: (introduced by cc882ae2ebb31aeda97852a552fe8e7bc9bdc7b5, 2021-07-19, which moved the barrier after load_shared)
location_buggy: hoomd/md/PotentialPairGPU.cuh:L160-L196: cooperative copy of s_params L179-L187, then load_shared loop L192-L194 reading s_params[cur_pair] (ManagedArray members written by other threads' int copies), barrier only at L196 at buggy_commit

Immediately afterwards every thread calls s_params[i].load_shared(), which reads the ManagedArray fields (pointer, size, managed flag) of the struct and rewrites the pointer; those fields were written by other threads of the block, and the first __syncthreads is only after load_shared.
fix_summary: Adds __syncthreads() between the parameter copy and the load_shared() loop.
evidence: Commit title 'Fix race condition in EvaluatorPairTable' (J. Anderson, 2021-09-22), one added __syncthreads.
driver: pytest hoomd/md/pytest/test_pair.py (md.pair.Table / tabulated potentials, GPU device); small systems.
dispute_points: Race window requires a param_type with ManagedArray members (Table). Commit has no sanitizer output. Needs HOOMD 3.x-era toolchain at the buggy commit (2021); building it with CUDA 13 may need patches; alternative: reintroduce by deleting the barrier at HEAD if present.

location_buggy: hoomd/md/VolumeConservationMeshForceComputeGPU.cu:L139-L176 (reduction while-loop L162-L167 without barrier; read volume_sdata[0] L170) at buggy_commit
race_description: Tree reduction over dynamic shared memory: in each step threads < offs add volume_sdata[tid+offs] into volume_sdata[tid], then offs is halved, but no __syncthreads separates one step from the next (and the final read of volume_sdata[0] at L170 by all threads is not ordered after the last step). Step k+1 therefore reads values that threads of other warps may not have written yet. The surrounding sliding-window loop only synchronizes before reloading.
fix_summary: Adds __syncthreads() at the end of each reduction step inside the while loop.
evidence: Commit title 'Fix read after write hazard in mesh.conservation.Volume' (J. Anderson, 2024-11-26), the same week as the racecheck-driven fix hoomd-1.
driver: pytest hoomd/md/pytest/test_meshpotential.py (mesh.conservation.Volume on GPU; look for the volume conservation test); small mesh (hundreds of triangles), single-block final reduction kernel.
dispute_points: Host code sets m_block_size = 256 (VolumeConservationMeshForceComputeGPU.cc:L43), so the reduction spans 8 warps and the race is cross-warp (verify the block size actually passed to gpu_volume_reduce_partial_sum_kernel; it is launched through the Autotuner/m_block_size). Exact pytest name for Volume on GPU unverified (test_meshpotential.py exists in the tree at the parent of hoomd-1).

kernel: warp_reduce<T>(NT, tid, x, volatile T* shared) as called from gpu_compute_pair_forces_shared_kernel (pair-force kernel with tpp threads per particle) and its DPD thermo twin
location_buggy: libhoomd/cuda/PotentialPairGPU.cuh:L73-L88 (warp_reduce) and L427-L449 (eight back-to-back warp_reduce calls on force.x/y/z/w and the six virial components, all reusing &sh[cta_offs]) at the buggy commit
race_description: Groups of tpp lanes reduce force and virial components through a volatile shared array: each lane stores shared[tid] = x, then in a halving loop lane tid reads shared[tid + dest_count] written by another lane in the previous round, with no barrier or __syncwarp. The same shared slots are rewritten by the next warp_reduce call (force.y, ...) while lane 0 may still be reading shared[0] of the previous call. Correct only under lockstep execution.
fix_summary: Rewrites warp_reduce: for sm_30+ uses __shfl_down so the lanes exchange values without shared memory; for sm_20 inserts explicit __syncthreads after the store and after each halving step.
evidence: Commit message (J. Glaser, 2015-03-25): 'Because of compiler optimizations, warp-synchronous reduction using shared memory can fail (race condition detectable using cuda-memcheck)'. Companion fixes the same day: 70dadf663 (missing __syncthreads in rigid body force reduction, rejected here as the rigid GPU code was removed) and 2525e285b.
driver: HOOMD 1.x unit tests for GPU pair potentials (libhoomd/potentials/test, e.g. test_pair_lj and the generic PotentialPairGPU tests) with a few hundred particles and threads_per_particle > 1 (tpp in {2,4,8,16,32}). A standalone harness is easier: copy warp_reduce (15 lines) and launch a kernel that calls it for four values with tpp=8, block 128.
build_notes: 2015 HOOMD 1.0 needs CUDA <= 7 era APIs (texture references, legacy __shfl_down without mask); will not build on CUDA 13. Extract warp_reduce into a standalone .cu (T=float/double) and launch <<<1,128,128*sizeof(T)>>>; this reproduces the exact buggy reduction. Current HOOMD no longer has this function.
already_reported_check: Not searched on GitHub issues.
dispute_points: Pre-Volta era fix that replaced the code rather than adding a sync; the buggy function no longer exists in current HOOMD, so only a standalone extraction can be run. 'volatile' was used to make lockstep reduction work in practice; the race only exists under independent thread scheduling or compiler register caching.

kernel: gpu_compute_external_forces_kernel<evaluator> (external field potentials: electric field, periodic, wall)
location_buggy: libhoomd/cuda/PotentialExternalGPU.cuh:L129-L148 at the buggy commit (cooperative copy of field data into s_field at L132-L146, then 'const field_type& field = *s_field;' and use by every thread, no barrier)
race_description: The block cooperatively copies the d_field structure into dynamic shared memory with a strided loop (each thread copies some ints) and then every thread constructs the evaluator with a reference to s_field. Without a __syncthreads between the copy and the use, a thread can read ints of the field that another warp has not yet written.
fix_summary: Adds __syncthreads() after the cooperative load of the field (before the 'idx >= N' early return).
evidence: Commit 'How about a __syncthreads()?' (J. Glaser, 2016-03-04), 'fixes #131' in the HOOMD tracker; no sanitizer output in the message.
driver: HOOMD 1.x/2.0-dev unit tests for external potentials on GPU (libhoomd/potentials/test/test_potential_external*_gpu*), a few hundred particles with a block of 128-256 threads and a field struct bigger than 32 ints so that more than one warp participates in the copy (field_size > block_size is not needed, but writers must be in other warps than readers: size in ints > 32).
build_notes: 2016 tree; will not build with CUDA 13. The kernel is 50 lines plus the evaluator template; extract it with a trivial evaluator whose field_type is a struct of 64 floats and launch with N=1024, block 256, dynamic shared = sizeof(field_type).
already_reported_check: Tracker issue #131 is cited by the commit (not fetched).
dispute_points: For tiny field structures (e.g. a few ints) all copy iterations are done by lanes of warp 0, which are lock-stepped with each other but not with the other warps, so the race still exists across warps; but effect is not observable in practice. Old code base.

kernel: lincs_kernel<> (GPU LINCS constraint solver, one thread per constraint, 256 threads/block)
location_buggy: src/gromacs/mdlib/lincs_gpu_internal.cu: sm_r declared L118, written L168, read L184; sm_rhs aliases sm_r L203-L206 (write L206 with no preceding barrier); sm_threadVirial aliases sm_r/sm_rhs L335-L344 (writes with no preceding barrier; last sm_rhs reads at L290/L220) at buggy_commit. Release-2021 copy: src/gromacs/mdlib/lincs_gpu.cu.
race_description: The same dynamic shared-memory buffer is reinterpreted three ways: as float3 sm_r[] (constraint direction vectors), then float sm_rhs[] (matrix-expansion RHS) and finally float sm_threadVirial[] (virial reduction). Each reinterpretation starts with plain stores by every thread, but there is no __syncthreads() between the last reads of the previous view (sm_r[c1] at L184 by other threads; sm_rhs[...] reads in the expansion loop) and the first stores of the next view, so one warp can overwrite data another warp is still reading.
fix_summary: Adds __syncthreads() before the sm_rhs stores ('Make sure that we don't overwrite the sm_r[..] array') and before the sm_threadVirial stores ('waiting for all threads in block').
evidence: Commit message: same shared buffer stores different intermediate values, extra blocking synchronizations needed to avoid overwriting prematurely; bug 'was not exposed by regression tests nor unit tests because it affected values rarely and deviations were within tolerances'. Release-2021 message: shared memory 'occasionally overwritten with the new data', may slightly shift atoms, Fixes #4199.
driver: mdlib-test constraint tests with GPU LINCS runner (src/gromacs/mdlib/tests/constrtestrunners_gpu.cpp + constrtest.cpp): systems of 2..~30 atoms, 1 block of 256 threads (extra threads are dummies), < 1e5 accesses per launch.
dispute_points: Maintainers say the effect was rare and within test tolerances; the stale read is only visible to a sanitizer/detector, not to the tests. Dummy threads still execute the stores, so cross-warp conflicts exist even for tiny systems.

links: https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/issues/4393 (issue number from commit message 'Closes #4393'; page not fetched)
kernel: lincs_kernel<> and settle_kernel<> virial reduction epilogue (shared-memory tree reduction of sm_threadVirial)
location_buggy: src/gromacs/mdlib/lincs_gpu.cu:L360-L396 (virial stores L360-L365, __syncthreads L367, reduction loop L374-L390 with conditional barrier at L385-L389); src/gromacs/mdlib/settle_gpu.cu:L301-L359 (stores L301-L311, loop with conditional barrier L342-L354, atomicAdd L359) at buggy_commit
race_description: In the block-wide virial reduction each step has threads < dividedAt add sm_threadVirial[tid+dividedAt] into their slot. A block-wide __syncthreads is issued only while dividedAt > warpSize/2; the final five steps (all within warp 0) have no synchronisation at all, relying on lockstep. On Volta+ lane i can read the slot of lane i+dividedAt before that lane has written its result of the previous step.
fix_summary: Adds an else branch with __syncwarp() after each reduction step (and release-notes entry).
evidence: Commit message: a __syncwarp call was missing from the last iterations of a shared-memory virial reduction; could have led to data races on Volta and newer when GPU update was used (wrong virial/pressure). Closes #4393; backported to 2021.6 and 2022.0.
driver: mdlib-test: SettleTest / ConstraintsTest GPU runners (settletestrunners_gpu.cpp, constrtestrunners_gpu.cpp); small systems, one 256-thread block.
dispute_points: Only affects the virial output; the existing tests did not compare virial strictly. Race is purely intra-warp.

kernel: nbnxn_kernel_prune_cuda (dynamic neighbour-list pruning kernel; header was later renamed to src/gromacs/nbnxm/cuda/nbnxm_cuda_kernel_pruneonly.cuh)
location_buggy: src/gromacs/mdlib/nbnxn_cuda/nbnxn_cuda_kernel_pruneonly.cuh, cjs shared-memory pre-load at ~L189 ('cjs[tidxi + tidxj*c_nbnxnGpuJgroupSize/c_splitClSize] = pl_cj4[j4].cj[tidxi];') and its reads at ~L199 ('int cj = cjs[jm + (tidxj & 4)*...]') at the buggy commit; HEAD equivalent nbnxm_cuda_kernel_pruneonly.cuh:L251-L259 (write + __syncwarp) and L319-L322 (trailing __syncwarp)
race_description: Lanes with tidxj == 0 or 4 write the j-cluster indices into the per-warp shared array cjs, then all lanes of the warp read cjs[jm + ...] in the jm loop with no __syncwarp in between (RAW across lanes), and in the next j4 iteration the writers overwrite cjs while slower lanes may still read the previous values (WAR). Correct only with lockstep warps; on Volta+ independent thread scheduling can reorder them.
fix_summary: Adds gmx_syncwarp(c_fullWarpMask) after the cjs store and at the end of the j4 loop body ('avoid shared memory WAR hazards between loop iterations'), and converts __any to gmx_any_sync with the full mask.
evidence: Commit 'CUDA 9/Volta support for the pruning kernel' (S. Pall, 2017-08-29): 'Added syncwarp to prevent WAR hazard and changes any to any_sync'. Part of the Volta/independent-thread-scheduling porting series (see also 97f9f399c for the main nonbonded kernel).
driver: mdrun with GPU nonbonded and dynamic pruning, e.g. 'gmx mdrun -nb gpu -pme cpu -nstlist 40 -nsteps 50' on a tiny water box (spc216, ~650 atoms, grompp from a minimal .mdp with verlet-buffer-tolerance default); pruning kernel runs every nstlist/2 steps on the rolling list. The 2017 tree can not be built with CUDA 13, and at HEAD cjs preloading is compiled out on sm_70+ (constexpr c_preloadCj = GMX_PTX_ARCH < 700), so see build notes. Also covered by src/gromacs/nbnxm/tests only through the CPU kernels (unverified for GPU).
build_notes: Build HEAD: cmake -DGMX_GPU=CUDA -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89 -DGMX_BUILD_OWN_FFTW=ON -DGMX_MPI=OFF -DGMX_THREAD_MPI=ON. To reproduce: in nbnxm_cuda_kernel_pruneonly.cuh set 'constexpr bool c_preloadCj = true;' (otherwise the shared array is not used on sm_89) and delete the two __syncwarp(c_fullWarpMask) calls at L258 and L322 (the HEAD lines mirroring the fix). The same pattern with another pair of syncs exists in nbnxm_cuda_kernel.cuh (L440, L690).
already_reported_check: Not searched on GitLab issues.
dispute_points: 2017 Volta-porting change: no failing run is documented; the racing code path exists at HEAD only when c_preloadCj is true (sm < 7.0), so on the target hardware (sm_89) the unfixed code has to be recreated by editing a constexpr. Under lockstep (pre-Volta) execution the code was correct.

location_buggy: include/gunrock/framework/operators/advance/block_mapped.hxx at buggy_commit: shared write degrees[local_idx] L90; __syncthreads L102 sits inside 'if constexpr (output_type != none)' L93-L103; reads of degrees[] in search::binary::rightmost(degrees, i, length) L121 and sedges/vertices L129-L134
race_description: Each thread publishes its exclusive-sum degree with 'degrees[local_idx] = th_deg[0]' (L90). The only __syncthreads that orders this write before the binary search over degrees[] by other threads was placed inside 'if constexpr (output_type != none)'. When the advance has no output frontier (SpMV, PageRank, triangle counting, BC, SpGEMM all use io_type none) the barrier is compiled out, so threads read degrees[] entries that other threads (possibly in other warps) have not yet written.
fix_summary: Move __syncthreads() out of the 'if constexpr' so it is executed for every output_type.
evidence: Commit titled 'Move syncthreads to correct location' by Muhammad Awad, 2022-06-23, immediately before the triangle-counting work (PR #141/#144 merged 2022-06-24/25). No issue or PR discussion found with the search tool; the diff is a 2-line move.
driver: At the buggy commit: examples/algorithms/spmv, examples/algorithms/pr, examples/algorithms/tc and unittests/algorithms/tc.cuh all launch block_mapped advance with output none. unittests/algorithms/tc.cuh uses a 4-vertex graph (intra-warp only); use examples/algorithms/spmv or pr with a mtx of >=256 vertices (datasets/ in repo) so that degrees[] spans several warps (THREADS_PER_BLOCK=128/256).
build_notes: Header-only C++17/CUDA with CMake; externals (thrust/cub/moderngpu/cxxopts, fetched by CMake FetchContent) and CUDA-13-era cub may need patches (this commit is mid-2022, CUDA 11.x). Alternative: copy block_mapped.hxx kernel + a tiny CSR graph view into a standalone .cu (needs graph_t get_starting_edge/get_number_of_neighbors/get_destination_vertex).
dispute_points: The fix is only meaningful for output==none instantiations; with output frontier the barrier already existed. For ExclusiveSum via cub::BlockScan a barrier follows at L87, but that orders the scan temp storage, not the later degrees[] writes.

location_buggy: gunrock/oprtr/edge_map_forward/cta.cuh at buggy_commit: cta_comm written L383 and read L389/L436; 'while(true)' loop L379-L484 exits via break at L393; next element Iterate<LOAD,VEC+1>::CtaExpand called at L487 with no barrier
race_description: CtaExpand elects a block-wide owner through the shared word cta_comm (every thread with a long neighbor list writes threadIdx.x into it at L383, all read it at L389 after a barrier). When no thread claims the CTA, all break at L393 and immediately call the next vector element's CtaExpand, whose first statement is again 'cta_comm = threadIdx.x' (L383). A fast thread can overwrite cta_comm before a slower thread (other warp) has executed its read at L389 of the previous element, so the slow thread sees a bogus owner.
fix_summary: Add __syncthreads() after the while(true) loop ('} // end of while (true)'), plus removal of debug printf and re-enabling of BFS traversal modes in bfs_enactor.cuh (mixed commit).
evidence: Maintainer's own commit message: the break at line 393 introduces a shared-memory data race on cta_comm, solved by adding __syncthreads() at line 486. Commit is on the gunrock 1.x lines (dev, master, tags v0.4/v0.5/release); the repository default branch main is the later rewrite and does not contain it.
driver: gunrock 1.x tests/bfs/test_bfs.cu with --traversal-mode=1 (ForwardAdvanceKernelPolicy), e.g. a ~10^5-edge graph from dataset/; also SSSP via tests/sssp (same advance).
build_notes: Legacy gunrock 1.x needs moderngpu (submodule), Boost, and CUDA <= 10/11 era APIs; probably will not compile on CUDA 13 without patches. Practical route: extract CtaExpand logic into a standalone kernel that reproduces the cta_comm election loop over two vector elements.
dispute_points: Not in the repo default branch (main); lives on legacy branches. The fix commit also contains unrelated debug cleanup.

kernel: WarpScan<LOG>::Iterate/Invoke and CooperativeGridScan::ScanTileWithEnqueue (used by CULL_filter/cta.cuh L587)
location_buggy: gunrock/util/scan/warp_scan.cuh L51-L57 and L151-L160; gunrock/util/scan/cooperative_scan.cuh L287-L300 at buggy_commit
race_description: WarpScan publishes partials through shared warpscan[1][tid] and reads a neighbour's slot guarded only by __threadfence_block() (a memory-ordering fence, not a barrier). In ScanTileWithEnqueue thread 0 stores reservation_offset to warpscan[1][0] and all raking threads read it back immediately with nothing but program order for synchronization; later warpscan writes can also overwrite slots still being read (WAR).
fix_summary: Replace __threadfence_block() by __syncthreads() in WarpScan and add two __syncthreads() around the atomic reservation in ScanTileWithEnqueue (cooperative_scan.cuh).
evidence: Commit/PR title: Fix RAW and WAR hazards found using cuda-memcheck (racecheck). Author notes __syncthreads may be more than needed. Maintainer neoblizz comments that some reported races leave the code functionally correct. PR was opened 2021-01-28, converted to draft after memory errors, merged by neoblizz 2022-09-09 into dev (merge commit 935f7d43).
driver: gunrock 1.x tests/sssp or tests/bfs with the CULL filter (filter kernel CULL_filter/cta.cuh calls CooperativeTileScan::ScanTileWithEnqueue); PR author reproduced on ak2010 dataset.
build_notes: Legacy 1.x tree (dev/master), moderngpu submodule, old CUDA; extract WarpScan+ScanTileWithEnqueue into a standalone kernel with RAKING_THREADS=32.
dispute_points: The author says the fix caused memory errors on other inputs and was left in draft for 1.5 years; maintainers say racecheck reports may be functionally benign. Intra-warp (32 raking threads) so it is a warp-synchronous/ITS pattern. On main (gunrock 2.x) this code no longer exists.

links: SuperCollider (PLDI 2026) appendix Table 6 lists Gunrock 'mst' among apps with detected races (Gunrock: color, dawn, kcore, mst, sssp)
kernel: gunrock::operators::parallel_for kernels instantiated with the add_to_mst and jump_pointers_parallel lambdas (Boruvka MST, one iteration = get_min_weights, get_min_neighbors, add_to_mst, jump_pointers_parallel)
location_buggy: include/gunrock/algorithms/mst.hxx:L156-L188 (add_to_mst: reads roots[dest] L167-L168, atomicExch(&roots[v], roots[dest]) L184) and L193-L201 (jump_pointers_parallel: plain reads roots[u], plain write roots[v] L199) at buggy_commit
race_description: In the Boruvka MST each vertex v is processed by one thread of a parallel_for kernel. add_to_mst reads roots[dest] (to detect 2-cycles) while other threads concurrently execute atomicExch(&roots[v], roots[dest]) on the same roots[] array, and jump_pointers_parallel does pointer jumping in place: it reads roots[u] chains and writes roots[v] = u while other threads read those entries. All of these are unsynchronised plain accesses to roots[] inside one kernel launch, so the result depends on thread interleaving (extra hops at best, a missed/duplicated 'cycle check' at worst).
fix_summary: Introduces a second array new_roots: add_to_mst writes atomicExch(&new_roots[v], new_roots[dest]) and jump_pointers_parallel writes new_roots[v] while reading from roots (double-buffering so reads and writes hit different copies); also fixes the cycle check to compare both endpoints. Commit title says 'partially resolve races': the code comments still mention a remaining race on roots[dest].
evidence: Commit message 'partially resolve races' (Annie, 2022-02-28). kernel: magma_zlarfg2_gpu_kernel (Householder reflector generation; multi-block launch <<<ceil(n/512), 512>>>; the sibling magma_zlarfg_gpu_kernel has the identical pattern at this commit)
location_buggy: magmablas/zlarfg-v2.cu at the buggy commit: magma_zlarfg2_gpu_kernel L87-L150; reads 'alpha = *dx0' at L118 (real) / L132 (complex); last-block stores '*dx0 = beta' at L126-L127 / L141-L142 (the same pattern is in magma_zlarfg_gpu_kernel L49/L58 and L62/L72, not touched by this commit)
race_description: Thread 0 of every block reads alpha = *dx0 to compute tau and scale, while thread 0 of the LAST block overwrites *dx0 with beta in the same launch. Whether other blocks read the old alpha or the new beta depends on block scheduling, so tau/scale can be wrong; there is no grid-wide ordering between the last block's store and the other blocks' loads. Needs n > 512 so the launch has at least two blocks.
fix_summary: Deletes the 'if (blockIdx.x == gridDim.x-1) *dx0 = beta' stores from magma_zlarfg2_gpu_kernel (beta is still delivered through dAkk) and adds a comment in zlaqps2_gpu.cu that the update of A(rk,k) must be done outside zlarfg2 to avoid the race; zlaqps2_gpu is reworked in the same commit (custom zgemv kernel replaced by magmablas_zgemv, extra copy of vn1 to vn2).
evidence: Commit 'remove the race condition' (I. Yamazaki, 2012-12-11) with an added code comment saying the update has to happen outside zlarfg2 to avoid the race condition. The GitHub mirror contains the old SVN history. No sanitizer output (2012).
driver: No small test exists in today's tree for the old kernel. Options: (a) extract magma_zlarfg2_gpu_kernel (about 60 lines, needs cuDoubleComplex helper macros MAGMA_Z_MAKE/MUL/DIV and BLOCK_SIZE 512) into a standalone .cu and launch it with n=2048 (4 blocks) and a precomputed dxnorm; ~5k thread accesses; (b) build the 2012 MAGMA tree and run testing_zgeqp3_gpu with M>=1024 rows.

already_reported_check: Not applicable (2012 SVN-era fix).
dispute_points: Very old code (CUDA 4/5 era) that no longer exists on the default branch, so the check is only against the buggy commit's kernel; the commit bundles other changes in zlaqps2_gpu.cu. The cross-block read/write is clear from the diff but the commit message does not spell out the two accesses.

location_buggy: slate_device_genorm.cu:L309-L324 at buggy_commit: `shmem_tile[j*33+idx] = abs(...)` L315 vs `sum += shmem_tile[idx*33+i]` L319, no barrier in the ii loop
race_description: The kernel is launched with blockDim.x = 32 (one warp per tile). In each ii iteration every lane writes column-strided entries shmem_tile[j*33+idx] for j=0..31, then each lane reads its own row shmem_tile[idx*33+i], i.e. entries written by other lanes; the same buffer is rewritten in the next ii iteration (WAR). Only implicit lock-step execution ordered this on pre-Volta GPUs; with independent thread scheduling neither the RAW nor the WAR is ordered.
fix_summary: Adds __syncthreads() after the shared-tile fill ('shmem_tile loaded') and after the accumulation ('done with shmem_tile'); also replaces the literal 32/33 by one_ib/one_ib1.
evidence: Commit message 'Add __syncthreads. Use one_ib constant.' (Mark Gates, 2018-06-27); the diff comments label the two new barriers. No sanitizer output or issue.
driver: Not used outside SLATE's norm routines; write a 40-line harness: copy genormOneKernel, replace blas::real_type<scalar_t> by scalar_t (float/double), launch <<<batch=4, 32, sizeof(float)*32*33>>> on tiles of m=n=64..128 with random data and compare to a CPU column-sum. A few 1e5 accesses.
build_notes: The .cu file includes SLATE/blaspp headers only for blas::real_type and cuComplex; extracting the kernel removes that dependency. Not compiled by me: unverified.
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream 2018).
dispute_points: 136 stars (below 300). The commit message does not call it a race; classification is mine from the diff (shared tile filled by one lane and consumed by others, no barrier). Intra-warp only, so a detector without ITS modelling will consider it ordered by lock-step; SLATE later moved this kernel to src/cuda/device_genorm.cu and rewrote it.

location_buggy: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmq_id.cu:L94 (store[it_compact + it_compact_add_lower] = ...) in the token loop vs L105 (store_it = store[itc]) in the read-back loop, one warp per block (blockDim = warp_size), no __syncwarp between, at buggy_commit 066e8664

kernel: batchApplyRepetitionPenalty<T, penalty_type> (TurboMind repetition penalty; launched by invokeBatchApplyRepetitionPenalty, one block of min(step,1024) threads per batch row)
location_buggy: src/turbomind/kernels/sampling_penalty_kernels.cu:L388-L422 at c9f32341 (Phase 1 loop reads logits[penalty_index] L396-L399 and stores to penalty_logits/penalty_indices; Phase 2 loop writes logits[penalty_indices[index]] L421; no barrier between the two loops)
race_description: Phase 1 of the kernel lets thread t read logits[output_ids[...]] for the tokens it owns; Phase 2 lets each thread overwrite logits[penalty_indices[index]] with the penalised value. There is no __syncthreads between the phases, so a warp that finishes Phase 1 early can write a penalised logit to a vocab id that a slower warp has not yet read in Phase 1 (WAR/RAW on the same global address, different threads), and the slower warp then penalises an already penalised value. Needs step > 32 so that more than one warp is active.
fix_summary: Inserts an unconditional __syncthreads() between Phase 1 and Phase 2.
evidence: Commit 'fix batchApplyRepetitionPenalty (#1358)' with the second squash bullet '__syncthreads unconditionally'; two-line diff. The conflict description is mine, read from the two phases.
driver: tests/csrc/unittests/test_penalty_kernels.cu (gtest target test_penalty_kernels in tests/csrc/unittests/CMakeLists.txt); the RepetitionPenaltyTest cases (names and sizes unverified) call invokeBatchApplyRepetitionPenalty. Choose step >= 64 and vocab ~32000 with repeated tokens in output_ids; a few 1e5 accesses.
build_notes: Full TurboMind CMake build with BUILD_TEST=ON (needs NCCL, cutlass submodule, gtest; see lmdeploy docs) at c9f32341; a lighter route is to compile sampling_penalty_kernels.cu alone with nvcc -arch=sm_89 -I src -I src/turbomind plus the headers it includes (cuda_utils, memory_utils) and a tiny main() that fills logits/output_ids and calls the invoke function (unverified). CUDA 13 compatibility of this 2024 tree is unverified.
dispute_points: The race changes the output only when the same vocab id appears in output_ids handled by different warps (repeated tokens across threads), which is common in real generation; with a single warp (step <= 32) there is no cross-warp race. No author explanation beyond the title, and no sanitizer log.

kernel: ProjectCUDA, pass-2 lambda run through core::ParallelFor (the colour pass)
location_buggy: cpp/open3d/t/geometry/kernel/PointCloudCUDA.cu:L70-L97 at 33743191 (colour stores at L93-L95; depth re-read at L87-L90)
race_description: Pass 2 launches one thread per 3D point. Every point that projects onto the same pixel and whose depth is within `dmap + 1e-4*depth_scale` of the pixel's final depth executes plain stores color_ptr[0..2] = point_colors[3*i+0..2] to that pixel's 3 floats. When several points land within the tolerance (or are equal-depth duplicates) several threads write different colours to the same pixel with no atomics or ordering, so the pixel gets a nondeterministic and possibly channel-mixed colour.
fix_summary: Pass 1 becomes a single 64-bit atomicMin on a packed (depth bits << 32 | point index) word per pixel, so each pixel has exactly one winner; pass 2 only lets the winning point write depth and colour. Depth-only path unchanged (atomicExch+atomicMinf).
evidence: Commit/PR #7424 'Fix color artifacts in PointCloud projection due to CUDA race condition': multiple points pass the fuzzy depth tolerance and 'race on the color write', giving nondeterministic colour artifacts.
driver: Open3D t::geometry::PointCloud::ProjectToRGBDImage(width,height,intrinsics,extrinsics,depth_scale,depth_max) / Python o3d.t.geometry.PointCloud.project_to_rgbd_image on a CUDA device with colored points; to trigger the race use many points mapping to few pixels (e.g. 10^5 points, 8x8 image) or two coincident points of different colour. The upstream tests added by the fix (ProjectToRGBDImage in cpp/tests/t/geometry/PointCloud.cpp, python/test/t/geometry/test_pointcloud.py::test_project_to_rgbd_image) are only smoke tests with 3 points. Pixel-level stress test needs to be written (10 lines).
build_notes: Full Open3D CUDA build is heavy (cmake -DBUILD_CUDA_MODULE=ON -DBUILD_PYTHON_MODULE=ON ... with many third-party deps). Cheaper: lift the two ParallelFor lambdas into a standalone .cu (they only need TransformIndexer/NDArrayIndexer -> replace with a hand-written pinhole projection); the kernel logic is ~40 lines. Or pip install open3d (CPU+CUDA wheels exist only for some versions; the buggy window is only up to 2026-08-01 so a source build of main^ is required).
dispute_points: Skeptic: the writers store colours of points that are (almost) the same depth, so the visible difference is small ('color artifacts'). But as a memory-model matter it is a WAW between different threads on the same 12 bytes without ordering. Pass 1 uses an atomicExch/atomicMinf scheme that is racy at the semantic level (lost-min) but atomic-only, so a detector will not flag it.

location_buggy: src/cudamatrix/cu-kernels.cu at buggy_commit: _softmax_reduce L2486-L2560 (warp tails at L2512 and L2542), _normalize_per_row L2574-L2610 (tail L2600), _log_softmax_reduce L2722 (tails L2749, L2778), _diff_softmax L3023 (tail L3051), _diff_log_softmax L3075 (tail L3105)
race_description: Each kernel reduces CU1DBLOCK partial values in a shared array with __syncthreads down to 2*warpSize entries and then finishes with 'if (tid < warpSize) for (shift=warpSize; shift>0; shift>>=1) smem[tid] = op(smem[tid], smem[tid+shift])' with neither volatile nor __syncwarp. Lane t reads smem[t+shift] that lane t+shift wrote in the previous shift step; the code relies on implicit lock-step execution that Volta+ independent thread scheduling does not provide.

evidence: PR #3080 by desh2608, merged 2019-03-10 by danpovey. NVIDIA's luitjens in the PR thread: the previous code is unsafe on Volta and Turing; anything assuming warp-synchronous behaviour. PR body lists the remaining unmodified warp-synchronous kernels (_vec_transform_reduce, _transform_reduce_mat_cols, _group_transform_reduce, _find_row_max_id, _trace_mat_mat*, _diff_normalize_per_row, _add_diag_mat_mat_*), later covered by lit-kaldi-2.

location_buggy: src/cudamatrix/cu-kernels.cu at buggy_commit: warp tails at L965, L1175, L1218, L1269, L1352, L1805 (_vec_transform_reduce), L2018, L2057, plus _group_transform_reduce, _diff_normalize_per_row, _find_row_max_id

kernel: Kokkos::Impl::CudaReductionsFunctor<...,false,false>::scalar_intra_warp_reduction (called from scalar_intra_block_reduction / scalar_inter_block_reduction; used by every shuffle-style scalar parallel_reduce with RangePolicy/MDRange/Team on Cuda)
location_buggy: core/src/Cuda/Kokkos_Cuda_ReduceScan.hpp:L529-L549 (loop at L542-L547; the shared-slot write it races with is L557 in scalar_intra_block_reduction) at buggy_commit
race_description: scalar_intra_block_reduction stores each thread's contribution into a shared slot (L557) and immediately calls scalar_intra_warp_reduction, whose first loop iteration reads value[lane+delta] written by a different lane of the same warp. There is no __syncwarp between the store and the first read (the __syncwarp(mask) only appears at the end of each loop iteration), so on Volta+ (independent thread scheduling) the read can precede the other lane's write.
fix_summary: Adds __syncwarp(mask) at function entry, before the first tree-reduction step.
evidence: Commit message embeds compute-sanitizer --tool=racecheck output on a tiny double-sum reduction (n=1): 3 hazards before the fix, 2 after (the remaining ones are the join-line race fixed by kokkos-2 and the final-result read fixed by kokkos-3). Merged via PR #4855 (merge commit 1d19a32b1, 2022-03-10).
driver: Any scalar Kokkos::parallel_reduce on Cuda, e.g. 'double s=0; Kokkos::parallel_reduce(Kokkos::RangePolicy<Kokkos::Cuda>(0,n), KOKKOS_LAMBDA(int i,double& u){u+=i;}, s);' with n=1..1e6; the commit's own repro was run with n=1. Also core/unit_test/TestReduce.hpp (cuda) . ~1e3-1e6 thread accesses.
dispute_points: Pure warp-level ITS race; on pre-Volta or in practice it never produced a wrong result (sum is correct on real hardware). A detector that models __syncwarp precisely will flag it; one that treats a warp as lockstep will not. Racecheck's 'after' output in the same commit shows other residual hazards (kokkos-2, kokkos-3), so expect additional reports at the buggy commit than this one alone.

location_buggy: core/src/Cuda/Kokkos_Cuda_ReduceScan.hpp:L301-L326 (racy join at L317-L322) at buggy_commit
race_description: In each tree step every lane with lane_id+delta<32 executes functor.join(value, value+delta), i.e. lane i writes its own slot value[i] while lane i-delta reads value[i] as its 'other' operand in the same step. Only lanes with lane_id % (2*delta)==0 should combine; the extra lanes write slots that are read concurrently by the other lanes, with the next __syncwarp only after the loop body. Read and write of value[i] are therefore unordered within one step.
fix_summary: Restricts the join to lanes with lane_id % (2*delta) == 0, so no lane writes a slot that another lane reads in the same step.
evidence: Commit message is just 'only compute with relavent entries' (PR #6236 'potential_racecondition_in_cuda_reduce'). Evidence is indirect but strong: the racecheck output in kokkos-1's commit message still lists a read/write hazard pair on the single join line inside scalar_intra_warp_reduction ('[144 hazards]') after kokkos-1 was applied; this one-line change removes exactly that conflict.
driver: Same as kokkos-1: any scalar Cuda parallel_reduce (double sum, n=1..1e6). Check out the buggy commit.
dispute_points: The commit message does not use the word 'race'; the mapping from the 144-hazard racecheck line to this fix is my inference from the PR branch name (potential_racecondition_in_cuda_reduce) and the code. Results were always numerically correct because lanes that must not combine write values that are never consumed.

location_buggy: core/src/Cuda/Kokkos_Cuda_Parallel_Range.hpp:L227-L251 (write by threadIdx.y==0 at L239-L242, read at L248-L250) at buggy_commit
race_description: In the final block of a RangePolicy reduction, thread threadIdx.y==0 calls reducer.final() which writes the result into shared[] (L239-242); then threads threadIdx.y=i<word_count read shared[i] and copy to global (L248-250). When word_count<=WarpSize only a lane-level barrier is required but none is issued (the existing __syncthreads is guarded by WarpSize<word_count), so the other lanes may read before lane 0 has written.
fix_summary: Adds an else-branch '__syncwarp(0xffffffff)' when word_count>1 and WarpSize>=word_count.
evidence: Commit message: compute-sanitizer racecheck found a potential race for Cuda parallel reductions with range policy where one thread in a warp updated data that was read without warp synchronization. PR #6630, merged 2024-01-24.
driver: Any Cuda RangePolicy parallel_reduce whose value type is 8 bytes or larger (word_count>1, e.g. double sum, or a struct/array reducer): Kokkos::parallel_reduce(RangePolicy<Cuda>(0,n), lambda, double&); n=1..1e6.
dispute_points: Whether final() performs a real write depends on the reducer (a plain Sum's final is empty), so the conflicting write may only exist for reducers with a non-trivial final(); the racecheck report in the PR was produced with some reducer the author does not name in the commit message. Use a reducer with non-trivial final (e.g. Kokkos::MinLoc/Max-type, or custom functor with final()) to be sure.

kernel: ILUKLvlSchedTP1NumericFunctor::operator() (team-policy ILU(k) numeric phase, SEQLVLSCHD_TP1; Kokkos TeamPolicy -> CUDA thread block per row)
location_buggy: sparse/impl/KokkosSparse_spiluk_numeric_impl.hpp:L275-L330 at a936394f ('scalar_t fact = L_values(k) / U_values(...)' read by all threads, then Kokkos::single(PerTeam, L_values(k) = fact), then team_barrier)
race_description: In the elimination loop every thread of the team computes fact from L_values(k), and then the team leader overwrites L_values(k) with fact in Kokkos::single(PerTeam) with no barrier between the reads and that write. A slower thread can read the already overwritten L_values(k) (now the factor, not the original value) and use a wrong fact. A second missing team_barrier sits between the unpack of L/iw and the 'KEEP_DIAG' single write.
fix_summary: The leader computes tmp_fact and writes L_values(k) inside Kokkos::single(PerTeam, lambda, fact), which broadcasts fact to all threads; adds a team_barrier after the first loop; replaces atomic_add on L/U values by plain += (distinct positions); also removes Volta-specific team-size code and the symbolic-phase hack.
evidence: Commit title: Fix race condition when read and write L_values at the same k (V. Dang, Feb 2023). Diff touches three files (numeric/symbolic impl and handle); net 13 insertions, 91 deletions.
driver: sparse/unit_test/Test_Sparse_spiluk.hpp run_test_spiluk (9x9 matrix, 21 nnz; uses SEQLVLSCHD_TP1 and SEQLVLSCHD_RP) instantiated for the CUDA execution space; tiny input. With team size AUTO on CUDA the team is one block of several warps.
build_notes: Build Kokkos with -DKokkos_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DKokkos_ARCH_ADA89=ON and Kokkos-Kernels at the parent with -DKokkosKernels_ENABLE_TESTS=ON, ETI limited to one scalar/ordinal/offset set (-DKokkosKernels_INST_DOUBLE=ON etc., rest OFF); build only the sparse spiluk test. Feb 2023 Kokkos-Kernels needs a matching 3.7/4.0 Kokkos; CUDA 13 compatibility with that old Kokkos is unverified (Kokkos 4.x may be required, so port needed).
already_reported_check: Not searched on GitHub issues. Related earlier PR #1390 (merge ca33f614, 2022-04-25) 'Improve spiluk numeric phase to avoid race conditions and processing in chunks' touches the same functor but was not analysed in depth.
dispute_points: Whether the written value is observed by other threads depends on Kokkos::single scheduling; on CUDA all threads of a team may be in one warp when team size is small (then ITS only). Mixed commit with simplifications, so wrong results at the parent could have more than one cause.

kernel: KokkosSparse::Impl::BSR_GEMV_Transpose_Functor<AMatrix,XVector,YVector>::operator()(team_member) (transposed BSR SpMV on GPU, one team per block row)
location_buggy: src/sparse/impl/KokkosSparse_spmv_bsrmatrix_impl.hpp:L943-L1002 at the buggy commit (conjugate branch: team_gemv into shared_view then parallel_for atomic_add reading shared_view(ijk) at ~L966-L971; non-conjugate branch: TeamVectorGemvInternal into shared_y then atomic_add reading shared_y[ijk] at ~L997-L1000; both inside 'for jBlock')
race_description: For each block jBlock of the row the team writes its partial product into the team-shared buffer (shared_y / shared_view), calls dev.team_barrier(), then threads read the buffer in a TeamVectorRange parallel_for with atomic_add into y. There is no barrier after that loop, so threads that finish early start iteration jBlock+1 and overwrite the shared buffer with the next GEMV while other threads are still reading the previous block's values.
fix_summary: Adds dev.team_barrier() at the end of each jBlock iteration in both the conjugate and non-conjugate branches (4 lines).
evidence: Commit 'Add barrier' (U. Hetmaniuk, 2022-02-24), 4 added lines and no message; the mechanism is read from the diff context (shared buffer reused per jBlock).
driver: unit_test/sparse/Test_Sparse_spmv_bsr.hpp (and Test_Sparse_BsrMatrix.hpp) on the Cuda backend with mode 'T' or 'H' (transpose) and a BSR matrix with block_dim >= 2 and several blocks per row; the GPU transposed path is spMatVec_transpose (TeamPolicy) in the same file. Small matrices (tens of rows) are enough: well under 1e6 accesses.
build_notes: Needs Kokkos with CUDA (-DKokkos_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DKokkos_ARCH_ADA89=ON) then kokkos-kernels with -DKokkosKernels_ENABLE_TESTS=ON and only sparse tests, or a ~40-line main that builds a BsrMatrix and calls KokkosSparse::spmv('T', ...). Check out 49eb4ddbf11f622ea496f1f6a5e516d27ae658aa (parent). Builds take tens of minutes because of many instantiations; restrict ETI types.
already_reported_check: Not searched on GitHub issues.
dispute_points: No message; effect is rarely visible because the window needs a very fast thread to wrap around; the shared buffer size is block_dim elements so races hit only on those words. Mechanism inferred from reading the code, not from a report.

location_buggy: src/sparse/impl/KokkosSparse_spiluk_numeric_impl.hpp:L287-L300 at the buggy commit (lines 289/291 read L_values(k) into fact, line 293 'L_values(k) = fact;' executed by every thread of the team, then the TeamThreadRange loop at ~L294 uses fact); operator() of ILUKLvlSchedTP1NumericFunctor starts at ~L232. A thread that reads L_values(k) after another thread has already overwritten it multiplies/divides the factor a second time, so fact differs between threads and the following update loop applies wrong values (the commit title says: team barrier for accurate results).

driver: unit_test/sparse/Test_Sparse_spiluk.hpp (run_test_spiluk, ILU(k) of a small matrix with SEQLVLSCHD_TP1) on the Cuda execution space with a team that has more than one thread; the matrix is tiny (about 10 rows).

kernel: FixWallRegionKokkos<DeviceType>::wall_particle (Kokkos parallel_reduce functor, one thread per particle) calling RegBlockKokkos/RegSphereKokkos::surface_kokkos
location_buggy: src/KOKKOS/region_block_kokkos.h:L66-L175 at 257b8364 (writes d_contact[n].r/.delx/.dely/.delz/.iwall in surface_kokkos); src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_region_kokkos.cpp:L154-L175 (reads regionKK->d_contact[m] after the call)
race_description: The region object owns ONE device view d_contact (6 entries in RegBlockKokkos; sphere analogous) used as scratch by surface_kokkos(). wall_particle() is executed concurrently by one thread per particle, so all threads write the same d_contact[0..n] entries (WAW) and then read back contacts that another thread may have overwritten (RAW/WAR). Same address, different threads, plain accesses, no ordering inside the one parallel_reduce launch.
fix_summary: The caller passes a per-thread stack array 'Region::Contact contact[MAXCONTACT]' into surface_kokkos/surface_interior_kokkos/surface_exterior_kokkos; the region methods become const and the device view d_contact and its destructor are removed.
evidence: Commit message (Stan Moore, 2026-08-26) describes it as a data race on the region contact list: every thread wrote into the same list; with four OpenMP threads 637 of 1827 per-atom force and stress components differed from the plain style, up to 170 percent. It says explicitly the same race affects the GPU backends, which could not be tested.
driver: A LAMMPS input with 'fix wall/region' on a block or sphere region (e.g. lattice-filled box of a few hundred to a few thousand atoms), run with '-k on g 1 -sf kk' (Kokkos CUDA); the commit message mentions a small 1827-component test, so a few hundred atoms (about 600) and a handful of steps keep the access count tiny.
build_notes: cmake -D PKG_KOKKOS=ON -D Kokkos_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -D Kokkos_ARCH_ADA89=ON (4060 Ti is sm_89) -D BUILD_MPI=OFF with only the minimal packages (KOKKOS, plus whatever 'lj/cut' needs, which is core); 2026 code base so CUDA 13 should work (unverified). The buggy parent is from Aug 2026, so a plain checkout builds. Race lives in Kokkos-generated CUDA code, so it is a genuine intra-kernel race on sm_89.
already_reported_check: Not searched on GitHub issues. The commit message is itself the diagnosis.
dispute_points: GPU behaviour was NOT tested by the author (OpenMP only); on the CUDA backend d_contact is device global memory shared by all threads, so the race is the same by construction, but the observed wrong forces were measured on OpenMP. Kokkos functor copies per thread do not help because d_contact is a View (shared pointer).

kernel: BondFENEKokkos<DeviceType>::operator()(TagBondFENECompute<NEWTON_BOND,EVFLAG>, int n, EV_FLOAT&) (also BondFENEExpandKokkos and BondFENENMKokkos; Kokkos RangePolicy parallel_reduce/parallel_for over the bond list)
location_buggy: src/KOKKOS/bond_fene_kokkos.cpp:L196-L206 at the buggy commit (the 'd_flag() = 2' / 'd_flag() = 1' plain stores at L202/L204; d_flag is a device scalar view shared by all threads)
race_description: Every bond thread whose rlogarg < 0.1 stores 1 or 2 into the single device scalar d_flag with a plain store. Several overstretched bonds (different threads, usually different blocks) store to the same address concurrently, and the values differ (1 vs 2), so the surviving value depends on the schedule. The host reads the flag after the kernel to choose which error to raise.
fix_summary: Replaces the plain stores with Kokkos::atomic_max(&d_flag(), 2) / atomic_max(&d_flag(), 1) in all three FENE styles.
evidence: Commit message (S. Moore's KOKKOS bonded-style sweep, 2026-09-08): 'The three fene styles raced on a plain store to the error flag'. The same commit changes several unrelated things; no sanitizer output.
driver: A KOKKOS+CUDA LAMMPS run (lmp -k on g 1 -sf kk) of bond_style fene with at least two bonds stretched beyond about 0.9*R0 so that rlogarg < 0.1 on two threads, e.g. a hand-made data file of a few hundred bonds; unittest/force-styles/tests/bond-fene.yaml (existing small system) does not obviously stretch bonds that far (unverified). The error path then aborts LAMMPS after the kernel, which is acceptable for a detector run. A few thousand accesses.
build_notes: cmake -D PKG_KOKKOS=ON -D Kokkos_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -D Kokkos_ARCH_ADA89=ON -D PKG_MOLECULE=ON -D BUILD_MPI=OFF; same build as lammps-1.
already_reported_check: Not searched on GitHub issues.
dispute_points: Benign-looking race: all racing writers store a nonzero value and the flag is only used for an error message just before the run aborts. It only executes when a bond is overstretched, so a detector sees it only with a purpose-built input. Bundled with other fixes in the same commit.

location_buggy: include/mma_tensor_op/gemm.cuh:L371-L430 at e2247a11 (function perform_mma_divide_k_no: a_loader.r2s/b_loader.r2s smem stores at ~L378-L383 with no leading barrier; zgemm smem reads in the c/tile_k loops)

kernel: gSoftmax, gLogSoftmax, gCrossEntropyPick, gCrossEntropyPickBackward (same pattern; gSoftmaxGrad/gLogSoftmaxGrad are not touched by this commit)
location_buggy: src/tensor_operators.cu:L125 (`float* _max = _share + blockDim.x;`), L145-L147 (`__syncthreads(); float max = _max[0];` - every thread reads _max[0]), L148-L150 (`float* _sum = _share + blockDim.x; _sum[threadIdx.x] = 0.0;` - same shared region) in gSoftmax at buggy_commit; the same two statements in gLogSoftmax (L192-), gCrossEntropyPick and gCrossEntropyPickBackward
race_description: The max-reduction result lives in _max[0] and the following sum phase reuses exactly the same shared region (_sum == _max == _share + blockDim.x). After the barrier all threads read `float max = _max[0]` (L147) and immediately start the sum phase, where thread 0 resets `_sum[0] = 0.0` (L150). With blockDim.x > 32 a thread of warp 0 can zero the word before threads of other warps have read it, so those threads use max = 0 (wrong, overflow-prone exponentials). Different threads, same shared word, no barrier between the read and the write.
fix_summary: Adds `__syncthreads();` right after `float max = _max[0];` in all four kernels (and an unrelated cross_entropy reshape/ConstantNode change in the same commit).
evidence: Commit message 'fixed synchronization in softmax and cross-entropy ...' (Marcin Junczys-Dowmunt, 2017-01-03); the diff only adds a __syncthreads after the read of _max[0] in those kernels.

The original Shape/Tensor types can be replaced by two ints.
build_notes: Marian at that date needs Boost/cuDNN/CUDA 8 so do not build it; copy the kernel text (Shape replaced by rows/cols) into a standalone .cu and compile with nvcc -arch=sm_89.
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream).
dispute_points: Commit message does not say 'race'; the classification is from the diff. Real effect needs blockDim.x>32 (cols>32). Marian later rewrote these kernels (see lit-marian-2).

location_buggy: src/tensors/gpu/tensor_operators.cu:L375-L443 (gSoftmax): row loop `for(int bid = 0; bid < rows; bid += gridDim.x)` L381; shared region _share + blockDim.x reused as _max (L389-L411) and _sum (L414-L434); `so[id] = so[id] / _sum[0]` read at L435-L440; next iteration rewrites `_max[threadIdx.x] = -CUDA_FLT_MAX` at L390; same loop shape in gLogSoftmax, gSoftmaxGrad, gLogSoftmaxGrad at buggy_commit

The shared scratch (_sum[0]) is read by all threads at the end of row j (L438) and the next row's first statement overwrites the same region (`_max[threadIdx.x] = -CUDA_FLT_MAX`, L390) with no barrier at the end of the loop body. Needs rows > gridDim.x (the launcher caps blocks at MAX_BLOCKS = 65535) and blockDim.x > 32.

build_notes: Marian full build is heavy (Boost, protobuf/sentencepiece, CUDA); copy the kernels. Needs functional::Shape replaced by two ints and CUDA_FLT_MAX defined.
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream).
dispute_points: The commit bundles an unrelated utf8ToUpper change. The race only triggers when a block handles more than one row, which the production launcher only does for >65535 rows, so the shipped path rarely hits it; the extracted kernel with a small grid does.

kernel: mfem::internal::SmemPADiffusionApplyTetrahedron (forall_2D lambda, one element per block; simplex/Bernstein PA diffusion)
location_buggy: fem/integ/bilininteg_diffusion_kernels.hpp:L2172-L2212 at c1d1df3d (y(idx,e) -= ..., y(idx,e) += p2*u, += p2*v, += p2*w at ~L2198-L2210)
race_description: Each thread (a1,a2,a3) performs four read-modify-write updates y(idx,e) -=/+= on the element output vector: its own lex index and the three neighbours (a1+1,a2,a3), (a1,a2+1,a3), (a1,a2,a3+1). The neighbour index of one thread equals the own index (or another neighbour) of a different thread, so two threads RMW the same y(idx,e) with no atomic and no barrier between the four statements.
fix_summary: Inserts MFEM_SYNC_THREAD between the four updates. This was incomplete: the barriers sit inside thread-varying FOREACH_THREAD loops, and a0022e033 (2026-05-22, parent 3a2f286e2d50e88cc0e8b0b431efbc195914a9e8) restructured it to compute u,v,w into shared memory and do the four updates in separate uniform loops with barriers.
evidence: Commit title: ... fix race condition in diffusion integrator (jdongg, 2026-04-17); the follow-up a0022e033 title says 'fix thread race in SmemPADiffusionApplyTetrahedron'. No sanitizer output quoted.
driver: tests/unit/fem/test_pa_simplices.cpp TEST_CASE('PA Simplices', '[PartialAssembly][Simplices][GPU]') (file added by a6fcf162a on 2026-04-29, i.e. it does NOT exist at c1d1df3d; use the parent of a0022e033 or cherry-pick the test). Runs with --device cuda on small simplicial meshes, orders p=1..4.
build_notes: MFEM with CUDA, serial, no hypre/metis needed: make config MFEM_USE_CUDA=YES CUDA_ARCH=sm_89 then make -j and build tests/unit (Catch2 header is bundled); run ./unit_tests --device cuda '[Simplices]'. 2026 code base so CUDA 13 should be fine (unverified). The kernel is only chosen for tetrahedra with the shared-memory dispatch and D1D,Q1D within MAX_*_SIMPLEX limits.
already_reported_check: Not searched on GitHub issues/PRs; a PR number is unverified.
dispute_points: The conflicting accesses are in global y, not shared memory, so shared-memory-only tools (racecheck) would not see them. Neighbouring updates may often not overlap in the same step on real hardware. Whether Smem path is taken for the tests at small orders is unverified.

location_buggy: fem/integ/bilininteg_diffusion_pa_simplices.hpp:L1060-L1100 at 3a2f286e (the four y(idx,e) updates separated by MFEM_SYNC_THREAD inside nested MFEM_FOREACH_THREAD loops)
race_description: Same overlapping y(idx,e) updates as mfem-1. In this version the barriers separating the four updates are inside loops whose trip count depends on (a1,a2) (D1D-a1-a2-1 iterations), so threads with an empty loop never reach the barrier; the updates of different threads are therefore still not reliably separated, and a barrier executed by only part of a block is undefined.
fix_summary: Computes u,v,w once into shared memory (uvw reuse of sm0) and performs the four y updates in four separate, uniform FOREACH_THREAD loops each followed by MFEM_SYNC_THREAD outside the divergent region; also changes the launch thread count to max(Q1D,D1D).
evidence: Commit title: Fix number of threads in simplices kernels to allow D1D > Q1D, ..., fix thread race in SmemPADiffusionApplyTetrahedron (camierjs, 2026-05-22).
driver: tests/unit/fem/test_pa_simplices.cpp TEST_CASE('PA Simplices', '[PartialAssembly][Simplices][GPU]') exists at the parent; run with --device cuda.
build_notes: Same MFEM CUDA build as mfem-1; this parent is the better target because the unit test exists there.
already_reported_check: Not searched on GitHub issues/PRs.
dispute_points: Mixed commit (thread-count fix for D1D > Q1D plus the race fix), so some wrong-result behaviour at the parent may come from the thread count, not the race. Global-memory conflict only.

location_buggy: Source/Math/GPUMatrixCUDAKernels.cuh:L850-L866 (init: colMax[0] = -1e7 by every thread L859, partials[tid] = -1e7 L860), L910-L915 (`if (threadIdx.x==0) colMax[0] = max(max(partials[0],partials[1]),max(partials[2],partials[3]));` L910-L913 then `partials[threadIdx.x] = 0.0f;` L914 BEFORE the __syncthreads at L915), L918-L919 (colSum[0] = 0.0f by every thread) at buggy_commit
race_description: After the max tree reduction thread 0 reads partials[0..3] (L912) to produce colMax. Immediately afterwards, and before the barrier at L915, every thread reuses the same array for the sum phase with `partials[threadIdx.x] = 0.0f` (L914). Threads 1-3 therefore zero partials[1..3] with no ordering against thread 0's read of those same words: a write-after-read hazard on shared memory (threads 0-3 sit in the same warp, so the hazard is intra-warp and only shows under independent scheduling or in a tool that does not assume lock-step). The commit also removes the `colMax[0] = -10000000` / `colSum[0] = 0` initialisations that every thread performed (same-value writes to one location; the intervening barriers order them before the later thread-0 write, so they are not shown to be hazardous, and which accesses cuda-memcheck actually reported is unverified).
fix_summary: Moves `partials[threadIdx.x] = 0.0f` to after the __syncthreads(), and removes the redundant all-thread initialisations of colMax[0] and colSum[0]; the follow-up ecdacd90 moves the __shared__ colMax/colSum declarations next to their use.
evidence: Commit message: 'Fixed races in the columnwise softmax GPU kernel implementation detected and reported by cuda-memcheck' (Amit Agarwal, 2016-06-14), merged to master next day via branch amitaga/fixRacesInColumnwiseSoftmaxKernel. This is a racecheck-found, maintainer-fixed race in a 17k-star framework.
driver: No unit test in the commit. Extract the kernel (it only needs CUDA_LONG, IDX2C and the ElemType template) into a 40-line driver: _assignColumnwiseLogSoftmaxOf<float><<<numCols, 512>>>(a, us, numCols, numRows) with e.g. numRows=1000, numCols=64 (about 6.4e4 elements). In the repo it is called from GPUMatrix<ElemType>::AssignColumnwiseLogSoftmaxOf.
build_notes: Do not build CNTK (huge, needs MPI/cuDNN/boost). Copy the kernel plus `#define IDX2C(i,j,ld) (((j)*(ld))+(i))` and `typedef int CUDA_LONG;` into a .cu file and compile with nvcc -arch=sm_89.
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream, repository archived 2022).
dispute_points: Written for 2016-era lock-step warps: threads 0-3 and the read/zero happen inside one warp, so in practice the pre-Volta result was deterministic; the hazard is formally a race (racecheck reported it) and real under ITS. Commit message says 'races' plural, but the all-thread initialisation writes of colMax[0]/colSum[0] are ordered against the thread-0 writes by barriers in the code shown, so only the L912/L914 pair is a clear conflicting access. The repo is archived, so the buggy tree no longer builds on modern CUDA; only the kernel is used.

location_buggy: gsplat/cuda/csrc/RasterizeToPixelsFromWorld3DGSBwd.cu:L410-L417 at b08c98c2 (write `rgbs_batch[t*CDIM+(CDIM-1)] = hit_dist` at L416, guarded by use_hit_distance); readers in the later loops (v_alpha loop and `buffer[k] += rgbs_batch[t*CDIM+k]*fac`, ~L460 and ~L560)
race_description: Block = one 16x16 pixel tile (256 threads); `rgbs_batch` is a shared array indexed by Gaussian t (one slot per batch Gaussian, shared by all pixels). When use_hit_distance is set, EVERY pixel thread recomputes its own per-pixel hit distance and stores it into the same shared slot rgbs_batch[t*CDIM+CDIM-1]; the 256 threads write different values to one address and read it back with no barrier, so each pixel can use another pixel's hit distance (WAW + RAW between warps).
fix_summary: Keep the per-pixel hit distance in a register (local_hit_dist) and select it in the two consumers instead of overwriting shared rgbs_batch; test tolerances tightened.
evidence: Commit message: stored recomputed hit_distance in shared-memory rgbs_batch which is per-Gaussian but hit_distance is per-pixel, 'this caused a race condition'; tests/test_basic.py tolerances for means/scales/backgrounds/rays tightened ~10-40x after the fix.
driver: pytest tests/test_basic.py -k test_rasterize_to_pixels_eval3d (parametrized with use_hit_distance=True; uses gsplat.cuda._wrapper.rasterize_to_pixels_eval3d_extra with the 3DGUT/eval3d backward; image downscaled to a few hundred pixels, assets/test_garden.npz). Backward only; need autograd.
build_notes: pip install -e . with torch (cu12.x/13.x) after git submodule update --init (glm); TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.9; BUILD_NO_CUDA=0. Extension compiled via torch.utils.cpp_extension (nvcc+ninja), several minutes.
dispute_points: Backward of an opt-in feature (use_hit_distance, world-space/3DGUT rasterizer, added early 2026), so window is short. Shared-memory race is a plain WAW with different values, effect is numerical error in gradients (visible as loose test tolerances).

location_buggy: gsplat/cuda/csrc/RasterizeToPixels2DGSSerialBatchBwd.cu:L672-L682 (gpuAtomicAdd into v_ray_transforms) and L697-L704 at d38d470e (plain read of v_ray_transforms_ptr[2],[5] and plain stores v_densify_ptr[0],[1])
race_description: Each warp atomically accumulates its partial gradient into v_ray_transforms[9*g+...] (global, per Gaussian g, contributed by every tile/warp that touches g). Right after, any valid lane executes plain stores v_densify[2g+0/1] = v_ray_transforms[9g+2/5] * depth, i.e. it plain-reads the same words that other warps/blocks are still atomically adding to (RAW against atomics), and many threads (all lanes, all tiles of g) store to the same v_densify slot (WAW, last writer wins). The stored value is a partial sum.
fix_summary: Each lane scales its z-gradient by depth, warp-reduces it with the other gradients and does a single gpuAtomicAdd per warp into v_densify (same path as v_ray_transforms); the plain read+store block is deleted.
evidence: Commit message: 'stored v_densify by reading the global v_ray_transforms while it was still being accumulated via atomicAdd from other blocks' giving 'a partial, last-writer-wins sum'; new test checks v_densify == v_ray_transforms[..,2]*depth.
driver: New test tests/test_2dgs.py::test_rasterize_to_pixels_2dgs_densify_gradient (N=1000 Gaussians, 640x480, 16x16 tiles, distloss=True, backward through rasterize_to_pixels_2dgs). Needs 2DGS build (gsplat.has_2dgs()). The test does not exist at the buggy commit - cherry-pick it from the fix commit.

race_description: Classic pre-Volta warp-synchronous programming: shared arrays are declared __shared__ volatile and a warp's lanes write to shared slots (s_diag, smem, s_threshold, s_b_row_ids, hash-set key tables) and then, after at most a ballot/shuffle, read slots written by other lanes, with no __syncwarp(). Under independent thread scheduling (sm_70+) the lanes are not guaranteed to be converged, so a lane can read a slot before the writing lane has stored it (RAW) or a lane can start the next row's reset while others still read (WAR).
fix_summary: Adds __syncwarp() after each warp-cooperative shared-memory write phase and inside the log-step reduction loops (about 20 sites in 5 files).
evidence: Commit title 'Adding missing synchronisation points. (#209)' by AMGX maintainers (no body). Follow-up PR 210 replaced raw __syncwarp by utils::syncwarp (for pre-Volta builds). No sanitizer output given.
driver: AMGX examples/amgx_capi.c with examples/matrix.mtx (12x12 Poisson-like matrix) and a classical-AMG config such as src/configs/AMG_CLASSICAL_PMIS.json or FGMRES_CLASSICAL_AGGRESSIVE_PMIS.json (the strength kernel runs at AMG setup of every classical config; distance2 kernels need D2 interpolator config - exact config unverified). Tiny input -> a few thousand thread-accesses.
build_notes: cmake -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89 (AMGX option CUDA_ARCH) without MPI (-DCMAKE_NO_MPI=1); AMGX has heavy template instantiation (30-60 min). Build parent 36e619b1 and fix 8bb693b4. AMGX HEAD is mid-2026, so the sync-fixed code is current; for 'buggy' use the parent commit.
dispute_points: Volatile shared memory + implicit warp sync is exactly the pattern CUDA 9 deprecated; on real hardware the divergence rarely makes it manifest. Detector must model ITS (no implicit warp convergence).

kernel: DILU_setup_NxN_kernel<Matrix_type,Vector_type,N,CTA_SIZE,WARP_SIZE> (small-block DILU setup: per NxN group of lanes inverts a block in volatile shared memory)
location_buggy: src/solvers/multicolor_dilu_solver.cu at buggy_commit: 'my_s_A_mtx[lane_id_mod_NxN] = e_out;' L618 followed directly by the row loop reading 'my_s_A_mtx[N*row+row]' L624; row scale 'my_s_A_mtx[N*row + lane_id_mod_NxN_mod_N] *= diag' L637 then rank-1 update reading 'my_s_A_mtx[N*lane_id_mod_NxN_div_N + row]' / '[N*row + ...]' L642; update then 'if (is_active && lane_id_mod_NxN_div_N == 0)' reading column row L651-L654; only syncwarp is at the end of each row iteration (L656, added by 677df76)
race_description: Groups of NxN lanes of one warp invert an NxN block in __shared__ volatile storage. Phases (store block, scale pivot row, eliminate, write inverse column) pass data between different lanes of the group purely by program order inside the warp, relying on lockstep execution and volatile; on Volta+ independent thread scheduling lets lanes of the group (and different groups) run out of order, so a lane may read an element before the lane that owns it has written it (RAW) or overwrite it before it was read (WAR).
fix_summary: Insert utils::syncwarp() after the initial store of e_out, after the pivot-row scale, and after the elimination update (a fourth syncwarp at the end of each row iteration had been added six days earlier by 677df76 'attempting to fix sync issues in multicolor DILU for NxN').
evidence: Commit message 'Fixing issue with DILU synchronisation. Fixing issues with matrix IO.' (Matthew Martineau, 2023-12-11); previous commit 677df76 'attempting to fix sync issues in multicolor DILU for NxN'. No sanitizer log.
driver: AMGX configuration using MULTICOLOR_DILU on a block-structured matrix with small block size N (NxN <= 16 or so selects DILU_setup_NxN_kernel; the exact selection rule is unverified), e.g. examples/amgx_capi.c with a block matrix input and config src/configs/PCG_DILU.json / CG_DILU.json; tiny matrix suffices (only the warp-level phases matter).
build_notes: cmake -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89 without MPI; template-heavy (30-60 min). Build parent cd856936 vs fix 2cf13ab. __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700 so utils::syncwarp is a real __syncwarp on sm_89.
dispute_points: Intra-warp lockstep-assumption race; may not produce wrong results on real hardware. The maintainers' own earlier commit says 'attempting to fix', so the exact failing configuration is not documented. Racecheck-style tools that assume warp lockstep will not flag it.
