location_buggy: cub/test/catch2_test_block_run_length_decode.cu:L228-L247 (while loop; BlockStore Store calls at L237-L243 with no CTA_SYNC between iterations); racing smem accesses in cub/cub/block/block_store.cuh:L980 (tid 0 writes temp_storage.valid_items) vs L983 (all threads read it in StoreDirectWarpStriped), at buggy_commit
race_description: The test harness calls BlockStore<..., BLOCK_STORE_WARP_TRANSPOSE>::Store repeatedly in a loop using the same temp_storage and without a barrier between iterations. Each Store has thread 0 write the volatile temp_storage.valid_items, a barrier, then every thread reads valid_items. In the next iteration thread 0 can overwrite valid_items (and the per-warp exchange buffers) while slower warps are still reading the previous value, because BlockStore's contract requires a CTA_SYNC before temp_storage reuse.
fix_summary: Harness switched both BlockStores to BLOCK_STORE_DIRECT (no shared memory), so repeated RunLengthDecode calls can still be tested without synchronization (RLD itself is documented as not needing syncs). Not a library change.
evidence: Issue #1903 pastes compute-sanitizer racecheck output (cub.cpp17.test.block_run_length_decode): Write at block_store.cuh:980, Read at block_store.cuh:983, 9208 hazards, Error severity. Initially judged possibly a false positive because valid_items is volatile; the PR author concluded it was a harness race.
driver: cub/test/catch2_test_block_run_length_decode.cu (single binary cub.cpp17.test.block_run_length_decode); a standalone kernel with one block of 64 threads and a few hundred runs reproduces: the issue's instance is BlockStore<float,64,1,WARP_TRANSPOSE>.
build_notes: Catch2-based test; to avoid CMake, copy AgentTestBlockRunLengthDecode and the TestKernel into a main() with fixed small inputs (or build the CCCL cub test target via CMake with -DCCCL_ENABLE_CUB=ON and Catch2 fetched through CPM, which needs network). Header-only CCCL at buggy_commit. Not compiled here.
dispute_points: A skeptic could say this is misuse of the test (the test purposely calls CUB collectives without the documented sync) rather than a bug in CUB; the maintainers first called the report a possible false positive (volatile) before fixing the harness. The racing accesses are real shared-memory conflicts though, and the fix removed the shared memory use.

kernel: cub::DeviceSelectSweepKernel -> AgentSelectIf::ConsumeSubsequentTile/ConsumeFirstTile (in-place DeviceSelect::If/Flagged, thrust::remove_if with aliasing in/out)
location_buggy: cub/cub/agent/agent_select_if.cuh:L831-L842 (BlockLoad of the tile's items + CTA_SYNC), L845-L862 (look-back then Scatter<IS_LAST_TILE,false>) and cub/cub/agent/single_pass_scan_operators.cuh:L602-L626 (SetInclusive/SetPartial = detail::store_relaxed) and L639-L646 (load_relaxed) at buggy_commit
race_description: For in-place stream compaction (d_out aliases d_in) block k loads its tile of items directly from global memory (BLOCK_LOAD_DIRECT-type policies, no staging through shared memory) and then publishes its selection count in the decoupled look-back tile state with a *relaxed* 64-bit store (primitive offset type). A later block i>k reads that status with a relaxed load, gets its output offset and scatters compacted items, which can overwrite d_in locations that block k has not (formally) finished loading. CTA_SYNC only orders threads of block k with each other; nothing orders thread loads of block k before block i's stores across blocks (no release/acquire), so global WAR load(blk k) vs store(blk i).
fix_summary: Introduce MemoryOrder acquire_release: tile-state SetPartial/SetInclusive use st.release and WaitForValid/LoadValid use ld.acquire (with a __threadfence hoist for pre-Volta) when the select may alias and the load does not go through smem; a CTA_SYNC before the status store orders all threads' loads; MayAlias template parameter plumbed from dispatch/thrust.
evidence: Issue #1730: intermittent wrong results from thrust::remove_if (zip iterator of 4 arrays, 5M items) when many processes share the GPU. PR #1782 explains: a block's input items may already be overwritten by a later block; needs primitive look-back type + BlockLoad that does not use smem; fix is st.release/ld.acquire on tile state. Bug introduced in CCCL/CUB 2.3 and absent in 2.2.
driver: Reproducer from issue #1730: thrust::remove_if(zip_iterator<int16,int16,uint32,uint32>, N, pred) in place; scale N down (the issue uses 5,000,000: far above the budget; several tile sizes of ~ 10^4-10^5 items give >1 block, tile = BLOCK_THREADS*ITEMS_PER_THREAD from policy). Alternative: cub::DeviceSelect::If with d_in == d_out on struct items. The race is probabilistic at run time (needs GPU contention), so the detector must find it from the access/ordering structure.
build_notes: Header-only: nvcc -std=c++17 -arch=sm_89 -I thrust -I cub -I libcudacxx/include test.cu against a checkout of buggy_commit (or any CCCL 2.3-2.5 release; CUDA 12.5-12.6 toolkits). Note CUDA 13 toolkits bundle CCCL 3.x which already has the fix, so the buggy tree must be fetched from git. Which BlockLoad algorithm the sm_89 policy picks for this value type was not checked (race needs a non-smem load policy). Not compiled here.
dispute_points: Requires reasoning about a relaxed vs release/acquire status flag. Hardware-wise the loads of the earlier block have already completed into registers before CTA_SYNC and the relaxed store, so the window is tiny (issue needed 40 processes under MPS); a detector that treats any atomic/flag access as synchronizing will not flag it. Under the PTX memory model it is a real data race (relaxed does not create happens-before). A skeptic could call it a memory-model-only race; maintainers accepted it as a real bug with an observed wrong output.

kernel: AgentRadixSortDownsweep::ProcessTile -> ScatterKeys then GatherScatterValues/LoadValues (DeviceRadixSort downsweep kernel, key-value sort)
location_buggy: cub/agent/agent_radix_sort_downsweep.cuh:L183-L200 (union _TempStorage aliasing load_values with exchange_keys/relative_bin_offsets), L244-L264 (ScatterKeys reads exchange_keys L256 and relative_bin_offsets L258), L379-L410 (LoadValues -> BlockLoadValuesT(temp_storage.load_values).Load), L443-L470 (GatherScatterValues, LoadValues call L459, no CTA_SYNC before it), L587-L591 (ProcessTile calls ScatterKeys then GatherScatterValues back to back) at buggy_commit
race_description: In a key-value radix sort, ScatterKeys ends with every thread reading arbitrary slots of temp_storage.exchange_keys[] and temp_storage.relative_bin_offsets[]. ProcessTile then calls GatherScatterValues, whose LoadValues uses BlockLoad (BLOCK_LOAD_TRANSPOSE / WARP_TRANSPOSE policies, i.e. a BlockExchange through shared memory) with temp_storage.load_values, which is a member of the same union as exchange_keys/relative_bin_offsets. There is no barrier between the last key-scatter read and the first BlockLoad shared-memory write, so a warp that finishes ScatterKeys early overwrites the aliased shared-memory bytes while slower warps still read them (WAR). Whether the write lands on a slot another thread still reads depends on key/value sizes and the exchange padding (equal-size keys/values without padding map thread t onto its own slot and are benign); the sub-case with 32-bit keys and 64-bit values, or ITEMS_PER_THREAD>4 power of two with padding, overlaps cross-thread.
fix_summary: Inserted CTA_SYNC() at the start of GatherScatterValues (before LoadValues) in the pair-sorting specialization. The same commit also moves a ShuffleIndex register-pressure workaround for valid_items from this function into LoadDirectBlocked/Striped/WarpStriped in block_load.cuh (unrelated to the race). Current cccl keeps the __syncthreads() before LoadValues in GatherScatterValues (cccl cub/agent/agent_radix_sort_downsweep.cuh L424 at HEAD).
evidence: Commit message is only 'Fix for missing CTA-barrier' (author dumerrill, 2018-01-24); the diff adds one CTA_SYNC(). No issue or racecheck output found; the hazard analysis above is from reading the diff and the union layout (the maintainer's own reason for the barrier is not stated).
driver: cub::DeviceRadixSort::SortPairs (values present => non-keys-only path) via cub/test/test_device_radix_sort.cu at the buggy commit, or a ~20-line program calling SortPairs on e.g. 1M uint32 keys + uint64 values (about 5 downsweep passes, each key and value touched a few times, well below 1e8 thread accesses). A full-range 32-bit key sort already exercises the Alt (MEMOIZE + BLOCK_LOAD_TRANSPOSE) policy in 3 of 5 passes on sm_89.
build_notes: Check out cub at 008293a7 (Jan 2018, pre-CCCL repo, header-only) and put it first on the include path ahead of the toolkit's CCCL; compile only a small main with nvcc -arch=sm_89 -I<cub-checkout>. Do not use cub/test/test_util.h unmodified with CUDA 13 (it likely uses cudaDeviceProp fields removed in CUDA 13, e.g. clockRate; unverified); write a standalone driver instead. Old CUB may need small patches for CUDA 13 (unverified). Policy selection on sm_89 (Policy700, dispatch_radix_sort.cuh at buggy commit): the main DownsweepPolicy is RADIX_RANK_MATCH (LoadValues = LoadDirectWarpStriped, no shared memory, no race) with 7-bit digits for keys wider than 1 byte; AltDownsweepPolicy is RADIX_RANK_MEMOIZE + BLOCK_LOAD_TRANSPOSE with 6-bit digits (shared-memory BlockExchange, race window). The dispatcher uses Alt for the first max_alt_passes = num_passes*7 - num_bits passes (dispatch L1157-L1179), so a full 32-bit key sort (5 passes, 3 Alt) or 64-bit (10 passes, 6 Alt) exercises the racy configuration. DeviceSegmentedRadixSort::SortPairs also uses BLOCK_LOAD_TRANSPOSE + MEMOIZE.
dispute_points: The commit message does not state what was racy and the same commit bundles an unrelated register-pressure refactor, so attribution of the hazard is my reading of the diff. Exact racing slots depend on key/value width and BlockExchange padding; for 32-bit key + 32-bit value without padding the aliasing is thread-private and racecheck would report nothing. The code is 2018-era (CUB 1.7.x -> fixed in 1.7.5), so it only runs from the archived cub checkout, not from current cccl.

links: https://github.com/NVlabs/cub/issues/91 (cited in the commit message only for the unrelated compiler-segfault workaround)
kernel: cub::BlockRadixRankMatch::RankKeys (block-level collective used by the downsweep of DeviceRadixSort with RADIX_RANK_MATCH policies)
location_buggy: cub/block/block_radix_rank.cuh:L588-L628 at buggy_commit (volatile digit_counters pointer L588, MatchAny L603, read of *digit_counters[ITEM] L609, 'Todo: warp-sync' L611, leader write L621-L624, 'Todo: warp-sync' L625, ranks[ITEM] L628); shared array warp_digit_counters[RADIX_DIGITS][PADDED_WARPS] declared L519
race_description: Each warp strip-mines its keys; for every key all lanes read the warp-private shared counter warp_digit_counters[digit][warp_id] (L609) and then the lowest lane among peers with the same digit overwrites it with prefix+count (L621-L624). Lanes with the same digit therefore read and write the same shared word within one warp, and the only thing ordering the peers' read before the leader's write (and the leader's write before the next key's read of the same counter) is implicit lockstep execution of a volatile access; the source even carries two 'Todo: warp-sync' comments at exactly these points. Under Volta independent thread scheduling a leader lane may run ahead, so a peer can read the already-incremented counter and get a wrong rank (WAR in the same iteration, RAW/WAW across iterations).
fix_summary: Replaced both 'Todo: warp-sync' comments with WARP_SYNC(0xFFFFFFFF) (one between the counter read and the leader's write, one between the write and the rank computation / next iteration). The same commit also adds '#pragma unroll' to a loop in BlockRadixRank (L362) and a workaround for a compiler segfault (NVlabs/cub#91); those parts are unrelated to the race. Current cccl keeps both barriers as __syncwarp(0xFFFFFFFF) in BlockRadixRankMatch::RankKeys (cub/cub/block/block_radix_rank.cuh L759-L780 at cccl HEAD).
evidence: Commit message: 'Added proper warp synchronization in match-rank' (author dumerrill, 2017-08-14), landing one day after match-based radix ranking was introduced (parent commit 2017-08-13). The removed 'Todo: warp-sync' comments are the maintainer's own marker of the missing ordering. No issue, no racecheck output found; sanitizer support at the time is unverified.
driver: Do not go through cub::DeviceRadixSort: at the buggy commit the highest policy (Policy620) uses RADIX_RANK_MEMOIZE, and on sm_89 only Policy350/600/610 (which are not chosen on a CC 8.9 device with a compute_89 build) use RADIX_RANK_MATCH. Write a ~40-line kernel that instantiates cub::BlockRadixRankMatch<128, 5 or 6 radix bits, false, BLOCK_SCAN_WARP_SCANS> with 2-4 keys per thread of random low-cardinality digits (many equal digits per warp, so peer sets have several lanes), calls RankKeys and checks ranks against a CPU stable-rank reference. One block of 128 to 256 threads: well under 1e4 thread accesses.
build_notes: Header-only: check out archived NVIDIA/cub at 6b397e4e (buggy) and 2f6f8430 (fixed), put the checkout first on the include path ahead of the CUDA toolkit's CCCL, compile the standalone kernel with nvcc -arch=sm_89. At that revision util_ptx.cuh already has the .sync PTX variants of ballot/shfl for __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700, so it should compile for sm_89, but old cub may still need small patches for CUDA 13 (unverified, not tried).
dispute_points: Pre-Volta this was correct lockstep code and the compiler can keep the read/branch/write sequence convergent (the straight-line body has no divergent control flow except a tiny guarded store), so an actual wrong rank on sm_89 may never be observable; a happens-before race detector that models warp-level ordering would still flag the volatile read/write pair. No sanitizer report or bug report exists; the evidence is the maintainer's own 'Todo: warp-sync' comments and the commit title. It is part of a pre-Volta-era archive, only reachable with an old cub checkout.

kernel: cutlass::gemm::kernel::GemmGrouped<Mma_,Epilogue_,ThreadblockSwizzle_,Transposed>::operator() (persistent grouped GEMM; launched via cutlass::gemm::device::GemmGrouped / example 24_gemm_grouped)
location_buggy: include/cutlass/gemm/kernel/gemm_grouped.h:L479-L605 (persistent `while (problem_visitor.next_tile())` loop): epilogue at L590-L601 of tile i vs `mma(...)` at L550-L555 of tile i+1; SharedStorage union at L424-L428 aliases problem_visitor, main_loop and epilogue storage; at buggy_commit
race_description: GemmGrouped is a persistent-threadblock kernel: each CTA loops over tiles. SharedStorage is a union of problem_visitor, Mma main-loop storage and Epilogue storage. After the epilogue of tile i (warps read the epilogue smem tile to write D), a fast warp proceeds to advance() / next_tile() and begins the next tile's mainloop, whose cp.async/st.shared writes land on the same smem bytes while slower warps are still reading the epilogue data from tile i. No barrier separated epilogue and the next mainloop.
fix_summary: Insert __syncthreads() before the mma() of each tile: 'Wait for all threads to finish their epilogue phases from the previous tile'.
evidence: PR #386 body: added missing synchronization to avoid WAR hazards between tiles in Grouped GEMM; says compute-sanitizer --tool=racecheck reports zero errors after the change (so racecheck reported them before).
driver: examples/24_gemm_grouped/gemm_grouped.cu (--groups=N, problem sizes from a file or random) or test/unit/gemm/device/gemm_grouped_sm80.cu. The race needs a CTA to process >=2 tiles: use e.g. 4 groups of 256x256xK=128 with 128x128 tiles (16 tiles) and force threadblock_count to 1-2 (the example sets it from occupancy via sufficient(); a one-line edit in GemmGrouped args is needed).

location_buggy: dali/operators/image/remap/displacement_filter_impl_gpu.cuh:L148-L179 at 6ef40370 (loop 'for (int lidx = 0; lidx < loopCount; ++lidx)': per-thread writes to my_scratch at L159/L170, __syncthreads L173, cross-thread reads scratch_32[threadIdx.x + i*nThreads] at L177; next iteration writes my_scratch again with no barrier)
race_description: Each thread computes nPixelsPerThread pixels into its slice of the block-wide shared scratch[], one __syncthreads, then reads a differently-indexed (coalescing) view scratch_32[threadIdx.x + i*nThreads] to write the output. The loop has a barrier only between write and read phase; at the next lidx a fast warp writes its my_scratch slice while a slower warp is still reading scratch_32 from the previous iteration (needs loopCount >= 2, i.e. a block covering at least 2*nThreads*nPixelsPerThread pixels).
fix_summary: Adds 'if (lidx) __syncthreads();' at the top of each loop iteration (a barrier between the read phase of iteration k-1 and the write phase of iteration k) and moves the scratch_32 definition.
evidence: Commit title 'Add missing __syncthreads in displacement filter. (#6168)' by Michal Zientkiewicz; no body, no sanitizer output.
driver: DALI operators built on the displacement filter: fn.jitter, fn.sphere, fn.water (dali/operators/image/remap/{jitter,sphere,water}.cu) on GPU with 8-bit HWC images of several megapixels so each block gets loopCount>=2; C++ gtest dali/operators/image/remap/displacement_test.cc; python dali/test/python/operator_2/test_water.py. Exact image size needed is unverified.

kernel: topk_stage2_sampling<T, BLOCK_SIZE_, BLOCKS_PER_BEAM_> (second stage of top-k sampling, launched by invokeBatchTopKSampling and invokeTopKSampling)
location_buggy: src/fastertransformer/kernels/sampling_topk_kernels.cu:L224-L229 (__shared__ s_sum, s_max initialised by every thread), L245-L249 (`TopK_2<float> total = BlockReduce(temp_storage).Reduce(...)`; `if (ite == 0) s_max = total.u;` executed by all threads) and L251-L262 (thread 0 reads s_max in `total.u - s_max` and accumulates s_sum), at c1b51804
race_description: cub::BlockReduce::Reduce returns the aggregate only in thread 0; the value in other threads is undefined. The kernel nevertheless lets every thread execute `if (ite == 0) s_max = total.u;`, so threads 1..BLOCK_SIZE-1 store their (different, meaningless) values to the shared scalar s_max while thread 0 stores the real maximum and, a few instructions later and with no barrier in between, reads s_max in `__expf(total.u - s_max)`. That is a WAW between all threads plus a RAW into thread 0, and can corrupt the softmax normaliser. Also, s_max/s_sum are zero-initialised by every thread while thread 0 later accumulates into s_sum.
fix_summary: Wraps the s_max store inside the existing `if (tid == 0)` block and makes the s_sum = 0 initialisation tid == 0 only; s_max no longer pre-initialised by all threads.
evidence: Commit title 'Update sampling_topk_kernels.cu', body: 'fix: fix bug of race condition on shared memory'. The diff is the six-line change described above. No sanitizer log.
driver: tests/unittests/test_sampling_kernels.cu (CMake target test_sampling_kernels, links sampling_topk_kernels): testBatchTopKSamplingKernel / testBatchTopKSamplingWithSkipDecode call invokeBatchTopKSampling, testTopKSamplingKernel calls invokeTopKSampling. Test sizes are batch <= 32, vocab ~32k, top_k 1..1024 (exact cases unverified); BLOCK_SIZE_2_ is 128 or 256 threads, so cross-warp. Roughly 1e6-1e7 accesses.
build_notes: FasterTransformer CMake project (cmake -DSM=89 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_UNIT_TEST? ... ; option names unverified), repo is archived (2023) and uses CUDA 11-era CMake, cutlass/ 3rdparty submodules; a CUDA 13 toolkit is likely to break (cub/thrust and removed APIs): use CUDA 11.8 or 12.x. Alternative: compile sampling_topk_kernels.cu alone with nvcc -arch=sm_89 -I src -I 3rdparty, plus the memory_utils/cuda_utils it includes, and a small main() (unverified).
dispute_points: The commit message calls it 'race condition on shared memory' without detail. In practice the extra writes store a per-thread value of `total` that CUB leaves as the thread's own input (so the damage depends on CUB internals); the s_sum init is ordered by the barriers inside BlockReduce, so that half is benign. The s_max WAW/RAW is the real conflict.

location_buggy: src/main/cpp/src/shuffle_assemble.cu: `if (threadIdx.x == words_in_batch - 1) { prev_word[0] = prev; }` L1408 (shared __shared__ bitmask_type prev_word[block_size], L1266) vs `store_word(dst_word_index, prev_word[0])` by threadIdx.x==0 L1416-L1417 after the do/while loop, at buggy_commit

After the loop thread 0 reads prev_word[0] to write the final trailing word (L1417). The barrier at L1406 precedes the store, and the loop exits without another barrier, so for batches with more than 32 words the writer and thread 0 are in different warps and the read is unordered with the store.

race_description: XQA fills shared-memory K, V and merge tiles with per-lane cp.async (ldgsts) and then waits with ldgsts::waitGroup<N>(), which only completes the calling lane's own copy groups. The tile is then consumed by ldmatrix/loads that read elements copied by other lanes of the warp, with no __syncwarp between the wait and the consumer (RAW across lanes). The merge-tile buffer is a two-stage circular buffer: without a second __syncwarp after consuming a slot a fast lane can issue the next loadBufAsync into the slot that a slow lane is still reading (WAR).
fix_summary: Adds __syncwarp() after ldgsts::waitGroup in the K-tile and V-tile paths and in the multi-block merge loop, plus a __syncwarp at the end of the merge loop body before the circular-buffer slot can be overwritten.
evidence: Commit '[https://nvbugs/6530268][fix] Fix XQA race condition and attn sink numerical accuracy (#18141)'. Added comments: each lane waits only for its own async-copy groups, so the warp must be synchronised before consuming the tile; make every lane finish the ldmatrix/row-stat reads before any lane overwrites the slot. location_buggy: modules/cudaobjdetect/src/cuda/hog.cu:L316-L343 at a0f86455 (kernel), reduce_smem at L284-L309; two reduce_smem calls at L334 and L339 reuse the same smem 'squares'
race_description: The kernel calls reduce_smem(squares, elem*elem) twice on the same shared buffer. reduce_smem finishes by returning smem[0] (every thread reads smem[0] after thread 0 wrote it, with a __syncthreads before the read). The second call immediately writes smem[tid] again (start of the block reduce), with no barrier after the first call's final read of smem[0]; a slow thread may still be reading smem[0] when thread 0 overwrites it (WAR), and the beginning of the 2nd reduction may also race with the first call's tail. For default HOG (36 bins -> nthreads=64, 2 warps) this is cross-warp.
fix_summary: Adds __syncthreads() before each of the two reduce_smem calls (the second one is the necessary one).
evidence: Commit 'Race condition bug-fix in hog.cu', refs Itseez/opencv issue 5721; author says the second __syncthreads is necessary, the first added for symmetry.
driver: cv::cuda::HOG::create()->compute(gpuImg, descriptors) or ->detectMultiScale; tests: opencv_test_cudaobjdetect --gtest_filter='*HOG*' (modules/cudaobjdetect/test/test_objdetect.cpp, now in opencv_contrib). 64x128 or 640x480 images; one block per HOG block histogram.
build_notes: The fix predates the 2018 move of CUDA modules to opencv_contrib; buggy source is OpenCV 3.0/3.1 era (Dec 2015) and does not build with CUDA 13. At current contrib HEAD the same two __syncthreads exist (hog.cu L338, L344); to reproduce, take current hog.cu from opencv_contrib (modules/cudaobjdetect/src/cuda/hog.cu) and delete the two '__syncthreads(); // prevent race condition' lines, then run the HOG test - cheap and valid for the detector.
dispute_points: Old (2015); the guarantee is subtle: for size==32 (1 warp) the code uses shfl and no smem, so only nthreads>=64 variants race. Reduce internals (cv::cuda::device::reduce with volatile smem) also have warp-synchronous steps. Racecheck may or may not report; no sanitizer output in the commit.

location_buggy: modules/cudaarithm/src/cuda/threshold.cu:L212-L217 at 735b7a0a (the `if (original_score == score) *otsu_threshold = threshold - 1;`, kernel starts L176)
race_description: otsu_score runs as a single 256-thread block (8 warps), one thread per candidate threshold. After a block min-reduction every thread whose score equals the minimum executes a plain store `*otsu_threshold = threshold - 1`. When several thresholds tie (e.g. an image containing only values 0 and 255, where all thresholds 1..255 give the same score) several threads store DIFFERENT values to the same global word with nothing ordering them; the surviving value is whichever thread stores last.
fix_summary: Adds has_lowest_score(): __syncthreads_count counts ties; if more than one, a block min-reduction over the tied thresholds picks the smallest so exactly one thread writes. Also adjusts bin_idx >= threshold to > threshold and guards division by zero (unrelated hunks).
evidence: PR #3970 'Fix race condition in Otsu's method': with equal thresholds 'the last thread to write the output gets to choose' the threshold, so returned threshold varies per run (image identical).
driver: Test CUDA_Arithm/ThresholdOtsuMulti.Accuracy added by the PR (modules/cudaarithm/test/test_element_operations.cpp): 1x100 CV_8U image, left half 0 right half 255, cv::cuda::threshold(src,dst,0,255,THRESH_BINARY|THRESH_OTSU). Trivial input size; the test file at the buggy commit lacks the test, so write the 10-line program or cherry-pick the test hunk.
build_notes: Build opencv + opencv_contrib with -DBUILD_LIST=core,cudev,cudaarithm,ts (or whole cuda modules) -DOPENCV_EXTRA_MODULES_PATH=.../opencv_contrib/modules -DWITH_CUDA=ON -DCUDA_ARCH_BIN=8.9; only cudaarithm+cudev+core needed. Pass the file via NVCC; the threshold kernels were added in 6329974d (2025-06-19, PR #3943), so buggy window is 2025-06-19..2025-07-17 on 4.x/5.x.
dispute_points: Skeptic: in the original code all racing threads store a value that is equally valid (any tied threshold is a correct Otsu threshold) and the thresholded image is identical, so it is 'benign'. But it is a genuine plain-store WAW between different threads on one address with different values, no ordering, result nondeterministic (the maintainer-accepted fix says so explicitly). Kernel was only introduced one month earlier, so the buggy window is short.

location_buggy: modules/cudafilters/src/cuda/median_filter.cu:L128-L157 (Par8: Hscan[tx]+=Hscan[tx-1/-2/-4] at L136,139,142) and L159-L186 (Par32: L167,170,173,176,179) at 61e0a2de
race_description: Inside a single 32-thread block (blockDim.x=32, launched by medianFiltering_gpu) the Hillis-Steele scan on the shared array Hscan is done in place: `if (k<=tx && tx<N) Hscan[tx] += Hscan[tx-k];`. In each step thread tx reads Hscan[tx-k] while thread tx-k (if tx-k>=k) writes Hscan[tx-k] in the same step; only a __syncthreads between steps exists, none between the read and the write inside a step. Correct only under lock-step warp execution; racy under independent thread scheduling.
fix_summary: Replaces the in-place update with a two-phase macro scanNeighbor: read both operands into a register, __syncthreads(), then write. Also refactors the median search into findMedian macro.
evidence: Commit message 'remove danger race condition' (Tomoaki Teshima, ported from opencv/opencv 5d1540f4). Same function had an earlier race fix in 2018 (see opencv_contrib-3) after test Median_Accuracy failed.
driver: opencv_test_cudafilters --gtest_filter='*Median*' (modules/cudafilters/test/test_filters.cpp, PARAM_TEST_CASE Median, calls cv::cuda::createMedianFilter(CV_8UC1,windowSize,partitions=128)); or a small program: createMedianFilter on a e.g. 640x480 CV_8UC1 GpuMat, window 5. NOTE: at HEAD the path is guarded by __OPENCV_USE_WAVELET_MATRIX_FOR_MEDIAN_FILTER_CUDA__ (wavelet matrix variant is an alternative) - the histogram path is the one to run. Block = 32 threads x 128 partitions: tiny.
build_notes: Build opencv + contrib with -DBUILD_LIST=core,imgproc,cudev,cudafilters,cudaarithm,ts -DWITH_CUDA=ON -DCUDA_ARCH_BIN=8.9; opencv_contrib at 61e0a2de (2021-02) is old: needs a matching opencv 4.x checkout (4.5.x era) and may not compile with CUDA 13 without small patches (texture refs / deprecated APIs). Alternative: lift median_filter.cu + a 30-line main into a standalone nvcc test (needs only PtrStepSz from opencv2/core/cuda).
dispute_points: Entirely intra-warp: with blockDim.x=32 all threads of the scan sit in one warp, and compilers emit all loads before the stores, so the bug has likely never produced a wrong result in practice (maintainers called it a 'danger' condition, no failing test attached to this commit). Only formal under ITS. Also old code base: build at 2021 commit with CUDA 13 may need patches.

location_buggy: modules/cudafilters/src/cuda/median_filter.cu:L123-L152 (Par8, chain at L130-L137) and L154-L180 (Par32, chain at L161-L172) at cfab48b4
race_description: The 8-/32-wide inclusive scan of the shared array Hscan is written as `if(tx<N){ if(tx>=1) Hscan[tx]+=Hscan[tx-1]; if(tx>=2) Hscan[tx]+=Hscan[tx-2]; if(tx>=4) ...; }` with NO barrier between the steps. Thread tx reads Hscan[tx-k] that thread tx-k is itself updating in the previous/next step; correctness relies on implicit warp lock-step with reconvergence between the divergent ifs (blockDim.x==32, one warp). Not guaranteed under Volta+ independent thread scheduling.
fix_summary: Splits the chain into separate steps, each guarded by its own range test and followed by __syncthreads().
evidence: Commit title 'fix test failure of cudafilters Median_Accuracy * avoid race condition' (Tomoaki Teshima, 2018, ported opencv->contrib). I.e. the accuracy test Median.Accuracy was actually failing.
driver: opencv_test_cudafilters --gtest_filter='*Median*' / cv::cuda::createMedianFilter(CV_8UC1, ksize, 128)->apply(src,dst) on 640x480 8-bit image. 32 threads x 128 blocks.
build_notes: Buggy state is Oct 2018 (OpenCV 4.0 era; contrib commit cfab48b4); will not build as is with CUDA 13 (cudaThreadSynchronize, texture refs etc.). Prefer lifting median_filter.cu into a standalone nvcc test, or use opencv_contrib-2 (same kernel, newer code). Included mainly because the commit message records an actual failing test.
dispute_points: Same kernel as opencv_contrib-2. The 2018 version had a stronger race (no barriers between steps in a divergent if-chain). The later 2021 fix showed that even after this fix an in-place read/write remained.

links: https://github.com/opencv/opencv/issues/13850 (issue number taken from the code comment '#13850'; page not opened, unverified)
kernel: stereoKernel<RADIUS> (cv::cuda::device::stereobm), with device helpers InitColSSD / StepDown / MinSSD / CalcSSD
location_buggy: modules/cudastereo/src/cuda/stereobm.cu:L259-L309 at 04041fd7 (opencv/opencv parent b12e1acd has the identical blob ccc6737f). Racing accesses: col_ssd[]/col_ssd_extra[] stores in InitColSSD L221-L228 (called at L263/L267 at the top of the next d iteration) vs neighbour reads col_ssd[i] (i=1..2*RADIUS) in CalcSSD L79-L92 reached from MinSSD at L273 / L301 in the last row of the previous d iteration. No barrier between L308 (end of row loop) and L263.
race_description: stereoKernel runs a loop over disparity groups d. Each iteration re-initialises the per-thread columns of the dynamic shared array (InitColSSD writes col_ssd[k*(BLOCK_W+2R)] for k=0..7, threads < 2R also write col_ssd_extra) and then the row loop calls MinSSD, whose CalcSSD reads col_ssd[1..2R] and col_ssd[RADIUS+1..2R] of OTHER threads (thread t reads the slots of threads t+1..t+2R). After the last row of iteration d there is no __syncthreads before iteration d+1 overwrites those slots, so a fast warp can start InitColSSD(d+1) while a slower warp is still reading the old sums of its neighbours. The same commit also fixes barrier divergence: MinSSD (which contains __syncthreads) was only called by threads with X < cwidth-RADIUS, which hung on RTX 2080 Ti (Turing).
fix_summary: Added `__syncthreads(); // before initializing shared memory at the beginning of next loop` at the end of the d loop; additionally made all in-range threads call MinSSD (X<cwidth-RADIUS test moved to after the call, plus X guard inside CalcSSD) so the barriers inside it are reached uniformly.
evidence: Commit by Namgoo Lee (NVIDIA): 'Fix hanging issue on 2080 Ti; Fix racing issue'. Code comment in the fix says replacing __syncthreads with __syncwarp in MinSSD would yield a race condition 'Checked via cuda-memcheck --tool racecheck' (so racecheck was in use). Hang part refers to #13850.
driver: cv::cuda::StereoBM via cv::cuda::createStereoBM(numDisparities, blockSize) (modules/cudastereo/src/stereobm.cpp -> stereoBM_GPU -> kernel_caller<RADIUS>); test opencv_test_cudastereo --gtest_filter='*StereoBM*' (needs opencv_extra stereomatching images) or a small program with two random CV_8UC1 images 256x128, numDisparities=32, blockSize=5: grid ~ 2x6 blocks of 128 threads, order 10^7 shared accesses. Larger images (640x480, 64 disp) reach ~3e8, avoid.
build_notes: Option A (cheapest): lift stereobm.cu (single file, needs opencv2/core/cuda/common.hpp and PtrStepb/PtrStepSzb types) into a harness that calls stereoBM_GPU-equivalent; Option B: build opencv + opencv_contrib with -DBUILD_LIST=core,cudev,cudastereo,imgproc,cudaarithm -DWITH_CUDA=ON -DCUDA_ARCH_BIN=8.9 and check out 04041fd7 (contrib) for the buggy version (CUDA 13 may need small fixes to cudev/texture code of 2019: unverified). At contrib HEAD the fix is present at stereobm.cu:L434.
dispute_points: The trailing-barrier race needs a warp that finishes the last MinSSD of iteration d far before another warp (4 warps per block), and the corrupted slots are neighbour sums used immediately for SSD comparison, so wrong disparities are rare; the author's own comment concentrates on the hang. The commit mixes two fixes (barrier divergence + WAR) so the 'racing' half is identified from the added barrier comment rather than a separate bug report.

location_buggy: src/adv-cuda/adv.cu:L1-L189; missing barriers after L86 (end of the c-loop) and after L137 (end of the k-loop body) at buggy_commit
race_description: Block is 16x16 (8 warps). s_U1/s_V1/s_W1 are read in the c-loop (L71-L73, after the barrier at L66) and then overwritten at L89-L91 at the start of the k-loop with no barrier in between; inside the k-loop they are written (L89-L91), barrier (L93), read (L100-L108), and rewritten by the next k iteration with no trailing barrier. dispute_points: Needs >1 warp per block (n_gpu_threads > 32); reader/writer window is small.

kernel: kps::details::BlockXReduce<T,ReduceOp> (used by ReduceAnyKernel / ReduceLastDim via kps::Reduce kGlobalMode)
location_buggy: paddle/phi/kernels/primitive/compute_primitives.h:L87-L118 at cb746665 (read shared[bid*block_dim_x+lane] L104 vs write shared[threadIdx.y]=val L114)
race_description: After the warp-level stage, every thread reads shared[bid*block_dim_x + lane] (L104) and runs a shuffle reduction; then threads with threadIdx.x==0 store shared[threadIdx.y] = val (L114) into the same 2*kWarpSize buffer. Nothing orders the L114 store of one warp after the L104 loads of all other warps (the next __syncthreads is only after the store), e.g. warp 0 lane 0 stores shared[0] while warps 1.. still read shared[0].
fix_summary: Adds __syncthreads() before the threadIdx.x==0 store (and replaces / and % by shifts/masks).
evidence: Commit/PR title 'fix reduce_any kernel data race on sharedMem (#47233)' by Bo Zhang; no description beyond title and refactor bullets.
driver: paddle.any / paddle.sum / paddle.max with multi-axis reduction on GPU so that ReduceAnyKernel runs with blockDim.x>32, e.g. paddle.any(paddle.rand([64,256,64])>0.5, axis=[0,2]) -- shape/axis choice UNVERIFIED. Existing tests: python/paddle/fluid/tests/unittests/test_reduce_op.py.
build_notes: Building Paddle at cb746665 (Oct 2022, CUDA 11 era) on CUDA 13 is impractical; either try the paddlepaddle-gpu 2.4.x pip wheel (UNVERIFIED that it predates the fix) or extract BlockXReduce + WarpReduce into a .cu harness (needs CREATE_SHFL_MASK and CudaShuffleDownSync -> __shfl_down_sync) and launch with block (128..512, 1..4), 2*32 shared T.
dispute_points: Race exists for any blockDim.y>=1 given blockDim.x>32 (thread 0 stores shared[0] while others read it). The fix PR gives no evidence of observed wrong results.

location_buggy: paddle/phi/kernels/gpu/cumsum_kernel.cu:L35-L57 at 00ed8b57 (stores sh_mem[offset]=0 L44 vs sh_mem[BLOCK_SIZE-offset-1]=data L48)
race_description: For a tail block with valid_item < 1024, threads with offset>=valid_item store 0 to sh_mem[offset] while threads with offset'<valid_item store data to sh_mem[1023-offset']. For offset' < min(valid_item, 1024-valid_item) the two index sets collide (offset = 1023-offset'), so two different threads (different warps) write the same slot with no barrier before the later __syncthreads; the winner decides whether data or zero is read back.
fix_summary: Rewrites BlockReverse so each thread reads src[BLOCK_SIZE-offset-1] (if in range) and writes only sh_mem[offset]: one writer per slot.
evidence: Commit 'Fix the race condition in cumsum operator (#42205)' (Leo Chen) with an 'optimize cumsum' bullet; no repro text.
driver: cumsum with reverse=True along an axis whose length is not a multiple of 1024 and size != axis length (so the thrust fast path at L224 is skipped), e.g. x=paddle.rand([4,1500]); paddle.fluid.layers.cumsum(x,axis=1,reverse=True) or _C_ops.cumsum(x,'axis',1,'reverse',True); tests python/paddle/fluid/tests/unittests/test_cumsum_op.py (reverse cases). MatrixRowReverse is launched <<<grid,1024>>>.
build_notes: Extract MatrixRowReverse + BlockReverse (50 lines, no dependencies except T) into a .cu harness: launch <<<dim3(outer,inner),1024>>> with reverse_size in {100, 600, 1500}. Building Paddle is not needed.
dispute_points: None noteworthy; plain WAW on shared memory visible to any detector.

location_buggy: paddle/fluid/operators/math/segment_pooling.cu:L27-L94 at eca8dcc7 (summed_ids written via CudaAtomicAdd / plain store L58-L67, read L80/L82/L92 after __syncthreads L71)
race_description: Phase 1 (threads with segment_offset==0) accumulates per-segment counts into the global array summed_ids using atomicAdd and, for interior segments, plain stores. Phase 2 of the same kernel divides by *(summed_ids + segment). The only ordering is __syncthreads() inside a CUDA_KERNEL_LOOP, which orders only one block (and is illegal when threads run different trip counts); a segment that spans several stripes/blocks has its count completed by other blocks, so phase 2 can read an incomplete or half-written count.
fix_summary: Split into two kernels: SegmentSumIdsKernel (counts, now with sortedness check) then SegmentMeanKernel (division), relying on kernel boundary for ordering.
evidence: Commit title '[OPs] Bug fix, fix the segment mean for illegal syncthreads usage. (#32596)'; the removed code carried a comment that a check 'may cause cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources'.
driver: paddle.incubate.segment_mean(data, segment_ids) (sorted ids) on a tensor large enough for several blocks: DimTileSize=8 rows per stripe, one stripe per thread: e.g. data [8192,16], ids with few long segments => 16384 stripes -> many blocks. python/paddle/fluid/tests/unittests/test_segment_ops.py (unverified path).
build_notes: Extract the kernel as is (depends only on CUDA_KERNEL_LOOP, CudaAtomicAdd) and launch it with the same grid/block as SegmentPoolFunctor (blocks=ceil(stripes/1024) -- unverified).
dispute_points: Fix is a rewrite; maintainers' wording is about 'illegal __syncthreads usage' (barrier inside a grid-stride loop) rather than a demonstrated data race, so the cross-block RAW is my reading of the code. A skeptic would say the race is only reachable when a segment spans blocks.

location_buggy: paddle/phi/kernels/funcs/layer_norm_impl.cu.h:L192-L330 at abf05e11 (smem[warp_m]=mu_local L271 vs row-mates reading smem[warp_m*WARPS_N+it] L269; var path L299 write vs L274 read, L308/L306)
race_description: Two bugs in the WARPS_N>1 cross-warp reduction (feature_size 2048: WARPS_M=2,WARPS_N=2; 4096: 2x... WARPS_N=4): (a) the reduced mean/variance is stored at smem[warp_m] but the partials live at smem[warp_m*WARPS_N + warp_n], so row 1's result slot aliases row 0's partial slot and is written while row 0's reducer still reads it; (b) after reading mu_local = smem[...] (L274) the variance partials are stored to smem[warp_m*WARPS_N+warp_n] (L299) with no barrier in between, overwriting what other warps are still reading.
fix_summary: Result slot changed to smem[warp_m*WARPS_N]; extra __syncthreads() before the variance partial store; also re-enables the fast kernel (can_call_fast_kernel=true) which had been force-disabled.
evidence: Commit title 'bugfix, read and write race at fast_ln_fwd (#56435)' (Jeng Bai-Cheng); at the buggy parent the dispatcher hard-codes can_call_fast_kernel=false, i.e. the kernel was switched off (reason not stated; unverified that this race was why).
driver: At the fix commit: paddle.nn.functional.layer_norm on CUDA with feature size 2048 or 4096 and scale+bias given (e.g. x=[256,2048]). At the buggy commit the kernel is unreachable (flag false) -- flip the flag at layer_norm_kernel.cu:L609 or call the kernel directly. Launch grid=ceil(rows/ROWS_PER_CTA), THREADS_PER_CTA=128.
build_notes: Kernel is a self-contained template using phi::AlignedVector / phi::Load; extract L192-L340 plus aligned_vector.h into a harness (~200 lines) and instantiate fast_ln_fwd_kernel<float,float,float,4,2,2,16,2048>. Paddle build not needed.
dispute_points: Kernel was disabled in dispatch at the buggy commit, so no user could hit it; a skeptic would call it dead code. Fix mixes index fix and sync. Template args for the 2048 instantiation derived from the launch macro by reading (WARPS_N=feature_size/1024, WARPS_M=4/WARPS_N) -- not compiled.

kernel: KernelRS<BatchType> -> Warp_radiusSearch::processLeaf (+ TestWarpKernel / scan_warp on storage.cta_buffer)
location_buggy: gpu/octree/src/cuda/radius_search.cu:L218-L262 at 3cb0cf4a (per-warp broadcasts via `storage.per_warp_buffer[warpId]` at L232-L251, IndividualRadius::bradcastRadius2 at L99-L104; smem declared `volatile int per_warp_buffer[16]`, `volatile int cta_buffer[512]` at L121-L128)
race_description: Block of 512 threads (16 warps). Each warp broadcasts values from the 'active lane' to all lanes via a single shared word: `if (active_lane==laneId) per_warp_buffer[warpId] = X; int v = per_warp_buffer[warpId];` repeated for found_count, begs, ends, query_index, query.x/y/z and radius^2, only protected by `volatile` - no __syncwarp. The write is in a divergent branch, so under independent thread scheduling the other lanes' reads can run before the writing lane stores (RAW), and the next broadcast's store can overwrite the word before slow lanes read the previous value (WAR).
fix_summary: All volatile per-warp smem broadcasts are replaced by __shfl_sync(0xFFFFFFFF, v, active_lane); IndividualRadius/SharedRadius::bradcastRadius2 removed, radius^2 broadcast with shfl too.
evidence: PR #4146 '[gpu] Fix octree radiusSearch' fixes issue #3583: 'Inaccurate results' - GPU radius search returned 'an irregular block of points', reported on Quadro T2000 (Turing) with CUDA 10.2 and Jetson TX2; CPU search correct. Commit message: replace read/writes to volatile storage by __shfl primitives. The PR text does not use the words 'race' or 'ITS' (cause inferred from the diff).
driver: PCL GPU test test/gpu/octree/test_radius_search.cpp (TEST(PCL_OctreeGPU, batchRadiusSearch), calls octree_device.radiusSearch with shared radius, per-query radiuses, and indices; defaults 871000 points x 10000 queries - reduce data_size to ~2e4 and tests_num to ~512 in DataGenerator) or example gpu/examples/octree/src/octree_search.cpp.
build_notes: Buggy source is Aug 2020 PCL 1.11-dev: cmake -DBUILD_GPU=ON -DBUILD_gpu_octree=ON -DBUILD_tests_gpu_octree... (needs Boost, Eigen, FLANN; PCL common/search/octree/io), legacy FindCUDA (CMake >=3.27 needs policy CMP0146 OLD or CMake<=3.30); nvcc 13 has dropped sm_<75 so set CUDA arch list manually in cmake/pcl_find_cuda.cmake. Cheaper: standalone nvcc test compiling gpu/octree/src/cuda/{octree_builder,radius_search}.cu + octree.cpp with pcl_common headers only.
dispute_points: All communication is inside one warp, so on pre-Volta GPUs the volatile idiom works; the bug appears only with Volta+ ITS (issue reporter has Turing). Maintainers' diagnosis in the PR is 'inconsistent/incorrect output for multiple radiuses' and the cause is not spelled out as ITS; confirm that the shfl rewrite is what fixed #3583 (the PR has 6 commits squashed into one).

location_buggy: gpu/octree/src/cuda/knn_search.cu:L165-L222 (processLeaf: volatile per_warp_buffer broadcasts L172-L210) and L224-L305 (NearestWarpKernel: volatile dist2/index arrays, warp reduction lane<16,8,4,2,1 at L253-L300) at 0de7b335 (first parent of merge c0c0cb258)
race_description: Same idiom as pcl-1 in the exact-KNN kernel. (a) per-warp broadcasts through the volatile word per_warp_buffer[warpId] written by one lane inside an if and read by all lanes; (b) NearestWarpKernel does a classic warp-synchronous reduction on __shared__ volatile float dist2[512]/int index[512]: lanes <16 read dist2[tid+16] written by lanes 16-31, then <8, <4, <2, <1, with no __syncwarp between steps, and finally every lane reads index[tid-lane] written by lane 0. Valid only under lock-step; racy on Volta+.
fix_summary: processLeaf broadcasts replaced by __shfl_sync; NearestWarpKernel keeps dist2/index in registers and reduces with __shfl_down_sync, then __shfl_sync from lane 0; no shared memory left.
evidence: PR #4306 '[gpu] Replace volatile shared memory with shfl_sync in KNNSearch': body says 'Fix for distance calculation issue caused by the use of volatile shared memory in GPU K nearest neighbour search'.
driver: test/gpu/octree/test_knn_search.cpp TEST(PCL_OctreeGPU, exactNeighbourSearch) (871000 points, 10000 queries by default; shrink DataGenerator.data_size/tests_num for the detector) - launches KernelKNN.
build_notes: Same module and build as pcl-1 (gpu_octree). One build of PCL commit 84f694372b507e970f8447a84e6f2d787bea9d14 (2020-08-05, base of PRs 4306/4294/4146) contains the volatile/warp-synchronous code of all three kernels (pcl-1, pcl-2, pcl-3).
dispute_points: Intra-warp only; cause ('distance calculation issue caused by volatile shared memory') is stated by the author. Commit 49b80de6 is not itself linked to an issue number. Merge commit is first-parent diff 0de7b335..c0c0cb258 which also contains const/refactor hunks.

location_buggy: gpu/octree/src/cuda/approx_nsearch.cu:L116-L163 (processNode: volatile per_warp_buffer broadcasts L118-L156) and L165-L245 (NearestWarpKernel: volatile dist2/index and lane<16..1 reduction L194-L242, return index[tid-lane] L244) at ec979e84
race_description: Identical to pcl-2 but in the approximate-nearest-neighbour kernel: volatile shared broadcast word per warp and volatile dist2/index warp reduction with no __syncwarp, relying on lock-step execution of the warp.
fix_summary: Volatile smem broadcasts replaced with __shfl_sync and the min-reduction with __shfl_down_sync / __shfl_sync (commit 'Replace read/writes to volatile storage by __shfl primitives').
evidence: Commit bb49225a (in PR #4294 'Add new traversal mechanism for gpuApproxNearestSearch & modify tests', merged 2020-08-19 as ca5f8320c): replaces volatile storage reads/writes by shfl primitives, same author/pattern as PR #4306 and #4146.
driver: test/gpu/octree/test_approx_nearest.cpp TEST(PCL_OctreeGPU, approxNearesSearch) via pcl::gpu::Octree::approxNearestSearch.
build_notes: As pcl-1. Buggy commit ec979e84 is a PR-branch commit (reachable from master through merge ca5f8320c, whose first parent is 60a50bc92 which also has the volatile code but the older traversal).
dispute_points: The commit message gives no bug report; it is a modernization in a PR focused on a new traversal. Weaker evidence than pcl-1/pcl-2, but the code pattern is identical.

location_buggy: fbgemm_gpu/src/jagged_tensor_ops/jagged_index_select_2d_forward.cu:L26 (__shared__ int smem[1]), L32-L36 (thread 0 binary_search_range(smem, ...) writes smem[0]), L37 __syncthreads, L41 (all threads read smem[0]) inside the grid-stride loop L27-L55 at buggy_commit
race_description: Each iteration of the grid-stride loop has thread 0 write the row index into the one-element shared array smem, a barrier, then every thread reads smem[0] (L41) and goes on to copy a row of num_cols values. There is no barrier at the end of the iteration, so in iteration k+1 thread 0 can overwrite smem[0] (L35) while threads of other warps are still reading the value written in iteration k (or are before their read of it). Different threads, same shared word, unordered (WAR, and also a RAW against the stale value).
fix_summary: Thread 0 first computes the search result into a register (local_index_pos), then the block does __syncthreads() (all reads of the previous iteration finished), thread 0 stores smem[0], and a second __syncthreads() publishes it. binary_search_range now writes to the register instead of smem.
evidence: Commit message (Arbaz Khan, 2026-01-05): fixes a memory violation crash; 'shared memory was being overwritten in the next iteration before all threads in a block had finished reading'. No benchmark impact. No racecheck output quoted.
driver: torch.ops.fbgemm.jagged_index_select(values[R, C], lengths, indices) with C>=64 columns (launch uses blockDim=num_cols, so C=256 gives 8 warps) and more selected rows than blocks (grid is min(1024, num_dense_output_rows), so >1024 output rows are needed for a second loop iteration); e.g. values 4096x256 float, 2048 indices, ~1e6 element copies.
build_notes: Kernel uses at::PackedTensorAccessor wrappers and FBGEMM launch macros, so extraction is awkward. Easiest route: pip install torch plus a fbgemm-gpu wheel released before 2026-01-05 (version of the wheel containing the buggy file is unverified) and run the op from Python; the detector works on the shipped SASS. Alternatively build fbgemm_gpu at buggy_commit (CUDA build only, sm_89) which takes tens of minutes.
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream).
dispute_points: Needs num_dense_output_rows > gridDim.x (i.e. >1024 here) to execute a second loop iteration; Meta's internal debug diff D90010554 is not public. The grid is also launched with dim3(num_cols) threads even though num_threads is computed, which limits C to <=1024. Racecheck should show a WAR on smem between thread 0 and other warps.

location_buggy: caffe2/operators/elementwise_linear_op.cu:L22-L46 at ef2701a5 (two back-to-back cub::BlockReduce::Sum calls on one __shared__ TempStorage, L39-L40)
race_description: Two cub::BlockReduce<float,512>(temp_storage).Sum() calls reuse the same TempStorage with no barrier between them. The second call's warp-aggregate stores into temp_storage can overwrite data that threads of other warps are still reading in the first Sum (thread 0 reads the per-warp aggregates after the first barrier inside CUB), a WAR hazard documented by CUB.
fix_summary: Inserted __syncthreads() between the two Sum calls.
evidence: Commit message (Aapo Kyrola, via Facebook diff D4949250): 'if a CUB tempstorage is reused, a thread sync is needed. So added this to the elementwise linear gradient kernel.' No sanitizer output.
driver: Extract the kernel (cub only) and launch <<<D, 512>>> with N>=512, e.g. N=2048, D=16. Or caffe2 op ElementwiseLinearGradient on GPU (old caffe2 build, not recommended). <10^6 accesses.
build_notes: Standalone .cu: copy lines 22-46 + includes cub/block/block_reduce.cuh (modern CUDA ships CUB in CCCL); replace CAFFE_CUDA_NUM_THREADS with 512 (caffe2/core/common_gpu.h:228 at that commit). Compile for sm_89.
dispute_points: The hazard lives inside CUB's implementation; a detector that excludes library headers or whitelists CUB would miss it (and modern CUB may have additional internal barriers). Very old (2017) code, caffe2 is removed from the tree.

location_buggy: aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Reduce.cuh at f8d379d2: run() L402-L421; block_y_reduce L669-L685 (read shared[config.shared_memory_offset(offset)] L676); block_x_reduce L635-L666 (first write shared[address_base]=value L641)
race_description: When a reduction needs both block_y_reduce and block_x_reduce, both use the same dynamic shared buffer. The last iteration of block_y_reduce (offset==1) has threads with threadIdx.y==0 read shared[(0+1)*blockDim.x+x], while block_x_reduce immediately starts with every thread storing shared[x + y*blockDim.x]; thread (x,1) writes exactly the slot thread (x,0) is reading. No barrier between the two calls (the x-reduce barrier only comes after its first store). Needs blockDim.x>warpSize and blockDim.y>=2.
fix_summary: Adds a single __syncthreads() between the block_y_reduce and block_x_reduce calls in ReduceOp::run.
evidence: Author (Eddie Yan) says it was reported by compute-sanitizer racecheck: block_y_reduce and block_x_reduce both use shared_memory for temporaries without synchronization between them. Quoted repro: compute-sanitizer --tool=racecheck python test/test_matmul_cuda.py -k test_scaled_mm_vs_emulated_block_wise_float32_lhs_block_128_rhs_block_1_cuda (needs H100 for the non-emulated half).
driver: Any plain torch reduction whose ReduceConfig has input_mult[BLOCK_X]!=0 and input_mult[BLOCK_Y]!=0 with block (>32, >=2). By reading setReduceConfig a candidate is torch.randn(2,65536,device='cuda').sum(dim=1) (block ~ (256,2), values_per_thread>=warp_split_threshold) -- UNVERIFIED shape, derived by reading code; confirm with compute-sanitizer racecheck or by printing the config. ~1.3e5 elements => well under 10^7 accesses.
build_notes: Fix is in v2.10.0; every release <= v2.9.1 contains the bug, so pip install torch==2.9.1 (or 2.8.0) is enough. The kernel is header-only templated (Reduce.cuh needs TensorIterator), so extracting it is NOT recommended; use the wheel.
dispute_points: Race window is a single smem slot-set; no reported wrong result. The sanitizer report is from an emulated scaled-mm test, the simple sum() driver is my inference.

location_buggy: aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Sorting.cu:L181 (valuesSliceStart[0]=median, all threads) and L184-L190 (indicesSliceStart[0]=i by every matching thread) at 7b2fe038
race_description: Same structure as gatherKthValue: every thread finds the first index equal to the median in its strided subset and writes indicesSliceStart[0] (and all threads store valuesSliceStart[0]=median) without ordering; with ties several threads write one global word.
fix_summary: atomicMin on a shared 64-bit index, barrier, thread 0 writes; removes nondeterminism alert; new test test_median_dim_index_is_first_occurrence.
evidence: Commit message: gatherMedian lets every thread that finds a value equal to the median write its index to the same output, so median(dim) returns whichever index lands last; the same race was fixed for gatherKthValue in #165762. Validated on ROCm MI355X only.
driver: torch.zeros(4,2048,device='cuda').median(dim=1) / nanmedian(dim=1) (ties everywhere); or test/test_reductions.py -k test_median_dim_index_is_first_occurrence (added by the fix). 1 block per slice.
build_notes: No release contains the fix (<= v2.14.1 all buggy): pip install torch.
dispute_points: Same 'benign nondeterminism' objection as pytorch-4; fix is two days old at time of writing.

location_buggy: aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Reduce.cuh at c0b87afc: global_reduce L783-L850: staging store reduce_buffer[offset]=value L802, release __threadfence L805, mark_block_finished (atomicAdd on semaphores) L807, then last block reads reduce_buffer[idx] L816/L827 without an acquire fence
race_description: Each CTA stores its partial result to reduce_buffer, executes __threadfence() and atomically increments a semaphore. The last CTA to arrive then reads all partials from reduce_buffer. The producer side had the fence; the consumer (last block) lacked the acquire-side fence after the atomic, so under the PTX memory model the reads are not ordered after the other CTAs' writes.
fix_summary: Adds __threadfence() right after is_last_block_done is observed true (also in the JIT copy reduction_template.cuh).
evidence: Commit message by Natalia Gimelshein: the final block must complete the acquire pattern after the atomic so that writes of other blocks are visible; links the PTX release/acquire docs. No failing test is reported.
driver: Any global (cross-CTA) reduction: e.g. torch.randn(1<<22,device='cuda').sum() or x.sum(dim=0) on a tall-skinny tensor so config.ctas_per_output>1 (setReduceConfig input_mult[CTA]!=0). ~4M element reads => ~5x10^6 accesses, OK.
build_notes: Fix first in v2.5.0; pip install torch==2.4.1 (or earlier) has the bug.
dispute_points: STRONGEST skeptic point: on real hardware the code works (the classic CUDA threadFenceReduction sample has the same shape); the race is only formal (PTX memory model). A detector that does not model acquire fences on the consumer side will not report it; one that requires fence+atomic+fence will. Rank by the detector's memory-model fidelity. Also, whether the detector treats atomicAdd+__threadfence on the producer side as release is what makes the 'before' version 'half-synchronized'.

location_buggy: kernel_backward.h at 9dc77392: after mma() calls at ~L1592-1600 (Q*K^T), L1846-1850 (gradV), L1902-1906 (gradQ), L2094-2098, L2232-2236 (gradK); each was followed by nothing or a plain __syncthreads() that does not wait for outstanding cp.async
race_description: Every sm80+ multistage GEMM in the backward ends its mainloop on cp_async_wait<stages-1>, leaving the last cp.async group (often zfill) in flight. Code that follows writes to shared memory that aliases the pending copies' destination before anything waits (__syncthreads does not wait for cp.async), so late-landing async writes can clobber or be clobbered.
fix_summary: Adds drain_cp_asyncs() (cp_async_fence; cp_async_wait<0>; __syncthreads) and calls it after the Q*K^T GEMM and in place of the __syncthreads after the other four GEMMs; no-op for CustomMmaPipelined.
evidence: Commit includes compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck --racecheck-detect-level info results on H100: e.g. f16 m=129 k=512: 10 errors before, 0 hazards after; f16 m=129 k=128: 4 errors; m=256 k=128: 2 errors; head_dim 64: 0. Author could not see wrong results.
driver: q,k,v=torch.randn(1,8,129,512, fp16, requires_grad) under sdpa_kernel(SDPBackend.EFFICIENT_ATTENTION); F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q,k,v).sum().backward() (script quoted in the commit). Smaller: head_dim 128, seq 129/256 also report (2-4 errors); try B=1,H=1 to keep thread accesses <10^8. Needs sm80+ (sm_89 ok).
build_notes: No release contains the fix, so pip install torch (>=2.4, CUDA 12.x/13) ships the buggy fmha_cutlassB kernels. The kernel is CUTLASS-templated: do not try to extract.
dispute_points: Author could not observe wrong results on H100; hazard exists only via cp.async zfill semantics. Detector must model cp.async (LDGSTS) completion; if it only understands plain ld/st it will miss it.

kernel: blockReduce<Reduction,AccumT> (device fn used by cunn_SoftMaxForward / cunn_SoftMaxBackward)
location_buggy: aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/SoftMax.cu:L317-L359 at 3c69c9a7 (reads smem[lane*32+i] L338 vs write smem[lane]=warpVal L340)
race_description: In the second phase of blockReduce the first warp's lanes (lane < blockDim.x/32) each read 32 entries smem[lane*32 + i], i=0..31, and then write smem[lane]. Lane 0 reads smem[1..31], which are exactly the slots lanes 1..31 write. This only works if the lanes execute the loop in lock-step; on Volta+ (independent thread scheduling) lane j can reach its store before lane 0 reads smem[j], and the branch is divergent when blockDim.x/32 < 32.
fix_summary: Adds __syncwarp(mask) (mask=(1<<(blockDim.x/32))-1, guarded by CUDA_VERSION>=9000) between the read loop and the store.
evidence: Commit message in full: 'fix WAR race ... was flagged by racecheck.' (Natalia Gimelshein, PR #20182).
driver: F.softmax(torch.randn(8,4096,device='cuda'),dim=1) (block-softmax path, blockDim>=64) in the 2019 code; any size where SoftMax_getBlockSize gives >=2 warps. In a standalone harness: kernel with extern __shared__ AccumT smem[], call blockReduce<Add,float>(smem, val, Add<float>(), 0) with 64..1024 threads; <10^5 accesses.
build_notes: Buggy tree is May 2019 PyTorch (needs CUDA 9/10 era toolchain) so do NOT build it; extract blockReduce verbatim (30 lines, only needs smem pointer + functor) into a .cu harness and compile for sm_89 (device code generated then has ITS semantics). Fix is in v1.2.0.

location_buggy: src/QMCWaveFunctions/detail/CUDA/cuBLAS_LU.cu:L81-L85 (`if (threadIdx.x == 0 && block_num == 0) { logdets[iw].x = 0.0; logdets[iw].y = 0.0; }`), L99-L100 (`atomicAdd((double*)&(logdets[iw].x), block_sum_log_det.x)` and .y by thread 0 of every column block), grid dim3(batch_size, num_col_blocks) L126 at buggy_commit
race_description: The kernel accumulates the per-walker log-determinant with atomicAdd from every column block (blockIdx.y = 0..num_col_blocks-1) into logdets[iw]. To initialise the accumulator, thread 0 of block blockIdx.y == 0 first stores 0.0 into logdets[iw] with a plain store. Blocks with blockIdx.y >= 1 can run their atomicAdd before block 0 has executed the zeroing store (no inter-block ordering), so their contribution is overwritten: plain write versus atomic add from different blocks. Happens only when n > 256 (more than one column block).
fix_summary: Removes the in-kernel zeroing and instead zero-fills logdets on the host side before the launch (CUDAfill_n(logdets, batch_size, {0.0, 0.0})); documents that logdets must be zeroed on launch; also adjusts the unit test.
evidence: Commit message 'fix possible race condition in logdet kernel' (Peter Doak, 2021-04-08). Diff matches the description above.
driver: Existing unit test test_cuBLAS_LU.cpp uses n=4 (a single column block), so it does NOT expose the race. Use a small harness: n=600 or 1024 (3-4 column blocks), lda=n, batch_size=2-4, LU matrices with nonzero diagonal, pivots array, launch cuBLAS_LU::computeLogDet_batched / the kernel directly; under 1e6 accesses.
build_notes: Kernel needs complexDetLog() from the same file (L40-L56) and cuDoubleComplex; extract computeLogDet_kernel + complexDetLog into a standalone .cu (nvcc -arch=sm_89). Full QMCPACK build (MPI/HDF5/Boost) not required.
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream).
dispute_points: The race is a cross-block ordering problem: it only changes the result when a later block's atomicAdd lands before block 0's zeroing store, which is rare in practice (block 0 is normally scheduled first). A detector that flags plain-store vs atomic from different blocks will report it regardless of timing. Default branch is 'develop'.

location_buggy: cpp/src/io/parquet/page_hdr.cu:L535-L650 (decode kernel: loop condition reads bs->cur/bs->end L579, leader-only invoke_one body L582-L643 writes bs->cur via parse_page_header_fn L595/L627/L640 and bs->page.* L583-L593), L659-L735 (count kernel: same shape L694-L729) at buggy_commit
race_description: Each warp parses Parquet page headers for one column chunk, keeping the parse cursor and page struct in shared memory (bs->cur, bs->end, bs->page). There is no warp.sync between the lanes' condition reads and the leader's writes, so under independent thread scheduling the leader can write while another lane still reads (intra-warp WAR); in addition the elected lane is not guaranteed to be lane 0, which the following shuffle(values_found) assumes as root.

The reader/writer pairs are in one warp, so in practice the lanes are converged at the loop head and the hazard is formal under the CUDA memory model rather than a reproducible wrong result (the PR does not say whether it produced wrong output). race_description: Each loop iteration declares/uses one __shared__ cub::BlockScan<int,decode_block_size>::TempStorage and calls ExclusiveSum on it. CUB requires a barrier between the last read of a collective's TempStorage and its next use, but there is none between iterations (nor between depth iterations in the nested variant), so a warp racing into iteration N+1 starts writing scan_storage while slower warps are still reading the iteration-N scan results from the same bytes.
fix_summary: Adds __syncthreads() at the end of each loop iteration (flat, nonlist, and the depth loop of nested) before scan_storage is reused.
evidence: PR 24249 (author Vyas Ramasubramani): 'observed this issue locally while working on the Parquet kernels'; says it is a race and there is no test that reliably reproduces it. No sanitizer log quoted.
driver: libcudf PARQUET_TEST (cpp/tests/io/parquet_reader_test.cpp etc.): any read of a fixed-width column page with nulls/nesting; decode_block_size 128 (verify). Run PARQUET_TEST under the detector with a handful of small files.
build_notes: libcudf full build + PARQUET_TEST (hours). Only decode_fixed.cu differs between parent and fix. Same suite is shared with cudf-3..cudf-6 so one build covers all cudf candidates (build parent of the oldest fix needed, then apply fixes one by one: all are in different kernels).
dispute_points: No reproducer; maintainer-observed locally. Standard CUB rule (barrier before temp storage reuse) makes this an unambiguous race by contract.

location_buggy: cpp/src/io/orc/dict_enc.cu at 73423f81: LoadNonNullIndices L69-L110: 'if (t == 0) { s->nnz = 0; }' L74, loop 'for (i = 0; i < s->chunk.num_rows; ...)' L75 containing the __syncthreads calls; caller reads 'nnz = s->nnz' at L168 in every thread
race_description: Thread 0 initialises the shared dictionary-builder field s->nnz = 0; every barrier that publishes it lives inside the loop over s->chunk.num_rows. When the leaf column of the chunk has zero rows (e.g. a LIST<STRING> column whose lists are all empty) the loop body never runs, so no barrier separates thread 0's store from the other threads' read 'nnz = s->nnz' in the caller. Other warps can read the uninitialised shared value, take the non-empty branch and touch unallocated temp memory (the reporter saw crashes).
fix_summary: If s->chunk.num_rows <= 0, execute a __syncthreads() after the thread-0 store so the loop-less path also publishes s->nnz.
evidence: PR 13214 (Robert Evans): a race on nnz in dictionary creation for ORC strings, hard to reproduce (needs a LIST<STRING> column with only empty lists plus a STRUCT of empty strings, >=140001 rows, T4); nnz set to 0 by thread 0 may not show up in all threads when the loop is not taken. No unit test was added.
driver: libcudf ORC writer on a table with a LIST<STRING> column of only empty lists (so the leaf has zero rows) plus a STRING column, dictionary encoding enabled; e.g. ORC_TEST-style small write. The race window exists for any chunk with num_rows == 0 regardless of row count (the 140001-row figure only made the crash reproducible). Exact gtest unverified.

kernel: gpuDecodeStream<level_t,rolling_buf_size> (warp-level RLE level decoder used by the Parquet page decode kernels)
location_buggy: cpp/src/io/parquet/page_decode.cuh at 39386c27: reads of s->lvl_start[lvl], s->initial_rle_run[lvl], s->initial_rle_value[lvl], s->lvl_count[lvl] by all lanes at function entry (L476-L483) vs 'update the stream info' block 'if (!t) { s->lvl_start[lvl] = ...; s->lvl_count[lvl] = value_count; }' (L553-L559) with no __syncwarp
race_description: Every lane of warp 0 loads the shared page-state fields describing the level stream at the top of gpuDecodeStream. At the end lane 0 writes the updated stream position/run/value/count back to the same fields. If the while loop runs zero or few iterations, lane 0 reaches the write-back while other lanes may not yet have executed their initial reads (and they are not synchronised after the loop), a WAR hazard between lanes of one warp.
fix_summary: Insert __syncwarp() between the decode loop and the lane-0 write-back (comment: 'racecheck reported race between reads at the start of this function and the writes below', issue 14597). The same commit adds other small guards (__syncwarp in delta_binary_decoder before current_value_idx++, t==0 guards for s->page.num_valids/num_nulls writes in page_bounds, an early exit in gpuUpdateValidityOffsetsAndRowIndices) and comment-only notes about racecheck RAW warnings on s->dict_pos that the authors judge false positives.
evidence: PR 14602 (Ed Seidl, Vukasin Milovanovic): 'Address potential race conditions in Parquet reader', related to issue 14597, fixes errors reported by racecheck; code comment cites issue 14597 for gpuDecodeStream.
driver: Any Parquet read with definition/repetition levels reaches gpuDecodeStream (PARQUET_TEST ParquetReaderTest.*, small files).
build_notes: Full libcudf build + the named gtest binary (./build.sh libcudf tests, ninja <TEST>; CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89; deps rmm/cuco/CCCL/nvcomp via CPM; hours). The same build serves every cudf-* candidate: check out the parent of the oldest fix, then toggle individual fix commits (each touches a different file/kernel).
dispute_points: The PR title calls these 'potential' races; the hazard is intra-warp and thus a lockstep-assumption race. Exact racecheck output is in issue 14597, which I could not load. Several sibling changes in the same commit are judged false positives by the authors, so only the gpuDecodeStream part is claimed here.

location_buggy: cpp/src/io/parquet/page_delta_decode.cu at 9b39eb66: lane 0 'memcpy(prefix_seed,last_string,last_string_len); last_string=prefix_seed' at ~L216-L224 (two copies, hunks at old L214 and L279) racing with other lanes' reads of last_string; prefix_lens[] blocker loop at ~L117-L123 (read prefix_lens[blocker] vs write prefix_lens[lane_id]); delta_binary.cuh ~L314-L318 (lane 31 'last_value = delta' vs other lanes' earlier read of last_value)
race_description: Three warp-synchronous spots assume lock-step execution: (1) in calculate_string_values lane 0 overwrites the shared last_string pointer/length while other lanes may still be issuing reads of it; (2) in the blocker loop each lane reads prefix_lens[blocker] while lanes that have completed write prefix_lens[lane_id] in the same iteration; (3) in delta_binary_decoder lane 31 writes last_value after a loop with lane-dependent trip count, while other lanes may not yet have read last_value. Under ITS lanes can be at different points, so reads and writes of the same shared word are unordered.
fix_summary: Adds __syncwarp()/warp.sync() before the conflicting write: snapshot last_string and its length into locals then __syncwarp() before lane 0's memcpy; compute 'completed' flag, __syncwarp(), then update prefix_lens, __syncwarp(); warp.sync() before 'last_value = delta'.
evidence: PR 23898 from weekly compute-sanitizer CI: ParquetReaderTest.DeltaByteArrayLargeMiniBlockSkipRows, 'Race reported between Read access ... calculate_string_values ... page_delta_decode.cu:222 and Write access ... page_delta_decode.cu:225 [8 hazards]' and [16 hazards]; fix text: 'Adds appropriate sync-warp to prevent the race condition'. Line numbers in the quoted log belong to the CI build, not necessarily parent 9b39eb66.

build_notes: Same libcudf PARQUET_TEST build as cudf-1..3; parent vs fix differ only in page_delta_decode.cu and delta_binary.cuh.
dispute_points: Warnings (not Errors) in racecheck; since all accesses are within a warp the hazard only manifests under ITS divergence. Fix is not purely a sync (introduces snapshots), but only to make the sync meaningful.

location_buggy: cpp/src/traversal/sssp_kernels.cuh:L460-L462 + traversal::atomicMin(old_addr, new_val) at ~L477 at 9da9c210: threads atomicMin distances[dst_id] while other threads of the same launch read distances[src_id] (L462) / distances[dst_id] (L461) with plain loads
race_description: In one relax_edges launch each thread processes one frontier edge (src,dst): it reads distances[src_id] and distances[dst_id] with plain loads and then does atomicMin on distances[dst_id]. A vertex that is a destination of one frontier edge can be the source of another frontier edge in the same launch, so one thread's atomicMin on distances[v] races with another thread's plain read of distances[v]; the computed new_val (and the relaxed_edges bitmap that populate_frontier_and_preds later checks with 'expected_val == dst_val') depends on the order.
fix_summary: Double-buffers the distance array: relax_edges reads the stable distances[] and performs atomicMin on a new next_distances[]; the host copies next_distances to distances after the launch (cudaMemcpyAsync D2D), and populate_frontier_and_preds compares against next_distances.
evidence: Commit message is only 'Fix race in SSSP' (author Prasun, 2019-08-13). Diff introduces next_distances so reads and atomic updates hit different buffers. No sanitizer output. This is a chaotic-relaxation style race: results may still converge, so the maintainers' notion of 'race' = nondeterministic distance/predecessor outputs.
driver: cugraph cpp/src/tests/sssp/sssp_test.cu (at that revision; legacy nvgraph-era API gdf_error/ALLOC_TRY) on a small graph (e.g. 10^3-10^5 edges).
build_notes: Legacy cuGraph v0.10 code depends on cudf C API (gdf_column), RMM old ALLOC_TRY; the legacy traversal was removed (HEAD cpp/src/traversal has only bfs_impl etc.). Practical route: extract relax_edges + its helpers (traversal_common.cuh: binsearch_maxle, atomicMin for float) into a standalone harness with a synthetic CSR graph; kernel is block-size 256 (TOP_DOWN_EXPAND_DIMX), uses cub::BlockScan only in populate_frontier_and_preds.
dispute_points: Plain-read vs atomicMin on distances is the classic benign-by-design relaxation race in label-correcting algorithms; maintainers nonetheless treated it as a bug (probably due to inconsistent predecessor/expected_val comparison). Skeptic: it is not a memory-ordering bug but algorithmic non-determinism.

location_buggy: cpp/src_prims/linalg/block.cuh:L385-L407 at 1d57cac4 (tile loop: store gemv_storage.acc[threadIdx.x] at L394 in tile t+1 vs thread th_off_j==0 reads gemv_storage.acc[tj*ThRows+th_off_i] at L402 in tile t)
race_description: Per tile iteration all threads write their partial dot-product to gemv_storage.acc[threadIdx.x], __syncthreads, then the first thread of each row sequentially reads the ThCols partials. The loop has no trailing barrier, so the next iteration's write by other threads (acc[threadIdx.x]) can overwrite a partial that the reducing thread has not yet read (shared WAR, different warps for BlockSize > 32).
fix_summary: Adds __syncthreads() at the end of every tile iteration so all reductions finish before the shared accumulator buffer is overwritten.
evidence: PR 6578 description: the kernel writes shared memory with all threads, syncs, reduces in thread 0, then continues the loop; a sync was necessary so other threads do not overwrite shared memory while the reducer is still reading. No sanitizer output mentioned.

location_buggy: cpp/src_prims/common/device_utils.cuh:L79-L90 at 6d74f124 (store sTemp[wrIdx] at L83 in iteration k+1 vs load sTemp[rdIdx] at L88 in iteration k); test: cpp/test/prims/device_utils.cu (batchedBlockReduceTestKernel, <<<1, blkDim>>>)
race_description: The reduction loop writes per-warp partials to sTemp[wrIdx], does one __syncthreads, then threads read sTemp[rdIdx] and loop again to write the next level into the same buffer. There is no barrier after the read, so a fast warp starting the next iteration can overwrite sTemp entries that a slower warp has not yet read (needs >= 2 loop iterations, i.e. nGroups > nGroupsPerWarp, e.g. blkDim=512 with NThreads=8). The same missing trailing barrier also affects a following reuse of smem by the caller.

evidence: Commit message: 'fixed a syncthreads race issue in batchedBlockReduce' (author Thejaswi Rao, one day after the function started being used by the eps-neighborhood kernel). No PR number in the message; commit is on the default history (ancestor of cuml HEAD). No sanitizer output quoted.

location_buggy: cpp/src/hdbscan/detail/kernels/condense.cuh:L90-L127 at f09341a5: frontier[node]=false (L94, own thread) and read of frontier[node] (L92) vs frontier[left_child]=true / frontier[right_child]=true (L117-L118, parent's thread); also ignore[left_child]/relabel[left_child] written by parent thread (L121-L125) and read by the child's thread (L96,L127). select.cuh kernel: frontier[cluster]=false (L44) vs frontier[child]=true (L50)
race_description: One thread is launched per node of the binary dendrogram and all threads run in the same kernel launch (BFS level). Thread of node N reads frontier[N] and then clears it, while the thread of N's parent sets frontier[N]=true (and writes ignore[N]/relabel[N]) in the same launch with no ordering between them. Depending on schedule the child either is processed in the same iteration (reading half-updated ignore/relabel) or has its 'true' erased by its own 'frontier[node]=false' (lost update), so the child is never visited. Plain stores, no atomics, no fence, no kernel boundary between parent write and child read.
fix_summary: Writes children into a separate next_frontier array inside the kernel, and copies/clears it between kernel launches (thrust::copy next_frontier->frontier, thrust::fill next_frontier=false); same change in select.cuh propagate_cluster_negation_kernel. Author notes an earlier __threadfence-based attempt was dropped as not correct.
evidence: PR 4024 'HDBSCAN bug on A100': author explains the kernel launches a thread per tree node; a node's thread may mark itself out of the frontier while its parent's thread marks it in - undefined behaviour; appeared on A100 only but could appear on any GPU. No racecheck output.
driver: cuML cpp/test/sg/hdbscan_test.cu: ClusterCondensingTest (calls build_condensed_hierarchy on small hand-built dendrograms from hdbscan_inputs.hpp) and the HDBSCANTest end-to-end cases; tens to a few thousand nodes -> < 10^6 accesses.
build_notes: Fix parent f09341a5 is mid-2021 cuML (needs RMM 21.08-era API, thrust/cub of that time) - will not build on CUDA 13 without porting. Recommended: extract condense_hierarchy_kernel + get_lambda (condense.cuh, ~80 lines, no raft deps besides typedefs) and the 25-line BFS host loop from detail/condense.cuh into a standalone .cu with a hand-made binary dendrogram of e.g. 1000 leaves; or build only the C++ hdbscan test with an old container. Block-size 256 (tpb in host loop).
dispute_points: The race produces wrong clustering rarely (A100 only reproduction); some orderings are benign. A detector flagging parent/child frontier flag conflicts is the intended ground truth. The root cause is in the algorithm design (single array used as current and next frontier) rather than a missing barrier.

location_buggy: cpp/src/fil/infer.cu:L242-L252 at fed77b3e: per_thread[threadIdx.x]=acc L247; __syncthreads L248; multi_sum<6>(per_thread,...) L249 (reads data[idx] of other threads in its last iteration with no trailing barrier, multi_sum.cuh L38-L54, loop L40-L53, barrier only at L52 when n_values>1); then write_best_class_in_block L250 -> BlockReduceBestClass(tmp_storage).Reduce L210-L211 writes its TempStorage into the same shared buffer
