kernel: letsdoitall_kernel (decision-tree histogram kernel, launched from lets_doit_all)
location_buggy: cuML/src/decisiontree/kernels/evaluate.cuh:L209-L252 (init loops L216-L224: minmaxshared[i]=globalminmax[i] and shmemhist[i]=0, then L226-L243 main loop reads minmaxshared and atomicAdd(&shmemhist[..]) with no barrier in between; first barrier is L250) at buggy_commit; kernel launched at L384 with 512 threads/block, dynamic smem = 2*ncols*4 + nbins*n_unique_labels*ncols*4 bytes
race_description: Each block cooperatively initialises dynamic shared memory with strided loops: threads i < 2*ncols copy globalminmax into minmaxshared, and threads i < n_unique_labels*nbins*ncols zero shmemhist. The very next loop makes every thread read minmaxshared[mycolid] / minmaxshared[mycolid+ncols] and atomicAdd into shmemhist[...] with no __syncthreads in between. With 512 threads per block and only ~100 histogram words (e.g. 3 labels x 8 bins x 4 cols = 96), warps other than the first few reach the atomicAdds / reads while the initialising warps have not yet written, so (a) minmaxshared is read before it is written (RAW across warps) and (b) a late plain store of 0 to shmemhist races with another warp's atomicAdd (plain write vs atomic, WAW/lost update). The first barrier after the init is the one before the final flush, too late.
fix_summary: Insert a single __syncthreads() between the shared-memory initialisation loops and the main accumulation loop.
evidence: Commit message 'adding missing sync threads' (author Vishal Mehta, 2019-03-22), 3-line diff adding only __syncthreads(). No issue, no racecheck output; diagnosis is from reading the kernel.
driver: cuML/src/decisiontree/test.cu at the buggy commit: a main() that reads the 150x4 iris data.csv (cuML/src/decisiontree/data.csv), calls ML::DecisionTree::DecisionTreeClassifier::plant(d_data,4,150,d_labels,rowids,150,3,depth) which reaches lets_doit_all (tree.cuh L297) once per tree node; tiny (about 600 elements per kernel launch, 2 blocks of 512 threads). cuML/test/rf_test.cu (gtest, random forest) also reaches it.
build_notes: Whole libcuml at this 2019 commit will not build with CUDA 13. Either compile test.cu stand-alone with nvcc (needs cuML/src/common utils.h/ml-prims headers on the include path and probably small CUDA-13 fixes; exact include set unverified), or, simpler, extract allcolsampler_kernel + letsdoitall_kernel + atomic_minmax.h from evaluate.cuh into a 60-line .cu, fill the data with iris-like random floats, 3 labels, nbins=8, ncols=4, nrows=150, and launch with 512 threads and the dynamic smem size above. Run compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck on it; expect shared-memory hazards in letsdoitall_kernel (init loop vs main loop). Note allcolsampler_kernel in the same file also has a __syncthreads inside a grid-stride loop with a data-dependent trip count (barrier divergence; separate issue, not claimed).
dispute_points: Very old code (cuML 0.6 era layout 'cuML/src/decisiontree'), later replaced by a rewritten decision tree; the kernel no longer exists at cuml HEAD, so it can only be run from the checkout at the buggy commit or an extracted copy. The fix commit message is terse; the hazard is my reading of the diff context, but it is unambiguous: smem written by a subset of threads and consumed by all with no barrier.

location_buggy: cpp/src_prims/sparse/csr.cuh:L713-L759 (xa[j_ind]=cj_allow_prop L742, m[0]=cj_allow_prop L743, xa[global_id]=ci_allow_prop L754, m[0]=ci_allow_prop L755) at buggy_commit; launched in weak_cc_label_batched L811
race_description: In the weakly-connected-components label-propagation kernel (one thread per vertex) every thread that lowers a label stores a boolean into xa[neighbour] and into the single global flag m[0], where the stored value is the neighbour's/own filter result (cj_allow_prop / ci_allow_prop). Several threads can target the same xa[j_ind] (a shared neighbour) and all of them target m[0]; some write true and others false, so the final value depends on thread order and a true can be overwritten by a false (lost 'frontier/changed' flag), making DBSCAN stop propagating early. The accesses are plain stores with no atomic or ordering.
fix_summary: Store the constant true instead of the data-dependent boolean (xa[j_ind]=true; m[0]=true; xa[global_id]=true), with a todo noting an atomic logical-or could be used. The plain concurrent stores remain, but all write the same value, so the outcome is deterministic.
evidence: Commit message 'fixed race condition, added appropriate test' (Matthias Jouanneaux, 2020-05-22); the added test is python test_dbscan_propagation (5000-point blob, eps 0.5, min_samples 5, compares to sklearn). No racecheck output; no issue number found (unverified).
driver: C++ gtest cpp/test/prims/csr.cu (weak_cc_batched<int,32> on a 6-vertex graph, two batches; default always-true filter) is tiny but only exercises the same-value store; the regression test that exposes the wrong result is python/cuml/test/test_dbscan.py::test_dbscan_propagation (5000 points) which needs the full cuml python build. For a detector, the 6-vertex gtest suffices to see concurrent stores to m[0].
build_notes: csr.cuh is a header in the 2020 cuml tree (src_prims); the weak_cc_batched kernels depend on MLCommon cuda_utils/allocator headers. Easiest is a stand-alone .cu that includes the buggy csr.cuh with the cuml include paths (cpp/src_prims, cpp/include, cpp/src) and RMM/cub from the toolkit; building the full cpp/test/prims gtest binary at this commit with CUDA 13 is unlikely to work (unverified).
dispute_points: Weak oracle: the fixed version still has concurrent plain stores of the same value to m[0] and xa[] (and plain reads of labels[j_ind] against other threads' atomicMin), which a happens-before detector will also flag, so the detector cannot distinguish buggy from fixed by conflict alone; only the value-dependence (true vs false) differs. The false-overwrites-true outcome requires a non-trivial filter_op (DBSCAN with non-core neighbours). Whether the original author considered the m[0] flag race the root cause of the dbscan failure is not stated beyond the commit title.

kernel: cuvs::neighbors::ivf_rabitq::detail::blockReduceSum<float> as called 4x back-to-back from pack_and_compute_factors_kernel (and 2x/4x from other quantizer kernels)
location_buggy: cpp/src/neighbors/ivf_rabitq/utils/reductions.cuh:L30-L41 at e626144b (shared[wid]=val at L35 of call N+1 vs shared[lane] read at L38 of call N); callers cpp/src/neighbors/ivf_rabitq/gpu_index/quantizer_gpu.cu:L267-L270 (pack_and_compute_factors_kernel, 4 consecutive calls), L378, L405-L408; searcher_gpu_quantize_query.cu:L112-L113
race_description: blockReduceSum uses one static __shared__ T shared[32] per instantiation. Each call writes shared[wid] (lane 0 of every warp), does one __syncthreads, then warp 0 lanes read shared[lane]. The function has no trailing barrier, so in pack_and_compute_factors_kernel (256 threads = 8 warps, 4 consecutive blockReduceSum<float> calls) warp k>0 can leave call N, finish its warp-local reduction of call N+1 and overwrite shared[k] while warp 0 is still reading shared[k] of call N: write-after-read on the same shared address between different warps with no ordering.
fix_summary: Adds a __syncthreads() between the warp-local reduction and the shared[wid] store (i.e. at the start of the next call) so every warp has finished reading shared[] from the previous call before it is overwritten.
evidence: Commit title: 'Fix missing trailing barrier in ivf_rabitq blockReduceSum' (PR 2322). Added comment says to wait until every warp finished reading shared[] in the previous call. No racecheck output quoted in the commit (unverified whether the PR text contains any).
driver: cpp/tests/neighbors/ann_ivf_rabitq.cuh (cpp/tests/neighbors/ann_ivf_rabitq/test_float_int64_t.cu): ivf_rabitq::build() launches pack_and_compute_factors_kernel (grid=num_points, block=256) in the quantizer; any build with a few thousand rows is enough (~10^5-10^6 thread accesses).
build_notes: Needs a full cuVS C++ build (raft/rmm/cuco/CCCL via CPM, ivf_rabitq tests only: ./build.sh tests -n --limit-tests=NEIGHBORS_ANN_IVF_RABITQ_TEST or CMake equivalent) - one to a few hours. ivf_rabitq also has jit_lto_kernels but the racy kernels are in ordinary .cu files, not JIT. Alternative: extract reductions.cuh + a 20-line kernel that calls blockReduceSum<float> four times with 256 threads - this is the exact bug and compiles standalone with only cuda_runtime.h (raft::WarpSize is the only raft dependency, = 32).
dispute_points: None for the pattern itself (maintainer-approved fix). Practical manifestation is timing dependent; detector should report it regardless of observed result.

location_buggy: cpp/include/raft/spatial/knn/detail/fused_l2_knn.cuh at 372a9a54: shared-memory store allWarpTopKs[rowId*256+numValsWarpTopK[i]] = otherKV at L443 (inside divergent 'if (needScanSort[i] & (1<<lid))' L436-L448) vs reads allWarpTopKs[rowId*256+k] in updateSortedWarpQ L154 (called at L451-L452); only a raft::shfl (L449) sits between them
race_description: Within one warp, only the lanes selected by needScanSort write their candidate (key,value) pairs into the per-row shared array allWarpTopKs; afterwards every lane of the warp reads all finalNumVals entries (updateSortedWarpQ loop 'allWarpTopKs[rowId*256+k]'). Between the divergent writes and the reads there is a shuffle but no __syncwarp, so under independent thread scheduling a lane can read an entry before the writing lane has stored it.
fix_summary: Adds one __syncwarp() after the divergent store loop and before raft::shfl / loadWarpQShmem / updateSortedWarpQ.
evidence: Commit/PR text: fix for a race in the smem read/write 'reported by racecheck tool of compute-sanitizer', addresses issue 676. Issue page itself could not be fetched, so exact hazard report (type/addresses) is unverified; PR page confirmed via WebFetch (merged to branch-22.06 on 2022-05-25).
driver: RAFT cpp/test/spatial/fused_l2_knn.cu (FusedL2KNNTestF.FusedBruteForce); small params {100,1000,16,10,L2Expanded} or {256,256,30,10} suffice (use k>32 e.g. {100,1000,16,50} to exercise the multi-register warp queue).
build_notes: Build old RAFT (22.06 era, branch-22.06 parent 372a9a54) with CUDA 11/12 maybe needs patching (thrust/cub API, rmm); the same kernel now lives in cuVS (cuvs::neighbors::detail::fusedL2kNN / fused_l2_knn.cuh) where it can be built with current toolchains - check there whether the __syncwarp is present (unverified).
dispute_points: Some would argue __shfl_sync provides warp convergence so the race is a theoretical ITS-only race; however per CUDA docs only __syncwarp provides memory ordering and racecheck flagged it, so it is a legitimate report.

kernel: fusedL2kNN (rowEpilog_lambda producer/consumer buffer exchange between blocks)
location_buggy: cpp/include/raft/spatial/knn/detail/fused_l2_knn.cuh:L224-L346 at buggy_commit. Consumer (blockIdx.x==0): atomicCAS acquire L257, fence L259, __syncthreads L261, plain loads out_dists/out_inds L274-L275 by all threads, then thread 0 releases mutex[..]=0 at L283 (after per-thread __threadfence L280) with no __syncthreads in between. Producer (blockIdx.x!=0): acquire L323-L327, plain stores out_dists/out_inds L336-L337 by all threads, __threadfence L341, then thread 0 releases mutex[..]=-2 at L344 with no __syncthreads in between.
race_description: Row-tile results are handed between thread blocks through global out_dists/out_inds guarded by a per-tile spin mutex that only threadIdx.x==0 manipulates. In the producer, every thread stores its rows into out_dists/out_inds and calls __threadfence(), but there is no __syncthreads() before thread 0 sets mutex=-2, so thread 0 can publish the flag while other warps of the same block have not yet written their rows; block 0 then reads incomplete rows (RAW across blocks). Symmetrically, in the consumer thread 0 resets mutex=0 (letting the next producer overwrite the buffer) while other warps may still be reading it (WAR). The buffer accesses are also plain (non-volatile) loads/stores.
fix_summary: Make mutexes/out_dists/out_inds volatile; wrap acquire/release in atomicCAS/atomicExch executed by thread 0 followed by __threadfence() and add __syncthreads() before the thread-0 release in both producer and consumer; move the row guard into the loop. Also re-enables the fused L2 kNN path in knn_brute_force_faiss.cuh.
evidence: PR #429 (Mahesh Doijade, 2021-12-21): incorrect output in the producer-consumer code was detected by a cuml UMAP test on GV100; the stated cause is not using volatile and syncthreads. No racecheck output.
driver: gtest cpp/test/spatial/fused_l2_knn.cu (FusedL2KNNTestF/FusedBruteForce) at the buggy commit calls detail::fusedL2Knn directly (the public brute_force_knn path has fused kNN commented out there). Smallest parameters {100 queries, 1000 index rows, 16 dims, k=10} for both L2Expanded and L2Unexpanded; gridDim.x>1 needed, which 1000 index rows give. Roughly 1e6-1e7 thread accesses.
build_notes: Header-only RAFT at Dec 2021 plus deps: RMM, thrust/cub, FAISS GPU headers (Select.cuh, StandardGpuResources in the test), gtest. Easiest is the RAFT conda environment of the time; alternatively extract fusedL2kNN + faiss/gpu/utils/Select.cuh + raft pairwise_distance_base/contractions headers into a stand-alone .cu and drop the FAISS reference check (compare against a naive CPU kNN). CUDA 13 compatibility of the old FAISS/cub-era headers is unverified.
dispute_points: Racecheck/iGUARD must understand the fence+flag protocol: after the fix the hand-off is still plain stores ordered by fences/atomics, so a naive conflict detector will flag both versions; only a happens-before aware detector (fence+atomic synchronizes-with) separates them. The kernel is also data-dependent: blockIdx.x==0 is the consumer, so results are only racy when gridDim.x>1 and rows >= 2 warps per block write concurrently.

kernel: fps_kernel<scalar_t> (THREADS=256, one block per point cloud)
location_buggy: csrc/cuda/fps_cuda.cu:L27-L63 at 9c33077e (write out[m]=best_dist_idx[0] by thread 0 at L60-L62 vs read `old = out[m-1]` by every thread at L28 of the next iteration; no barrier between the end of iteration m-1 and the top of iteration m)
race_description: Farthest-point sampling loop. At the end of iteration m-1 only thread 0 publishes the newly selected point with `out[m] = best_dist_idx[0]` (global memory, after the block-wide reduction and its final __syncthreads). At the top of the next iteration every thread of the block immediately reads that global location (`int64_t old = out[m - 1]`) to compute distances to the newly selected point. Nothing orders thread 0's store before the other warps' loads, so a thread can read the stale / uninitialised out[m-1] (the buffer is torch::empty) and index src[dim*old+d] with garbage -> wrong selection or an out-of-range read.
fix_summary: One __syncthreads() inserted as the first statement of the m-loop body (3 lines changed incl. blank).
evidence: Commit message is only 'fix illegal memory access' (rusty1s, 2020-03-26, two days after 'fix fps implementation'); the diff consists solely of the added barrier. An illegal access is the observable consequence of reading a stale out[m-1]. No sanitizer output quoted. Barrier is still present at HEAD (fps_cuda.cu L28).
driver: torch_cluster.fps(x[N,3] float32 cuda, batch=None, ratio=0.5, random_start=False) -> fps_cuda; test/test_fps.py. Launches <<<batch_size,256>>>; e.g. N=2048, ratio 0.5 gives 1024 iterations x 8 points per thread x 3 dims ~ 3e7 accesses incl. reduction; use N<=1000 for a quick run.
build_notes: Kernel is self-contained apart from CHECK_CUDA macros: extract fps_kernel (L9-L64) into a ~50-line .cu with host-side setup: ptr={0,N}, out_ptr={0,N/2}, start={0}, dist filled with 1e38, out allocated with cudaMalloc WITHOUT memset (uninitialised, as torch::empty). Launch <<<1,256>>>. Release tags (git tag --contains on the fix): the fix is first in tag 1.5.4, so tag 1.5.3 or earlier is the buggy version; source build against torch/CUDA 13 would be needed, so the standalone harness is preferred.
dispute_points: The race is on one global word that thread 0 wrote just after a barrier; on real hardware the other warps almost always see it because they are ordered by the final __syncthreads at L59 + global memory write visibility within a block, but only if the store becomes visible before the loads, which is not guaranteed without a barrier AFTER the write (the write is after the barrier). A detector built on happens-before will report it; the maintainer saw 'illegal memory access' in practice which supports a real manifestation.

location_buggy: sgl-kernel/csrc/gemm/per_token_quant_fp8.cu:L49-L57 at 250477d2 (`__shared__ float scale; scale = warp_max / FP8_E4M3_MAX;` L51-L52, read at L55 and L57 `scale_inv = (scale == 0.f) ? 0.f : 1.0f / scale`)
race_description: The kernel assigns one token to each of 8 warps in a 256-thread CTA, but declares a single block-wide `__shared__ float scale`. After its warp reduction every warp stores its own token's scale into this one word and then reads it back (token_scale[0] = scale; scale_inv = 1/scale), with no barrier. Warps overwrite each other's value (WAW) and a warp can read another token's scale (RAW), giving wrong quantisation scales/outputs depending on warp timing.
fix_summary: Make `scale` a per-thread register (`const float scale = warp_max / FP8_E4M3_MAX;`) instead of a shared variable; also makes scale_inv const. No barrier needed.
evidence: PR 16886 title: 'Fix sgl-kernel per_token_quant fp8 kernel scale shared_memory bug'; code comment in the fix: one CTA has multiple warps (each handles one token) so scale must be per-warp/per-thread. No sanitizer log quoted; read the diff.
driver: sgl-kernel/tests/test_per_token_quant_fp8.py calls sgl_kernel.sgl_per_token_quant_fp8(input, output_q, output_s); NOTE the warp kernel is used only if num_tokens >= sm_count*2*8 (544 tokens on RTX 4060 Ti with 34 SMs, 2112 on H100) while the stock test goes only up to 512 tokens, so call it with e.g. x=torch.rand(1024, 2048, fp16) directly. ~2M elements, about 4e6 thread accesses. A standalone harness is easy: the __global__ kernel needs only flashinfer/vec_dtypes.cuh (header-only), warpReduceMax (shuffle max) and FP8_E4M3_MAX=448.
build_notes: Option A: pip install the sgl-kernel wheel built at the buggy commit (cd sgl-kernel && pip install -e . --no-build-isolation; CMake builds all of sgl-kernel, ~30+ min, set TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.9 / SGL_KERNEL_CUDA_ARCH if supported). Option B (cheap): copy lines 1-87 of per_token_quant_fp8.cu into a stand-alone .cu with a main() that allocates input/output and launches per_token_quant_fp8_kernel<__half,__nv_fp8_e4m3,8,16><<<ceil(T/8),256>>>; include flashinfer's vec_dtypes.cuh from the flashinfer clone and define warpReduceMax with __shfl_xor_sync.
dispute_points: Straightforward data race; same-lane values are identical within a warp (benign same-value WAW), the cross-warp ones differ. At the fix commit the code was also merged without a log. Stock test would not exercise the kernel at its default sizes on a 4060 Ti (see driver).

location_buggy: sgl-kernel/src/sgl-kernel/csrc/moe_align_kernel.cu:L44-L64 at bf2a7087 (`__shared__ int32_t shared_counts[WARP_SIZE][8]` zeroed per warp at L50-L54, then `atomicAdd(&shared_counts[warp_idx][expert_offset], 1)` at L63 by all threads, first barrier only at L66)
race_description: Each warp zero-initialises its own 8-entry row of shared_counts with plain stores (warp w clears row w). Immediately afterwards every thread of the block does atomicAdd on whatever row its token's expert maps to, i.e. rows initialised by other warps, with no barrier in between. A plain store of 0 from warp w can overwrite an atomic increment already done by another warp (lost counts), or the increment can be overwritten, so token counts per expert (and therefore the padded cumsum used for block alignment) come out wrong.
fix_summary: Adds one __syncthreads() between the shared_counts initialisation loop and the token-counting loop.
evidence: PR title 'fix moe_align_kernel shm init not sync bug (#3534)'; two-line diff adding __syncthreads(). No sanitizer log.
driver: sgl-kernel/tests/test_moe_align.py (exists at the buggy tree; calls sgl_kernel.moe_align_block_size with topk_ids of a few thousand entries, num_experts must be 256 because of the TORCH_CHECK). One CTA of 1024 threads, numel <= 8192, well under 1e7 accesses.
build_notes: Build the sgl-kernel python package from the buggy tree (cd sgl-kernel && pip install -e . or make build; it is a torch cpp_extension). RISK (unverified): this early-2025 source includes <THC/THCAtomics.cuh>, which recent PyTorch releases removed, so use a torch of that era (about 2.5) or replace the include with <ATen/cuda/Atomic.cuh>; or compile the single .cu together with a tiny C++ main that calls the kernel directly (the kernel itself needs no torch).
dispute_points: No author explanation beyond the title. The window is only hit when atomicAdd of a fast warp lands before the owning warp's init stores; in practice thread 0's warp usually initialises early, so wrong output was probably rare. Note the precondition in the host function: num_experts == 256 only (DeepSeek V3).

location_buggy: src/gpu/kernels.gen/compute_strain_kernel.cu:L211-L214 at buggy_commit: `if (NSPEC_STRAIN_ONLY == 1) { epsilon_trace_over_3[tx] = eps_trace_over_3; } else { epsilon_trace_over_3[ijk_ispec] = ...}`
race_description: When NSPEC_STRAIN_ONLY == 1 the output array epsilon_trace_over_3 is only a one-element-per-thread dummy buffer, but every block (one per spectral element, ispec = blockIdx.x + blockIdx.y*gridDim.x) still stores its own trace value to epsilon_trace_over_3[tx]. All blocks therefore write the same NGLL3 addresses with different values: a global write-write race between blocks.
fix_summary: Drops the dummy store: the assignment now happens only when NSPEC_STRAIN_ONLY > 1 (applied in the BOAST generators and in all regenerated .cu/.cpp/_cl.c kernels).
evidence: Commit message: 'avoids dummy assignments when NSPEC_CRUST_MANTLE_STRAIN_ONLY or NSPEC_INNER_CORE_STRAIN_ONLY == 1 (solves race-conditions on GPUs)' (Daniel Peter, 2021-10-31).
driver: Only reachable via the full SPECFEM3D_GLOBE GPU build (Fortran + MPI + configure --with-cuda, run xmeshfem3D/xspecfem3D with a tiny example under EXAMPLES/ and UNDO_ATTENUATION or strain-only settings). The generated .cu kernel itself needs mesh_constants_gpu.h and the config macros. Alternative: copy compute_strain_kernel with NSPEC_STRAIN_ONLY=1 into a harness with NGLL3_PADDED=128 threads and a few dozen blocks.
build_notes: Needs gfortran/MPI and the project's configure; or harness extraction (the kernel body is self-contained apart from a few macros). Not compiled by me: unverified.
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream).
dispute_points: Write-write race on a dummy buffer: the stored value is never consumed (benign in practice), only the commit message calls it a race; 116 stars (below 300). Only the NSPEC_STRAIN_ONLY==1 configuration (strain-only undo-attenuation mode) is affected, and sources under kernels.gen are generated from BOAST Ruby.

kernel: d_div_by_x_minus_z<fr_t, N=2, rotate, BSZ> (cooperative kernel, dynamic shared array xchg[])
location_buggy: polynomial/div_by_x_minus_z.cuh: xchg[] write L197 / barrier L199 / read L201; write L237 / barrier L239 / read xchg[laneid] L241 vs write xchg[threadIdx.x] L254; read xchg[blockIdx.x-1] L258 vs write xchg[warpid] L405 (N>1) ; read xchg[warpid-1] L412 vs next-chunk write L197; conditional tail barrier L422-L425 at buggy_commit. Same pattern in the sizeof(fr_t)>32 branch L342-L360
race_description: The block-wide scratch array xchg[] is reused for several carry exchanges. After a barrier all threads read xchg[laneid] (L201, L241) or xchg[blockIdx.x-1] (L258), but the next phase (L254 write xchg[threadIdx.x]; L405 write xchg[warpid] by lane 31 when N>1; and, in the next grid-stride chunk, L197) overwrites the same slots with no barrier in between, so a fast warp can overwrite a slot that a slower warp has not yet read. The reuse across chunks is only protected when tail_sync is true (the trailing __syncthreads is inside `if (tail_sync)`).
fix_summary: Adds __syncthreads() after the xchg[laneid] read at L241, after the xchg[laneid] read at L346 (>32-byte-field branch), before the xchg[warpid] write at L405, and makes the tail __syncthreads() after `if (tail_sync) __grid.sync()` unconditional.
evidence: Commit message: 'weed out shared memory race conditions. Fixes #85.' Issue #85 reports wrong quotients (14 mismatches at grid 36, RTX 4070 Laptop) and a racecheck RAW/WAR hazard on xchg[] between the inter-block carry read and the warp-0 write (second commenter, KZG mismatches on L4 sm_89 and H100 under racecheck; zero hazards after adding three barriers).
driver: No test in the repo for this header (poc/ only covers msm and ntt). Write a ~60-line harness: typedef gl64_t fr_t (ff/gl64_t.cuh; BSZ=1024), a minimal stream_t/gpu_t shim providing sm_count() and launch_coop() (util/gpu_t.cuh L113-L135 shows launch_coop = cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel) or link util/all_gpus.cpp + gpu_t.cuh, then call div_by_x_minus_z<false>(d_buf, len, z, stream, gridDim=34) with len=2^18 (4 grid-stride chunks, grid>32 so the L241/L254 pair is exercised). A few 1e6 thread-accesses.
build_notes: Header-only kernel: include ff/gl64_t.cuh, polynomial/div_by_x_minus_z.cuh, util/gpu_t.cuh (needs util/all_gpus.cpp for select_gpu/gpu_props, or replace stream_t with a shim). Not compiled by me (no nvcc here): unverified. Cooperative launch needs all grid blocks co-resident: with 1024-thread blocks on sm_89 one block per SM, so gridDim <= SM count (34 on RTX 4060 Ti, still > 32 so the gridDim.x > WARP_SZ paths run).
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream, issue #85).
dispute_points: Stars (222) are below the usual 300 threshold. The issue author says racecheck was noisy on this kernel (flagged hazards even on the correct N=1 control), so a detector should be compared against the 'before fix' vs 'after fix' difference, not absolute counts. In the single-block case several of the pairs are only ordered by timing, and the original failures were rare (3/10 sanitizer proofs, 0/600 without sanitizer for the second reporter). The sizeof(fr_t)>32 branch is, per the file comment, 'yet unused'.

kernel: sort (-> sort_row -> lower_sort), device function lower_sort(); dynamic shared array counters[]
location_buggy: msm/sort.cuh: read `counters[off]` L267 (off = warpid*WARP_SZ*N_SUMS + laneid + i*WARP_SZ) vs write `counters[warpid] = prefix_sums[N_SUMS-1]` L278 at buggy_commit
race_description: In lower_sort every warp w first reads its own slice counters[w*256 .. w*256+255] (N_SUMS=8 for DIGIT_BITS=13, 1024 threads), then lane 31 of warp w writes its warp total to counters[w]. For w>=1 index w lies inside warp 0's slice, which warp 0 lane w reads at L267 (i=0), and there is no __syncthreads between L267 and L278, so a fast warp w can overwrite counters[w] before warp 0 has read it.
fix_summary: Spreads the carry slots so each warp writes inside its own slice: counters[warpid*(WARP_SZ*N_SUMS+1)], and reads them back with the same stride at L282; the intra-warp ordering is provided by the full-mask shuffles.
evidence: Commit message: 'avoid potential race condition. Fixes #24.' Issue #24 'Race condition in msm/sort.cuh' names the exact pair, lines 267 and 278 (matching the buggy file); found by code reading, no racecheck output in the issue; reporter notes tests still pass on Ampere.
driver: No standalone test; sort is launched through launch_coop from msm/pippenger.cuh (digits(), L418-L445) and thus by the Rust test poc/msm-cuda/tests/msm.rs (cargo test, needs a BLS12-381/377 build). Smaller option: harness that includes msm/sort.cuh (DIGIT_BITS 13, SORT_BLOCKDIM 1024) and launches `sort` cooperatively with grid {2,1}, shared = sizeof(uint32_t)<<13 bytes, len ~ 1e5 digits from random data; with wbits<=13 the else-if (blockIdx.x==0) path reaches lower_sort.
build_notes: Needs util/ headers (vec2d_t.hpp, gpu_t.cuh, exception.cuh) and -rdc-free cooperative launch; the kernel is compiled non-RDC with __MSM_SORT_DONT_IMPLEMENT__ unset. Not compiled by me (no nvcc here): unverified. 1024-thread blocks with 32 KB dynamic shared memory: fine on sm_89.
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream, issue #24).
dispute_points: Stars (222) below the 300 threshold. Reporter found it by eyeballing; one commenter argued warps of a 1024-thread block may sit on different schedulers so the ordering is not guaranteed either way, and observable failures were not demonstrated. The fix is not a pure barrier but an address change. The reads at L267 happen right after the preceding __syncthreads in count_digits, so only the timing between warps makes the bad interleaving possible; a race detector should flag it regardless of timing.

location_buggy: msm/batch_addition.cuh: read `acc = ret[tid]` L45-L46 (accumulate && tid < gridDim.x*blockDim.x/WARP_SZ) vs write `ret[tid/warp_sz] = acc` L93-L94, grid sync only at L96, at buggy_commit
race_description: With accumulate=true each thread with tid < nthreads/32 reads ret[tid] at kernel start; at the end the lane-group leader (xid==0) of thread tid writes ret[tid/warp_sz]. The written slot index (tid/warp_sz) equals the read index of another thread (tid'=tid/warp_sz), usually in a different warp or block, and the grid-wide barrier comes only after the write, so a block that finishes its work early overwrites ret[] entries that blocks which have not started yet will still read as their initial accumulator.
fix_summary: Moves cooperative_groups::this_grid().sync() before the `if (xid == 0) ret[tid/warp_sz] = acc;` store, so every read of ret[] precedes every write.
evidence: Commit message: 'fix race condition by @sandsentinel.' (no issue number in the message; the reporter's PR/issue was not located: unverified). Race analysis above is from my reading of the pre-fix kernel, not from a maintainer description.
driver: Not used inside the repo at this revision; write a harness instantiating batch_addition<xyzz_t<fp_t>> (ec/xyzz_t.hpp has degree, uadd, shfl_down) with accumulate=true, launched with cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel (grid = SM count, 256 threads), npoints ~ 1e5 and a random bitmap. Roughly 1e6 thread accesses.
build_notes: Needs a curve/field setup (ff/bls12-381.hpp + ec/xyzz_t.hpp) and a hand-written launcher; the default static `streams[]` counter must be zero. Not compiled by me: unverified.
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream 2023-05-10).
dispute_points: Inferred from code reading: commit message does not describe the race. The reader/writer pair only conflicts when accumulate=true and the chosen slot is read by a different thread than the writer; with accumulate=false there is no read. Stars (222) are below 300. Requires a cooperative launch.

location_buggy: tensorflow/core/kernels/random_op_gpu.cu.cc:L127-L157 at 2cbcda08 (stride bug at L144: offset += (total_thread_count - 1) * kGroupSize)
race_description: The fill loop advances each thread's write offset by (total_thread_count-1)*kGroupSize instead of total_thread_count*kGroupSize. Thread 0's second-iteration offset (N-1)*G equals thread N-1's first-iteration offset, so thread 0 and the last thread (different blocks, or different warps) write the same output elements; the last writer wins nondeterministically.
fix_summary: One-line stride fix: offset += total_thread_count * kGroupSize; test arrays enlarged to 10^6 elements to expose it.
evidence: Commit message: GPU Philox fill kernel had race conditions causing non-deterministic output; the 0th and N-1st threads write the same locations, racing for who writes last.
driver: tf.random.normal/uniform/truncated_normal with >= ~10^6 elements on GPU (random_ops_test.py); the kernel is launched with a fixed number of thread contexts so size >> threads is needed.
build_notes: TF June-2017 cannot be built today. Extract the kernel with a minimal Philox implementation (tensorflow/core/lib/random/philox_random.h + random_distributions.h are header-only and need only Eigen); launch <<<num_blocks, 256>>> with size 10^6. SampleCopier specialisations at L60-L123.
dispute_points: Pure logic/stride bug that happens to be a WAW race; a detector will flag it only once the loop runs a second iteration (size > threads*group). Both writers write the same *value* distribution but different random numbers.

kernel: bitonicSortKVInPlace<...,Power2SortSize> via device helpers bitonicSort / bitonicSortKeys
location_buggy: lib/THC/THCSortUtils.cuh:L58-L100 (bitonicSort) and L104-L145 (bitonicSortKeys): `// Single warp per slice is completely synchronous  if (Power2SortSize > 64) { __syncthreads(); }` before every compare-exchange stage; shared arrays declared L168-L170 (sharedKeys/sharedValues/sharedValid) at buggy_commit
race_description: Each block sorts one slice of up to Power2SortSize elements in shared memory with a bitonic network; thread t compares keys[pos] and keys[pos+stride] with pos = 2t - (t & (stride-1)). For Power2SortSize <= 64 the block is a single warp (32 threads) and the code skips every __syncthreads because the warp is assumed lock-step. Consecutive stages read elements written by other lanes in the previous stage, so under independent thread scheduling these accesses are unordered (RAW and WAR on sharedKeys/sharedValues/sharedValid).
fix_summary: Makes the __syncthreads() unconditional before every stage and at the end (removes the `Power2SortSize > 64` guards).
evidence: Commit 'Get rid of warp-synchronous code (#739)' by ngimel (NVIDIA), 2017-03-29: 'Time to get rid of warp-synchronous code. It will break!'
driver: torch.sort on a CUDA tensor with sort dimension <= 64, e.g. `x = torch.CudaTensor(4096, 64):uniform(); torch.sort(x, 2)` (Lua Torch). Or extract THCSortUtils.cuh's bitonicSortKVInPlace into a C++ harness with 32 threads per block and 64-element slices.
build_notes: Lua Torch (LuaJIT + torch7 + cutorch) is unmaintained and hard to build against CUDA >= 12; the practical route is extracting bitonicSort/bitonicSortKVInPlace (needs TensorInfo, THCNumerics replaced by plain < ) into a standalone .cu. Early PyTorch THC carried a copy of this header (not checked by this agent).
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream).
dispute_points: Proactive hardening (before Volta shipped) rather than a reported failure; the same hazard is a documented property of ITS. Repository activity level not checked (Lua Torch is legacy).

kernel: reconstruct_gptq_kernel (dequantises a GPTQ 4-bit weight matrix to fp16; launched from QMatrix::reconstruct)
location_buggy: exllamav2/exllamav2_ext/cuda/q_matrix.cu:L216-L230 (perm[t] = b_q_perm[offset_k + t] stored to __shared__ uint16_t perm[BLOCK_KN_SIZE]; `if (n >= size_n) return;`) and the reads perm[lk++] at L291-L292, at 6940f1f2
race_description: Thread t (t < 128 = BLOCK_KN_SIZE) stores one entry of the act-order permutation table perm[t] to shared memory. In the main loop every thread reads perm[lk++] for lk = 0..127, i.e. entries written by other threads of other warps, with no __syncthreads between the stores and the first read (the kernel goes straight to the column computation). Only active when b_q_perm != null (GPTQ models with desc_act / act-order).
fix_summary: Adds one __syncthreads() after the perm preload and before the early `if (n >= size_n) return;` (so every thread of the block reaches it).
evidence: Commit title 'Fix sync bug in GPTQ reconstruct kernel'; the whole diff is a single added __syncthreads() after the perm[] preload block. No sanitizer output and no issue link.
driver: exllamav2.linear.ExLlamaV2Linear.get_weight_tensor_dq() -> ext_c.reconstruct(q_handle, tensor) (linear.py:L280) on a GPTQ 4-bit act-order layer; also reached by the prompt-phase gemm when rows exceed the small-batch limit. A synthetic call to ext_c.make_q_matrix with random tensors and a permutation (b_q_perm non-null) plus ext_c.reconstruct needs no model file (that path is unverified). One layer, e.g. 4096x4096, is about 16M outputs x few accesses, i.e. roughly 1e8; use a 1024x1024 layer to stay under 1e7.
build_notes: exllamav2 builds its extension with torch.utils.cpp_extension (JIT on first import, or `pip install .` at the buggy commit). Needs torch with CUDA and nvcc; this 2024 source with CUDA 13 + a current torch is unverified (older torch/CUDA 12.x is the safe pairing).
dispute_points: No reproduction or sanitizer log, and the visible effect would be a wrong dequantised weight only for act-order GPTQ layers. A kernel-level harness is easy but needs the extension's Python/ATen glue; the race window is small because perm is read only after the global-memory loads and dequant prep for the first group.

links: merged via merge b12acc6 ('Merge remote-tracking branch quarticcat/master into master2', 2023-09-08), i.e. a contributor PR/branch by QuarticCat
location_buggy: exllama_ext/cuda_func/q4_matmul.cu:L47 (extern __shared__ half2 x_cache[]), L88-L93 and L115-L120 (lanes write x_cache_h[i] then `if constexpr (THREADS_X*THREADS_Y > 32) __syncthreads();`), L99/L105/L127/L134 (dot_product_8 reads x_cache), L70-L74 (__syncthreads inside `if (... (threadIdx.x & 1) == 0)`) at buggy_commit
race_description: The block is 32x1 threads (THREADS_X=32, THREADS_Y=1), i.e. exactly one warp, and the author compiled the barrier out for that case (`THREADS_X*THREADS_Y > 32`). Lanes cooperatively fill the shared x_cache_h[] with a group of x values and then every lane reads the whole cache in dot_product_8; the next iteration's fill overwrites it again. Without a barrier or __syncwarp this relies on lock-step execution: on Volta and later (independent thread scheduling, e.g. sm_89) a lane can read an entry before the lane that writes it has stored it (RAW) or a fast lane can refill the cache while a slow lane still reads the old group (WAR). The same commit also moves the zero-init __syncthreads out of a divergent `if` (barrier divergence).
fix_summary: Makes both __syncthreads() calls in the k loops unconditional (drops the `THREADS_X*THREADS_Y > 32` guard) and hoists the __syncthreads() after the output-zeroing out of the divergent branch.
evidence: Commit title 'Optimize q4_matmul: fix __syncthreads' (QuarticCat, 2023-09-06), no body. It does not use the word race; classification as warp-synchronous/ITS hazard is mine, based on the diff and the 32x1 launch geometry.
driver: exllama's CUDA extension (exllama_ext, built with torch cpp_extension): q4_matmul_cuda is reached from the 4-bit Linear layers, e.g. the repo's test_benchmark_inference.py or a small script that builds a Q4Matrix and calls the extension's q4_matmul; a 4096x4096 4-bit matrix and a 1-token x (height=1) is enough (blocks = (width/32, height, dim/384)).
build_notes: Needs a GPTQ 4-bit model or synthetic Q4Matrix, torch + nvcc extension build (several minutes); the kernel is not usable in isolation without MatrixView/Q4Matrix helpers from matrix.cuh. Check out buggy_commit's parent chain in the fork merge (the fix itself sits on a side branch merged 2023-09-08).
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream).
dispute_points: No mention of a race in the commit; the original author deliberately omitted the barrier for single-warp blocks, which was valid pre-Volta. Whether a tool reports an intra-warp RAW as a race depends on its ITS handling. Merged through the merge of a contributor's branch, so verify the fix_commit is in master's history (mk check says it is an ancestor of HEAD).

kernel: compute_dynamic_per_token_scales (group-quant path) via warpReduceMaxSpecialized, used by the fused rms_norm_per_block_quant kernels
location_buggy: csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/fused_kernels/layernorm_utils.cuh:L50-L71 (warpReduceMaxSpecialized, volatile smem) and L110-L129 (s_max_vals[start] = fmaxf(s_max_vals[start], s_max_vals[j + warp_size]) loop) at 6ec92bcb; a second copy of the same group-reduce code exists later in the same header
race_description: A per-group max over s_max_vals[] is done 'warp-synchronously': each stage val[tid] = fmaxf(val[tid], val[tid + off]) reads a value written by another lane in the previous stage, and the strided pre-loop does the same, with only a volatile qualifier and no __syncwarp()/shuffle. Under independent thread scheduling lanes can run ahead and read stale/partially-reduced values, so scales were occasionally wrong (flaky CI).
fix_summary: Replaced by register reduction with warp shuffles (warpReduceMax via VLLM_SHFL_DOWN_SYNC) and a single lane-0 write of the result to shared memory.
evidence: PR 54111 (mgoin, fixes flaky H200 CI): 'caused by a real shared-memory race in warpReduceMaxSpecialized ... CUDA racecheck reported thousands of hazards for the failing specialization'; after the fix 'RACECHECK SUMMARY: 0 hazards'. Failing tests: tests/kernels/core/test_fused_quant_layernorm.py::test_rms_norm[...2048x1024-int8-group-64...] and ...float8_e4m3fn-group-64...
driver: vLLM pytest `tests/kernels/core/test_fused_quant_layernorm.py::test_rms_norm` with params 2048x1024, group-64 (int8 or float8_e4m3fn), residual=True, bf16, run under `compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck python -m pytest -q -x <that test id>`. Smaller shapes (e.g. 1x1024 / 16x1024 group-64) should suffice for the hazard but the PR only lists 2048x1024 as failing. 2048x1024 is ~2M elements (~2e7 accesses, within budget).
build_notes: Needs a vLLM source build with CUDA kernels (VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cuda TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.9 pip install -e . at the buggy commit; ~30-60 min, needs torch matching the checkout). The layernorm_utils.cuh kernel depends on vLLM headers/torch-stable shims, so a standalone harness is not trivial; building only the _C extension target may be faster. sm_89 supported (FP8 e4m3 needs sm_89).
dispute_points: Warp-synchronous (ITS) class; the lanes' exact conflicting pair is reported by racecheck only on specialisations where threads_per_group < blockDim (group-64). Test failing flakily on H200 means the symptom is real. Build effort is the main drawback.

kernel: Marlin<...> (GPTQ/AWQ Marlin GEMM): pipeline smem `sh`, thread_block_reduce / global_reduce / write_result
location_buggy: csrc/quantization/gptq_marlin/gptq_marlin.cu: scale prefetch ~L925-L945 (cp_async4 into sh_s_stage only every group_blocks/thread_k_blocks pipe steps, read via a shifted stage index ~L1039-L1045), reduction writes/reads `sh[...]` ~L1335-L1365, write-back staging `sh[c_sh_wr...]`/`sh[threadIdx.x]` ~L1395-L1550 (all at 187e3299)
race_description: (Three read/write hazards found by racecheck.) (1) Scale tiles are cp.async-prefetched into stage buffers while earlier pipeline stages still read them. (2) The thread-block/global reduction uses the same shared array `sh` that holds the A/B pipeline stages, so reduction writes race with cp.async prefetches/reads of matrix A. (3) The result reordering buffer used for write-back also aliases the A staging area. The same cp.async pipelines may still be in flight (no full cp.async.wait_all/barrier before reuse).
fix_summary: Carved out a dedicated `sh_red` shared region after sh_s and used it for reductions and write-back; changed the scale prefetch/stage indexing; extended the shared-memory budget check (reduce_size in is_valid_cache_size).
evidence: PR 11493 (wchen61): 'After using the racecheck tool in compute-sanitizer, I found that there is a read-write race condition in the kernel implementation of Marlin' at 3 places; fixes occasional NaN outputs in GPTQ inference (issues 10656, 11205). After the patch the race no longer occurs. A reviewer notes other projects (optimum-quanto, TGI) copy the original Marlin kernel.
driver: tests/kernels/test_marlin_gemm.py::test_gptq_marlin_gemm (name per PR thread; path at this commit is tests/kernels/ ), run under `compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck`. Pick a small shape (e.g. size_m=1..16, size_k=128..256, size_n=256) for 4-bit, group_size 128. Original IST-DASLab/marlin shares the same structure -- see llamacpp?/marlin entry if recorded.
build_notes: vLLM source build at the buggy commit with TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.9 (Marlin needs sm_80+; 4060 Ti OK; shared-memory budget differs between A100 and Ada, PR author hit test failures on L4 due to 128 KB limit -> sm_89 has 99 KB opt-in smem, so the fixed kernel picks smaller configs there). Alternatively test the original IST-DASLab/marlin kernel (standalone torch extension).
dispute_points: Three bundled races; exact lines inferred from the diff (the PR does not list racecheck addresses). Fix changed config selection as well (fix_is_sync_only false). Kernel is heavy (hundreds of registers/threads) and the cp.async ordering analysis relies on the author's description.

links: Simulee (ICSE 2020) Sec. 4 / Table 2: 'thundersvm febf515a82 smo-kernel.cu, data race, fixed by adding __syncthreads()'
location_buggy: src/thundersvm/kernel/smo_kernel.cu at buggy_commit: f_val2reduce read at L169 (low_value_p) vs refill at L172-175; read at L203 (f_val_j2p) vs refill at L206-211
race_description: nu_smo_solve_kernel runs several get_block_min reductions back to back over the same shared array f_val2reduce. After each reduction every thread reads f_val2reduce[j] (j = argmin, e.g. L169 and L203) and then immediately refills f_val2reduce[tid] for the next reduction (L172-175, L206-211). With no barrier in between, the thread whose tid==j (or any fast thread) overwrites the slot while a thread in another warp has not yet read it, so the read returns the next phase's value (or INFINITY).
fix_summary: Insert __syncthreads() after the f_val2reduce[j1p] read and after the f_val2reduce[j2p] read (plus one more before the first reduction). The same commit also rewrites is_I_up/is_I_low conditions and wires the kernel into a new NuSMOSolver (nusmosolver.cu), so the diff is not sync-only.
evidence: Commit message 'nu-svc fix bugs'. Simulee paper cites this exact revision as a write&write/write-after-read shared-memory race fixed by __syncthreads.
driver: At the buggy commit nu_smo_solve_kernel is defined but never launched (NU_SVC path is commented out in svmmodel.cu), so build the fix commit's tree and revert only the added __syncthreads() in smo_kernel.cu (or write a harness that calls nu_smo_solve_kernel<<<1,ws_size,smem>>> with ws_size=64..1024). Train NU_SVC on a small libsvm dataset (dataset/get_datasets.sh; test_dataset.txt is in-tree).
build_notes: CMake + CUDA; 2017 code uses cuSPARSE/thrust of that era and may need patches for CUDA 13 (cusparse csrmm API). A standalone harness around the single kernel avoids that: it only needs label/f/alpha/working_set/k_mat_rows arrays and dynamic smem = ws_size*(sizeof(int)+sizeof(float)) + 2 floats + ws_size floats.
dispute_points: Same hazard repeats in the current HEAD only if the barriers are missing; HEAD has them, so this is a pure fixed-bug target. Kernel is launched with one block; ws_size must be >32 for the hazard to be cross-warp.

kernel: GPUTPCGMMerger::MergeBorderTracks<0> (fills border-track ranges range1/range2 in global memory)
location_buggy: GPU/GPUTracking/Merger/GPUTPCGMMerger.cxx:L630-L665 at 3670f0e1 (range1[itr] = ... ; 'if (sameSlice) for i<N1: range2[i] = range1[i];')
race_description: In the sameSlice case every thread, after writing its own range1[itr], loops over ALL N1 entries and copies range1[i] into range2[i]. Entries range1[i] of other threads may not be written yet (RAW) and range2[i] is written by several threads (WAW). Each thread should only copy its own entry.
fix_summary: Builds a local GPUTPCGMBorderRange, stores it to range1[itr], and in the sameSlice case writes only range2[itr] = range; the other-slice fill is changed the same way. The commit also contains unrelated host-chain guards (doGPU checks).
evidence: Commit title: GPU: Fix race condition and incorrect implementation for creating border tracks (D. Rohr, 2020-06-18). No sanitizer output quoted.
driver: No unit test. Only the GPU/GPUTracking Standalone benchmark (cmake in GPU/GPUTracking/Standalone) with a recorded TPC event dump or raw ZS pages; the dump is not in the repo (size and availability unverified), so a custom micro-driver that calls the device function with synthetic input is likely needed.
build_notes: Standalone GPUTracking build is possible without the full O2 stack (Standalone/CMake, CUDA backend) but is a large project (hours) and ties to a 2021-2023 code base; CUDA 13 compatibility of the old parent is unverified. Alternative: vendor the single kernel into a small .cu with the GPUCA macros.
already_reported_check: Not searched on GitHub issues.
dispute_points: Whether threads of one block cover all entries before the copy loop depends on how the kernel maps threads to blocks (not read here); the 'incorrect implementation' wording suggests part of the fix is functional, not only a race. Driver weak.

kernel: build_cells(): the 'fix face for small cells' AMREX_LAUNCH_HOST_DEVICE_LAMBDA(bxg1, tbx, ...) (x-face loop then y-face loop in one kernel; 3D adds a z loop)
location_buggy: Src/EB/AMReX_EB2_2D_C.cpp:L333-L378 at the buggy commit (the 'fix face for small cells' lambda: x loop writes fx/apx/cell/vfrac..., y loop reads apx/apy via set_eb_data); 3D: AMReX_EB2_3D_C.cpp from L749
race_description: One kernel handles the x-direction face fix and then the y-direction (and z in 3D) face fix. For faces next to a covered cell it writes fx/apx=0, setSingleValued() on the two adjacent cells and recomputes their EB data with set_eb_data, which reads apx/apy of neighbouring faces. Another thread's x-direction phase writes apx(i,j) while this thread's y-direction set_eb_data(i,j) reads it, and adjacent threads both write cell(i,j) and its EB data. The phases are not separated by any barrier, so the order is undefined.
fix_summary: Splits the single lambda into one AMREX_HOST_DEVICE_FOR_3D launch per direction (x faces, then y faces, then z), turning the missing barrier into a kernel boundary; the condition is also tightened to vfrac == 0.
evidence: Commit message (W. Zhang, 2020-10-29): a GPU race condition introduced in #1451 is fixed by launching a separate kernel for each direction. The code comment added says races do not happen within one direction because multiple cuts are not allowed.
driver: Any EB geometry build on GPU, e.g. Tests/LinearSolvers/CellEB with inputs.rt.2d or inputs.rt.3d (eb2.geom_type = sphere, sphere_radius 0.25 in the unit box; n_cell small such as 32). The racy lambda runs for every face adjacent to a covered cell. A few 10^5 accesses.
build_notes: Old tree (Oct 2020) uses the GNUmake build: make USE_CUDA=TRUE USE_MPI=FALSE DIM=2 or 3 in Tests/LinearSolvers/CellEB with CUDA_ARCH=89 (nvcc 13 may reject old AMReX code: -std=c++14 and removed APIs; unverified). The cmake build of that era needs -DAMReX_EB=ON.
already_reported_check: Not searched beyond the commit message.
dispute_points: AMREX_LAUNCH_HOST_DEVICE_LAMBDA gives each thread a sub-box tbx of bxg1, so the conflicting threads are different threads/blocks of one launch; I did not confirm the per-thread box shape for this 2020 tree. The commit message does not say which accesses conflict; the description above is from reading the diff.

location_buggy: cupyx/scipy/sparse/_csr.py:L1116-L1132 at 4cb51274 (`OUT[col + N*row] += DATA;` / `OUT[row + M*col] += DATA;` at L1124-L1128); csr2dense() wrapper L1108-L1113; reached from csr_matrix.toarray() only for dtypes not in 'fdFD' (L398)
race_description: One thread per stored CSR element (i = nnz index). In a CSR matrix with duplicate (row,col) entries (non-canonical format, which csr_matrix allows) several threads compute the same OUT index and each does a plain read-modify-write `OUT[idx] += DATA`, losing updates; threads of the same warp or of different blocks can collide.
fix_summary: Use atomicAdd(&OUT[index], DATA) (or `if (DATA) OUT[index]=true` for bool, where a same-value write is benign).
evidence: Commit title: 'Fix csr2dense to avoid race conditions' (Akifumi Imanishi, Preferred Networks). Diff replaces += with atomicAdd.
driver: Python: import cupy, cupyx.scipy.sparse as sp; A = sp.csr_matrix((cupy.ones(1000,'i4'), cupy.zeros(1000,'i4'), cupy.array([0,1000],'i4')), shape=(1,4)); A.toarray()  -> expected 1000 at [0,0] (non-float dtype takes csr2dense path). Thousands of duplicate entries to force collisions; tiny. Also covered by cupy tests/cupyx_tests/scipy_tests/sparse_tests/test_csr.py (toarray with int dtypes), exact duplicate test unverified.
build_notes: pip install cupy-cuda12x (or cuda13x wheel) of a version released before 2023-07-14, e.g. cupy 12.1.0 (released 2023-06?, unverified) - kernel is compiled at runtime by NVRTC (jit: true), so a detector must work on runtime-loaded cubins; else build current cupy and monkeypatch the kernel source back to `+=`.
dispute_points: Only the int/bool path was racy (float dtypes used cusparse sparseToDense after sum_duplicates). Race needs duplicate entries - uncommon but legal. NVRTC/JIT-compiled.

kernel: fir_sos (CUDA source embedded in IIR_KERNEL string, launched by apply_iir_sos)
location_buggy: cupyx/scipy/signal/_iir_utils.py:L441-L492 at 25aea408 (carry read `fir_cache[pos] = group_carries[pos]` at L475, carry write `this_carries[pos-(m-k)] = acc` at L487-L489; this_carries(g) aliases group_carries(g+1))
race_description: fir_sos has one thread-block per group of m samples. Block g loads the FIR carry of the previous group from carries[(g-offset)*k + pos] while block g-1 (same launch) writes exactly those words as `this_carries[pos-(m-k)] = acc` (this_carries(g-1) == group_carries(g)). There is no inter-block ordering (no fence/flag/second kernel), so block g can read stale or half-updated carries.
fix_summary: fir_sos no longer writes carries; a separate carries_kernel launch computes them after fir_kernel completes (kernel boundary). The per-section loop was also moved to the host.
evidence: Commit title 'Prevent data races on FIR carries' (Edgar Margffoy, cupyx.scipy.signal sosfilt work); adds TestIIRUtilSos.test_sections/test_sections_nd (sizes 11..250, sections 1..5, block_sz=32).
driver: Python: from cupyx.scipy.signal._iir_utils import apply_iir_sos; out = apply_iir_sos(x, sos, block_sz=32) with x float32 length 250 (>=2 groups), sos shape (sections,6), sos[:,3]=1 (test added by the fix commit; compare with scipy.signal.sosfilt). Tiny input.
build_notes: pip install a cupy wheel from before 2023-05-09 (kernel NVRTC-compiled at runtime via cupy.RawModule, jit: true) or use cupy source at buggy_commit; the kernel string can also be extracted and compiled with nvcc using thrust::complex headers.
dispute_points: The commit refactors the whole sos pipeline, so what exactly raced is partly inferred from the diff (carry words aliased between neighbouring blocks in one launch). Author's message is only the one-line title. JIT-compiled.

links: https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/commit/9b0bc978729d5470aaf5667b8f65df6fa2b3a007 (first of the 2022-10/11 Triton race series; adds test_flash_attn_triton_race_condition)
location_buggy: flash_attn/flash_attn_triton.py:L326-L349 at 86862cfd (bias load `if BIAS_TYPE != 'none':` L328 followed by the bias-dependent softmax recompute; the existing debug_barrier() calls are at L347, L381, L385)
race_description: The author states only that the Triton backward kernel with a bias has a race condition caused by the Triton compiler and that a tl.debug_barrier() before the bias load removes it. Inferred mechanism (not stated by the author): the 2022 Triton code generator stages operands/layout conversions through compiler-allocated shared-memory buffers and reuses one of them between the qk recompute and the bias load/add without a barrier, so a fast warp overwrites the buffer while a slow warp still reads it (cross-warp smem WAR). The actual conflicting accesses are only visible in the generated PTX/SASS, not in the Python source.
fix_summary: Adds one `tl.debug_barrier()  # Race condition otherwise` at the top of the `if BIAS_TYPE != 'none':` block in the backward kernel (a CTA-wide bar.sync).
evidence: Commit 'Fix race condition in Triton bwd when there's bias' (2022-11-04) plus the series 9b0bc97, 731f154, aacc10f, 470010f, 62025e1 over 2022-10-31..11-04, all described by the author as races caused by the Triton compiler, found with the new test tests/test_flash_attn.py::test_flash_attn_triton_race_condition (results differ between runs).
driver: tests/test_flash_attn.py::test_flash_attn_triton_race_condition at ff78ea4 (flash_attn.flash_attn_triton.flash_attn_func(q, k, v, bias, causal) forward+backward repeated and compared with the first run; test is skipped unless is_sm80, i.e. it needs the sm80 check changed for the RTX 4060 Ti sm_89); use batch 1-2, d=64, seqlen 113/203, a few 1e6 accesses.
build_notes: Needs the contemporaneous Triton (about 2.0.0.dev20221030..20221202 nightlies; pip wheels for that era target Python <= 3.10 and CUDA 11.x) because modern Triton rejects this API (tl.dot, eviction_policy arguments, autotune restore) and its code generation is different. RISK (unverified): wheels may no longer be installable; CUDA 13 definitely not. sm_89 should work through PTX JIT.
dispute_points: The race is a Triton-compiler (smem allocation) bug of 2022, not a bug visible in the Python kernel source; it may not reproduce on any Triton available today, and the buggy commit cannot be rebuilt without an archived Triton nightly. Related earlier fixes in the series changed EVEN_M/EVEN_N masking to dodge the same compiler issue (not pure synchronisation), so only this one and 62025e1 are pure barrier insertions.

kernel: flash_fwd_splitkv_mla_kernel (Hopper split-KV MLA decode, 2 consumer warpgroups + producer; sM = per-row running softmax max in shared memory)
location_buggy: csrc/kernels/splitkv_mla.cu:L1098-L1100 (threads 0..63 initialise sM) vs first reads of sM in wg0_bunch_0 L360-L368 and wg1_bunch_0 L440-L447, reached via wg0_subroutine after the first QK^T gemm at L1124-L1126; at 70b94685
race_description: sM (BLOCK_SIZE_M=64 floats) is initialised to MAX_INIT_VAL_SM by threadIdx.x < 64, i.e. only warps 0 and 1 of warpgroup 0. Warpgroup 0 then reads sM(row_idx) for all 64 rows (each warp handles 16 rows, so warps 2 and 3 read rows written by warps 0/1) with no barrier between the init store and the first read (only a __syncwarp inside wg0_bunch_0, which orders nothing across warps). The fix adds a 128-thread named barrier (sMInitialized) after the first Q@K^T gemm, before wg0_subroutine.
fix_summary: Adds NamedBarrier::arrive_and_wait(128, NamedBarriers::sMInitialized) (new enum value 4 in traits.h) after the first QK^T gemm in warpgroup 0 so sM is visible to the whole warpgroup. The same commit also stops using __ldg for tile_scheduler_metadata and num_splits (PDL reordering past cudaGridDependencySynchronize, inter-kernel, out of scope).
evidence: Commit title 'Fix synchronization issues'; the added comment says the barrier makes sure previous writes to sM are visible to warpgroup 0. A second part of the same commit (comment mentions ldg reordered before the PDL grid-dependency wait causing a data race) is an inter-kernel issue and is not the candidate. No sanitizer log.
driver: tests/test_flash_mla.py (python tests/test_flash_mla.py; test_flash_mla(b, s_q, mean_sk, h_q, h_kv, d=576, dv=512, causal, varlen); use b=1, s_q=1, mean_sk=256..1024, h_q=128, h_kv=1 so only a few CTAs run, ~1e7 thread accesses). Needs an sm_90 GPU (wgmma, TMA, setmaxnreg).
build_notes: git checkout 70b94685 && git submodule update --init (cutlass) && pip install -v . (setup.py builds sm_90a only; the original source needs CUDA >= 12.3, uses PTX that CUDA 13 ptxas should still accept (unverified)). Not runnable on the sm_89 RTX 4060 Ti; needs the H100.
dispute_points: Only the H100 can run it. The race hits the first iteration only (sM init vs first read) and in practice the first QK^T gemm and K0 wait take long enough that the init store is almost certainly visible, so there is no known wrong output; the fix is attributed to 'synchronization issues' with no reproducer in the commit. The sibling reads of sM in warpgroup 1 are ordered after warpgroup 0's update through the sScale0Ready named barrier, so the race is confined to warpgroup 0.

location_buggy: pytorch3d/csrc/sample_farthest_points/sample_farthest_points.cu:L56-L122 at 597bc7c7 (all threads read dists_idx[0] at L116 after the last barrier of the tree reduction at L107; thread 0 overwrites dists_idx[0]/dists[0] at L87-L88 in the next k iteration; no barrier in between)
race_description: The block iterates k=1..K and in each iteration reduces per-thread (max_dist, max_dist_idx) through shared arrays dists[]/dists_idx[] with a tree reduction ending in __syncthreads (L107). Afterwards every thread reads the winner `selected = dists_idx[0]` (L116). In the next iteration thread 0 can finish its (point-loop) work and store its new candidate into dists_idx[0] (L88) while a slower warp has not yet executed the L116 read of the previous iteration: no barrier separates the read at the end of iteration k from the write at the beginning of iteration k+1 (the first barrier of iteration k+1 is at L90, after the write).
fix_summary: Commit replaces the hand-written shared-memory block reduction by cub::BlockReduce<KeyValuePair<int64_t,float>> and broadcasts the winner through a dedicated __shared__ selected_store with an explicit __syncthreads() before every thread reads it; the cub internal barriers order the next write.
evidence: Commit summary (Max Wasylow, FB): 'Replacing custom CUDA block reductions with CUB in sample_farthest_points' to reduce code complexity; the commit does not mention a race and no sanitizer output is given. The race is identified by reading the removed code - the fix is incidental to a refactor.
driver: pytorch3d.ops.sample_farthest_points(points[N,P,3] cuda float, K=int) -> FarthestPointSamplingCuda: grid=N blocks of min(pow2>=P,1024) threads; e.g. N=2, P=4096, K=32 gives 32*4096*3*2 ~ 8e5 global accesses plus smem reduction (1024 thr x 10 steps x 32 iters). Test: tests/test_sample_farthest_points.py.
build_notes: Easiest is to extract the old kernel (git show 597bc7c7:pytorch3d/csrc/sample_farthest_points/sample_farthest_points.cu, L17-L123) into a harness replacing the at::PackedTensorAccessor64 with raw pointers (points[b*P*D+p*D+d]) and launch with dynamic smem threads*(4+8) bytes. Full pytorch3d build against torch for CUDA 13 is heavy (setup.py compiles all csrc).
dispute_points: Not described as a bug by the authors; the window is very narrow (thread 0 must complete a full point loop of P/block_size distance evaluations before a lagging warp executes a single shared load that follows a block barrier), so it has probably never produced a wrong result. It is a textbook happens-before violation though, which a detector should flag. Treat as a low-confidence ground truth for the 'fixed' list.

kernel: AttentionBackwardKernel<...>::processBlockIJ, GradK matmul + accumulateInGmem<MatmulGradK> epilogue (fmha_cutlassB, head_dim > register-resident limit i.e. kOutputInRF == false)
location_buggy: xformers/csrc/attention/cuda/fmha/kernel_backward.h:L2196-L2211 at 2cc77aea (end of the `for col` GradK loop body: accumulateInGmem<MatmulGradK>(isLastColumn ? gradK_epilogue_final() : gradK_epilogue(), ...) L2201-L2208, nothing after it); next processBlockIJ call (L1415) / next col iteration writes smem aliased with the epilogue storage (SharedStorageNoPrologue part6 gradK_epilogue_final aliases part1 mm_qk_k/mm_qk_q, part5 gradK_epilogue aliases mm_gradK, L1039-L1118)
race_description: After the dK accumulation the kernel runs the pipelined CUTLASS epilogue (accumulateInGmem) that stages the tile through the gradK_epilogue(_final) shared storage. That storage overlaps (union) with the operand staging of the Q.K^T / gradK matmuls that the next loop iteration (next query block or next head-dim column) starts with; the epilogue ends with smem reads and no barrier, so a fast warp can begin the next iteration's smem stores while a slow warp is still reading the epilogue tile. Only reachable when !kOutputInRF (large head dim).
fix_summary: Adds a single __syncthreads() right after accumulateInGmem inside the else branch of the dK write-out.
evidence: Commit title '[cutlassB] Fix race-condition'; one-line diff adding the barrier. The mechanism above is my reading of the shared-storage unions, not stated by the authors.
driver: xformers.ops.fmha.cutlass.BwOp / xformers.ops.memory_efficient_attention(...).backward() with head_dim 192-256 (kMaxK > 128 so !kOutputInRF), fp16 on sm80, seqlen >= 3 query blocks (e.g. B=1,H=2,M=N=512,K=192). tests/test_mem_eff_attention.py::test_backward covers K up to 256 (name unverified). A few 1e7 accesses.

RISK (unverified): this old source with a CUDA 13 toolchain and a modern torch (extension API, CCCL 3) may not compile; prefer a CUDA 11.8/12.x toolkit and the torch version contemporary with the commit. Note that the C++ extension was removed from the open-source xformers tree on 2026-09-22 (commit 0568e0d), so only historic commits are buildable; PyTorch ships a copy of the same cutlass kernels (aten/src/ATen/native/transformers/cuda/mem_eff_attention) with later history.
dispute_points: No author explanation or log; my mechanism may not be the exact one the authors fixed (their one-line diff could also cover a different pair of accesses, e.g. between accumulateInGmem and prologueQkNextIteration). Unions in SharedStoragePrologue differ from SharedStorageNoPrologue, so the race may exist only in the kPreload=false (sm75/sm50) variants. Needs sm80 hardware only if kPreload (cp.async) path is used.

kernel: flashinfer::sampling::SamplingFromLogitsKernel<BLOCK_THREADS, ..., VEC_SIZE, DETERMINISTIC, DType, IdType> (Gumbel-max argmax over a row, looped over vocab chunks)
location_buggy: include/flashinfer/sampling.cuh:L741-L762 at a81e6b47 (loop `for i < ceil_div(d, BLOCK_THREADS*VEC_SIZE)`; cub BlockReduce(temp_storage).Sum<VEC_SIZE>(cur_data) at L759-761 reuses the same shared TempStorage every iteration; no __syncthreads at the end of the loop body)
race_description: Each loop iteration of one block performs a CUB BlockReduce on the same shared TempStorage. CUB requires a __syncthreads between consecutive uses of one TempStorage, because the final phase of the reduction reads the per-warp partials from shared memory while a fast warp that has finished the previous iteration already writes its next partial into the same slots. For vocab_size >= BLOCK_THREADS*VEC_SIZE (e.g. 32000) the loop runs several times, so the write of iteration i+1 races with the read of iteration i by another warp.
fix_summary: Adds __syncthreads() after each BlockReduce in the loop (the actual race fix). Also makes padding lanes carry index 0 instead of an out-of-range index so a corrupted reduce can no longer return token id >= vocab.
evidence: PR 3624 body (flaky test_int64_indices_sampling): reuse of CUB temp storage without a barrier violates CUB's contract; 'compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck: original kernel reports hundreds of Write/Read hazards in SamplingFromLogitsKernel, fixed kernel 0 hazards'. Related issue 3470.
driver: flashinfer.sampling.sampling_from_logits(logits, ...) / the test tests/utils/test_sampling.py::test_int64_indices_sampling (name from the PR text, file path unverified) with logits shape (batch=1..4, vocab=32000) float32; e.g. `compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck python -c 'import torch,flashinfer; l=torch.randn(4,32000,device="cuda"); flashinfer.sampling.sampling_from_logits(l)'`. About 4*32000 elements: well under 10^7 accesses.

Kernels are built on first call by nvcc/ninja (JIT cache ~/.cache/flashinfer); export FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.9 to build only sm_89. This is nvcc JIT, not NVRTC, so the resulting .so/cubin can be run under the detector; run python under the detector (python -m pytest ... or a 20-line script). dispute_points: The fix commit also changes index handling (padding lanes) so part of the diff is not sync-only; the barrier hunk itself is one line. CUB documents the barrier requirement, so the race is not disputable in the memory model. Whether a given REDUCE_ALGORITHM instantiation actually has the shared read-after-write overlap (warp-reductions vs raking) depends on the template, racecheck found hazards on the instantiation used by the test.

location_buggy: include/flashinfer/topk.cuh:L2732-L2776 at 97b7de68 (round loop: `if (tx < RADIX + 1) s_histogram[tx] = 0;` at L2736 in round r+1 vs `topk_remain -= s_histogram[threshold + 1]` at L2770 in round r; the loop body ends without a barrier)
race_description: In the multi-round overflow fallback every round reuses s_histogram. At the end of round r all threads read s_histogram[threshold+1] (L2770) to update topk_remain; at the start of round r+1 threads clear s_histogram[tx] (L2736). The only barrier after the clear is at L2737, so a fast warp can clear the histogram before a slow warp has done its read of the previous round.
fix_summary: One-line fix: adds a __syncthreads() after the topk_remain decrement, before the loop breaks or continues to the next round.
evidence: PR 3529 flags it as found by racecheck and includes a repro and output on a GB300: 'Race reported between Read access ... and Write access ... FilteredTopKUnifiedKernel<float, int, 4, true, 0> [3852 hazards]' (three such records, RACECHECK SUMMARY: 3 hazards displayed (3 errors, 0 warnings)). Repro: all-zero logits, rows=512, vocab=131072, k=128, float32, deterministic=True, which forces every element into one coarse bin and thus the overflow refinement loop.

kernel: RadixSelectOneRound / RadixSelectFromSharedMemory used by the multi-CTA kernels (e.g. RadixTopKRenormProbKernel_MultiCTA)
location_buggy: include/flashinfer/topk.cuh:L544-L558 (RadixSelectOneRound: per-thread atomicAdd(&current_hist[i]) L546 and leader-CTA `next_hist[i] = 0` L553, then AdvanceRadixGroupBarrier L558) and L729-L737 (RadixSelectFromSharedMemory, same shape) at 8c54f344; barrier = tx==0 red_release at L174-183
race_description: Multi-CTA radix top-k uses a software grid-group barrier whose release is a thread-0-only fence.acq_rel.gpu + red.relaxed. Other threads of the CTA do their atomicAdd into the shared global histogram (and the leader CTA clears next_hist) right before the barrier with no __syncthreads, so thread 0's release fence is not ordered after those writes by CTA causality and does not publish them: a peer CTA can pass the barrier and read current_hist (plain load) before a contributor's atomicAdd lands, or start the next round's atomicAdd into next_hist before the leader's lagging threads finished clearing it.
fix_summary: Adds __syncthreads() immediately before AdvanceRadixGroupBarrier at both sites so tx0's release covers every thread's writes (same idiom as RadixGroupResetStateLastCTA).
evidence: PR 5251: 'There is no __syncthreads() between those per-thread writes and the barrier, so the release does not cover them'. Validated by injecting 10us-1ms delays at the global atomics of RadixTopKRenormProbKernel_MultiCTA: unpatched output deviates ~0.03 from an exact reference every run, patched is exact. No racecheck log (racecheck does not model grid-level release/acquire).
driver: Multi-CTA path of flashinfer.sampling.top_k_renorm_probs / top_k_mask_logits / top_k_top_p_sampling_from_probs for a large vocab (e.g. batch 1-4, vocab 128K-256K, k 50-256) which makes ctas_per_group > 1; function name for the python entry is unverified. Access count is a few million per row.

dispute_points: Pure cross-block release/acquire modelling: a detector must treat 'bar.sync then thread0 fence+red' as the only valid publication path. In silicon the failure needed artificial delays, so the symptom is not observable without stress. Atomics are involved, but the conflicting pairs are atomic-vs-plain-load and plain-store-vs-atomic, which count as conflicts. Multi-CTA path needs enough SMs to co-schedule the group (cooperative-style spin barrier), fine on a 4060 Ti (34 SMs) for small groups.

kernel: checkpointing_ssu_kernel -> ssu_checkpoint (must_checkpoint == true path): load_data/load_state_per_warp then replay_state_mma
location_buggy: include/flashinfer/mamba/kernel_checkpointing_ssu.cuh:L1036 (load_data, per-warp cp.async into smem.state, ends with __pipeline_wait_prior(0)+__syncwarp) vs L1075-L1079 dispatch -> ssu_checkpoint L861-L880 -> replay_state_mma L279 (reads full smem.state in every warp) at 2cf8f4cc; the barrier was inside ssu_nocheckpoint (L896) only
race_description: load_state_per_warp splits the DIM rows of smem.state across the 4 warps; each warp loads its quarter with cp.async and waits only for its own copies (__pipeline_wait_prior(0) + __syncwarp). replay_state_mma then uses a 1x4 tiled MMA in which every warp reads the full M extent of smem.state, i.e. rows loaded by other warps, with no __syncthreads between (the single barrier existed only on the no-checkpoint branch). So warp 0 can read rows warps 1-3 have not finished landing/committing.
fix_summary: Hoists one __syncthreads() out of ssu_nocheckpoint to the dispatch site in checkpointing_ssu_kernel, before `if (must_checkpoint)`, so both branches have cross-warp visibility; barrier count unchanged.
evidence: PR 3439: per-launch nondeterminism; hashing state/out over 5 launches with identical inputs gave 5 different hashes per config, state_diff up to ~13 in fp16 at batch=99; the fix adds test tests/mamba/test_checkpointing_ssu.py::test_checkpointing_ssu_determinism_across_launches (4 params: fp16/fp8 x checkpoint/no_checkpoint). No racecheck output quoted.
driver: tests/mamba/test_checkpointing_ssu.py at the fix commit (determinism test; run the test file from the fix commit against the buggy kernel header): flashinfer.mamba.checkpointing_ssu.checkpointing_ssu with nheads=16/32, head_dim=64, d_state=128, state fp16 (generic kernel only), prev_k=12 so that prev_k + seq_len > MAX_WINDOW (must_checkpoint=True), batch 2..99. kernel: BlockBatchReductionPersistent<KTraits>::Run (reduction stage of the persistent BatchAttention kernel)
location_buggy: include/flashinfer/attention/persistent.cuh:L519-L590 at 075775e4 (grid-stride loop over (packed_qo_idx, kv_head); cp.async prologue into v_smem L545-L551 and s_smem store L555 at the top of each iteration; previous iteration's warp_sync_state L581 -> warp_sync_state in state.cuh/cascade.cuh L139-L156 reads v_smem/s_smem of sibling lanes after one __syncwarp)
race_description: Each warp owns a private slice of v_smem/s_smem and loops over work items. The tail of an item (warp_sync_state, bdy > 1) has lanes read the partial results of the other lane rows from shared memory after a single __syncwarp; the next item immediately starts with cp.async writes into v_smem and a store to s_smem. Without a __syncwarp at the loop top, a lane that finished early can overwrite a row a sibling lane is still reading.
fix_summary: Adds __syncwarp() at the start of each iteration of the work loop (comment: 'avoid data hazard due to reordering st.cast_store').
evidence: PR 1826 title 'Bugfix: Fix data hazard in persistent reduce'; body only says 'Same as in PR 1661' (flashinfer-5). No log. Derived from code reading.
