build_notes: git clone --recursive https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer && git checkout <buggy_commit> && git submodule update --init --recursive; pip install -e . --no-build-isolation (JIT mode, no AOT needed). Kernels are built on first call by nvcc/ninja (JIT cache ~/.cache/flashinfer); export FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.9 to build only sm_89. This is nvcc JIT, not NVRTC, so the resulting .so/cubin can be run under the detector; run python under the detector (python -m pytest ... or a 20-line script). Needs a torch build matching the CUDA toolkit.
dispute_points: Intra-warp WAR; only matters when bdy > 1 and under independent thread scheduling; one-line fix with terse message, so the maintainers' own description of the hazard is vague ('reordering st.cast_store'). A skeptic may say lanes of one warp are lock-stepped; on Volta+ that is not guaranteed.

location_buggy: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/fattn-mma-f16.cuh near L877-L896 at df849192 (the __syncthreads added by PR 13438 is only executed by warps with threadIdx.y % np == 0)
race_description: __syncthreads() was executed only by the leader warps (threadIdx.y % np == 0). Hardware bar.sync counts arrivals, so the leader warps' barrier is satisfied by the non-leader warps' *next* (different) __syncthreads; from then on the warps wait at misaligned program points and shared-memory phases (write -> barrier -> read) are no longer ordered for long contexts.
fix_summary: Added `else if (np > 1) { __syncthreads(); }` so all warps execute the same number of barriers.
evidence: PR 13469: barrier 'only executed for part of the warps so the points at which warps wait for each other become misaligned. On a sufficiently long context this then causes incorrect results.' Not a sanitizer report. Related open issue 27678 (synccheck on the same pattern, still open for the other if/else instance at HEAD? -- fixed by b74f590e 'fix divergent barrier in f16 flash attention', see rejected.md).
driver: `compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck` or `--tool synccheck` on `test-backend-ops test -b CUDA0 -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT` (needs a long KV, e.g. kv=1024, so that multiple KV tiles misalign). Not verified which tool reports it.
dispute_points: Weak fit for the detector scope: the conflicting accesses are only indirectly unordered through misaligned barriers; the commit message says wrong results, not a sanitizer hazard. A sound race detector that models bar.sync by barrier id/arrival count might or might not flag it. Rank low.
build_notes: git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp && git checkout <buggy_commit>; cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89 -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release (add -DCMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS=-lineinfo for sanitizer line numbers); cmake --build build --target test-backend-ops -j (builds ggml-cuda only for sm_89; many template instances so ~10-25 min). Run: compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck build/bin/test-backend-ops test -b CUDA0 -o <OP> [-p '<regex over test vars>']. The CPU backend is used as reference, so no GPU model files are needed.

kernel: cub::DeviceRadixSort::SortPairs / SortPairsDescending, DeviceSegmentedRadixSort and DeviceSegmentedSort kernels, launched from argsort_f32_i32_cuda_cub with d_keys_in == d_keys_out == temp_keys
location_buggy: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/argsort.cu:L45-L156 at 60081bb2 (argsort_f32_i32_cuda_cub; the six sort calls at L88-L116 and L125-L155 pass `temp_keys, temp_keys // keys (in-place)`); CUB path taken when ncols > 1024 or the bitonic kernel's shared memory does not fit (L266-L273)
race_description: llama.cpp called the one-shot CUB device sorts with the same buffer as keys-in and keys-out. CUB's radix sort ping-pongs between the input and output key buffers across passes, and the fix's own code comment says the Device*Sort algorithms do not allow in-place sorting/aliasing; with aliased buffers one block can write the sorted keys of a pass to addresses another block of the same launch has not yet read (cross-block read/write conflict on global memory inside the CUB kernel), so the permutation comes out corrupted intermittently.
fix_summary: Allocates a distinct keys-out buffer (temp_keys_out) and passes it as the keys output in all six size-query and execution calls, with the comment that Device*Sort algorithms do not allow in-place sorting/aliasing.
evidence: PR 28389 commit text: with aliased buffers 'the sort partially overwrites its own input mid-pass' and returns a corrupted permutation, seen as intermittent garbage indices in backend top_k over a 248k-column vocab (Maxwell, CUDA 12.5, CCCL 2.x). Co-authored by a CUB maintainer (Oliver Simons), code comment states in-place is not allowed. The conflict analysis inside CUB is mine; no sanitizer log.
driver: `test-backend-ops test -b CUDA0 -o ARGSORT -p 'ne=\[2049,2,1,3\]'` (ncols > 1024 forces the CUB path; other cases from the test list: {1025,256,1,1}, {2048,512,1,1}, {65000,16,1,1}, {200000,1,1,1}; test_argsort vars are type, ne, order). Needs a build with GGML_CUDA_USE_CUB (default on CUDA >= 11 with CCCL). {2049,2,1,3} is 12k elements and a handful of CUB kernels, tiny.
build_notes: git checkout 60081bb2 && cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89 -DLLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=ON && cmake --build build --target test-backend-ops -j (use --target to avoid building everything; CUDA 13 compatibility of this 2026 tree is expected since upstream CI targets it, but unverified). The race is inside the CUB headers shipped with the toolkit (CCCL), so the CCCL version (toolkit-bundled; llama.cpp can pin CCCL since PR 29792) decides whether the aliasing misbehaves.
dispute_points: The conflicting accesses live in CUB library kernels, not llama.cpp code, and aliasing is API misuse that may happen to work for some CUB versions/sizes (the reporter saw it on Maxwell/CCCL 2.x). A detector would have to be able to instrument CUB's kernels (they are compiled into the llama.cpp binary). Radix-sort onesweep vs segmented-sort kernels behave differently; I did not establish which of the three CUB algorithms races for which size.

kernel: get_matching_group_value (extern "C" __device__ runtime function called from JIT-generated group-by kernels)
location_buggy: QueryEngine/cuda_mapd_rt.cu:L59-L75 at buggy_commit: winner does `memcpy(groups_buffer+off, key, ...)` and `memcpy(... init_vals ...)` L62-L65 after atomicCAS on the first key word; every thread then does `__syncthreads()` L67 and reads `groups_buffer[off+i]` L69-L74
race_description: Hash-table slot claim: the thread whose atomicCAS on the first key word succeeds then writes the whole key and the aggregate init values with plain stores. Losing threads (any thread of any block hashing to the same slot) skip the claim and immediately read the slot's key words to test for a match. The only 'synchronisation' is a block-level __syncthreads(), which orders neither threads of other blocks nor threads that did not reach the same barrier (it sits inside a function called from divergent code), and no fence publishes the winner's stores. Losers can see a half-written key or uninitialised aggregates.
fix_summary: Winner writes the middle key words with memcpy then publishes the LAST key word with atomicExch as a ready marker; a __threadfence() is issued and all threads spin with atomicAdd(...,0) on that last word until it is no longer EMPTY_KEY_64; the unsound __syncthreads() is removed.
evidence: Commit message: 'Fix synchronization in get_matching_group_value. Fixes #479.' (Alex Suhan, 2016-11-13). Issue number refers to the old pre-rename repository; the current heavyai/heavydb issue #479 is unrelated (TRANSLATE), so the original issue text is unverified.
driver: Full engine needs the HeavyDB server (high build cost, JIT). Cheap alternative: compile cuda_mapd_rt.cu's get_matching_group_value (needs EMPTY_KEY_64 from the headers) into a harness kernel where 32 blocks x 128 threads insert the same few multi-word keys (key_qw_count=2..3, row_size_quad=key_qw_count+2) into one groups_buffer and then check slots; ~1e5 accesses.
build_notes: Harness only: copy the function and the two defines (EMPTY_KEY_64 = 0xffff... ), no libraries. Race needs a multi-word key (key_qw_count>1) and two threads hashing to the same slot in different warps/blocks. Not compiled by me: unverified.
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream 2016).
dispute_points: Ranked low because the function is only reachable through JIT-generated kernels in the product (jit=true), 2016-era code that was later rewritten (get_matching_group_value moved to a different file and uses a different protocol). The harness proves the pattern, not the product path. Note the pre-fix __syncthreads() inside a device function called under divergence is itself a barrier-divergence hazard.

links: https://github.com/huggingface/candle/commit/f2ac5547fc12ae864d8647a67d4d7d0964714017 ('Avoid the race condition on cuda sums.': single-thread launch workaround 12 min earlier)
https://github.com/huggingface/candle/commit/f6104c4b6479891a90e340890cf0aee83fe1c633 (original 'Add the reduce-sum kernel.' with the plain +=)
kernel: sum_f32 / sum_f64 / sum_u32 (macro SUM_OP in reduce.cu)
location_buggy: kernels/src/reduce.cu:L26 (`out[dst_index] += inp[i];`, contiguous branch) and L39 (`out[dst_index] += inp[strided_i];`, strided branch) at buggy_commit
race_description: The sum kernel parallelises over input elements: each thread i computes the destination index dst_index of the reduced output and does `out[dst_index] += inp[i]`. All input elements along a reduced dimension map to the same dst_index, so many threads (of one or several blocks) perform a non-atomic read-modify-write on the same global word: a lost-update race. The first version (f6104c4b, 687c5beb) shipped this with the full grid; f2ac5547 hid it by launching a single thread; 3761f02a is the real fix (atomicAdd) and restores the parallel launch.
fix_summary: Replaces both `out[dst_index] += ...` with atomicAdd(out + dst_index, ...), adds a TODO to use a proper distributed reduction, and drops the 1-thread LaunchConfig hack in cuda_backend.rs (LaunchConfig::for_num_elems again).
evidence: Three commits on 2023-06-26 by Laurent Mazare: f2ac5547 message 'Avoid the race condition on cuda sums' (also fixes `post = dst_index / stride` -> `%`), then 3761f02a message 'Use atomicAdd as a quick workaround some cuda synchronisation issue'. No racecheck output; found by wrong results.
driver: No ready driver at that commit: cuda_basics example forces a 1-thread launch at buggy_commit (so the race is not exercised by the shipped host code). Write a ~40-line harness that nvcc-compiles reduce.cu (needs cuda_utils.cuh, compatibility.cuh, cuda_fp16.h) and launches sum_f32<<<1,8>>> for shape [4,2], sum dim 0: info = dims{4,2}, strides{2,1}, sum_dims_l{4}, sum_dims_s{2}; threads 0,2,4,6 all update out[0]. Tiny input.
build_notes: Kernel is plain CUDA (candle compiles it to PTX via build.rs/bindgen_cuda and loads it with cudarc, hence jit=true if the Rust path is used); with a custom harness use nvcc -arch=sm_89. Verified at buggy commit: dst-index math is correct (the `%` fix is already in f2ac5547) so no OOB confounds the race.
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream, same-day).
dispute_points: Fix is a same-day follow-up to a brand-new kernel, never in a release. Race is a plain float RMW (lost update), so also visible as wrong sums. The repo's own host code at buggy_commit launches a single thread, so a detector run through the shipped candle binary will see no race unless the launch config is patched; use the harness. If the harness is taken from 687c5beb instead, the `/` index bug adds out-of-bounds writes.

kernel: Pallas Mosaic GPU pipelined kernel generated by lower_jaxpr_to_module (test: test_add_one_grid_pipelined)
location_buggy: jax/_src/pallas/mosaic_gpu/lowering.py: pipelined fori loop around L449-L500 at 8599dbc9 (line numbers approximate; derived from the diff hunks, unverified against the blob)
race_description: The pipelining loop lets the compute threads write the next step's output window in shared memory without first waiting for the asynchronous (TMA) copy that stores the previous use of the same output slot to global memory. With max_concurrent_steps > 1 and a sequential grid dimension, the async-proxy read of the smem output slot is unordered against the generic-proxy writes of the next iteration that reuses the slot.
fix_summary: Adds launch_ctx.await_async_copy(max_concurrent_steps - 1) before the kernel body writes the output window; also renames num_stages to max_concurrent_steps and fixes the test (grid 2x4, steps 1..4).
evidence: Commit message: 'We never checked if the output windows are done writing before we reused them.' Test change: test_add_one_grid_pipelined now parameterised by max_concurrent_steps in [1,2,3,4] with grid (2,4).
driver: pytest tests/pallas/mosaic_gpu_test.py -k test_add_one_grid_pipelined (output 256x64 f32, a few thousand accesses).
build_notes: Needs a jax/jaxlib build with Mosaic GPU at the buggy commit (Sept 2024) and an sm_90 GPU (TMA, Hopper-only path). The kernel is JIT-generated MLIR->PTX, not an nvcc source. Racy accesses involve the TMA (async proxy) read of smem, which the detector may not model. Rank low for the 4060 Ti cluster.
dispute_points: Async-proxy (TMA store) vs generic-proxy race; the detector would need to treat cp.async.bulk reads as accesses. The commit author notes the old test passed for reasons he did not understand (it did not write all output entries), i.e. the race was found by inspection, not by a sanitizer. Not reproducible on sm_89.

kernel: KokkosBatched::TeamVectorHouseholderInternal::invoke and TeamVectorQR_WithColumnPivotingInternal::invoke (batched team+vector level QR; run inside a user TeamPolicy kernel)
location_buggy: src/batched/KokkosBatched_Householder_TeamVector_Internal.hpp:L63-L70 at the buggy commit (the TeamVectorRange parallel_for 'x2[i*x2s] *= inv_chi1_minus_alpha' with no following team_barrier); src/batched/KokkosBatched_QR_WithColumnPivoting_TeamVector_Internal.hpp near L96 and L172 (norm update loops without barrier)
race_description: The team-vector loop scales x2 (and the column-norm update loop rewrites the norm array) element-wise across the team's threads and the function proceeds, or returns to the caller, which then reads x2 / the norms written by other threads, without a team barrier. When the team has many more threads than vector lanes (spans several warps) the reader can run before the writer.
fix_summary: Adds member.team_barrier() after the x2 scaling in the Householder routine and after the two norm computations in the pivoted QR; the commit also generalises UTV/SolveUTV/SetIdentity to m x n matrices.
evidence: Commit message (P. Kuberry, 2020-12-03): added some team_barrier()s to QR and Householder algorithms to eliminate a race condition exposed when threads per team >> vector lanes. Mixed with feature work (m x n support, a 10x threshold change).
driver: unit_test/batched/Test_Batched_TeamVectorQR_WithColumnPivoting.hpp, Test_Batched_TeamVectorUTV.hpp and Test_Batched_TeamVectorSolveUTV.hpp on Cuda, using a team size larger than the vector length (e.g. team_size 32+, vector_length 1-4); small batches (tens of matrices of 4x4..16x16).
build_notes: Kokkos with CUDA sm_89, then kokkos-kernels with batched unit tests only (-DKokkosKernels_ENABLE_TESTS=ON and restrict ETI); parent is 2db7b62d82d442edef56915b7e38f90e18e4b507. Heavy template instantiation: expect tens of minutes.
already_reported_check: Not searched on GitHub issues.
dispute_points: The exact conflicting accesses are inferred (commit names the symptom but not the accesses); the commit mixes functional changes with the barriers; the global-memory space is assumed (Householder operates on user-provided views, which may live in scratch) so the 'space' field may be shared for some callers.

location_buggy: src/treelearner/cuda/cuda_histogram_constructor.cu:L406 at fe267372 (`shared_hist_packed = global_hist_buffer + (blockIdx.y*num_total_bin + partition_column_start)`), zeroing at L407-L410, atomicAdd_block accumulation in the following loop
race_description: Each blockIdx.x owns a slice [partition_hist_start, partition_hist_end) of the global histogram buffer, but the slice base was computed with partition_column_start (a column index) instead of partition_hist_start (a bin index). Slices of neighbouring blockIdx.x therefore overlap: block x zeroes its `shared_hist_packed[i]=0` region with plain stores and accumulates with atomicAdd_block (block-scope atomics) while block x+1 does the same on partly the same words. Plain store vs block-scoped atomic from a different block = cross-block conflict with no ordering.
fix_summary: One-token change: use partition_hist_start instead of partition_column_start, like the three sibling kernels.
evidence: Commit message: kernel 'mis-based its shared_hist_packed pointer'; the two quantities coincide only if every column had exactly one bin; affects dense + use_quantized_grad + USE_GLOBAL_MEM_BUFFER dispatch. No mention of 'race' - consequence is corrupted histograms.
driver: Python: lightgbm built with -DUSE_CUDA=ON; lgb.train({'device_type':'cuda','use_quantized_grad':True,'num_leaves':...,'max_bin':255}, dense data with many features/bins so the global-memory histogram buffer path is chosen (USE_GLOBAL_MEM_BUFFER dispatch ~L615 of the .cu), e.g. 10^4 rows x 100+ features. Exact dispatch condition (shared-memory limit) unverified. A regression test is claimed by the commit message but not in the diff (unverified).
build_notes: cmake -B build -DUSE_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89 ; build lightgbm lib + python package from source at fe267372. Needs the global-memory buffer path forced (many features*bins exceeding shared mem per block).
dispute_points: Root cause is an address-arithmetic (wrong offset) bug, which the brief lists as another class (wrong results from math errors). The race is a consequence of aliasing between per-block slices; a skeptic can say it is an indexing bug, not a synchronization bug. Detector would flag it as a cross-block WAW/RAW because blocks overlap. Low confidence as a 'race' target.

kernel: ScanTileState<T,false>::WaitForValid (decoupled look-back consumer, used by DeviceScan / device reduce-by-key for non-primitive value types)
location_buggy: cub/agent/single_pass_scan_operators.cuh:L412-L425 at buggy_commit (ScanTileState<T,false>::WaitForValid polls the status byte with ThreadLoad<LOAD_CG>, then loads d_tile_partial or d_tile_inclusive); producer side SetInclusive L381 and SetPartial L397 (store value, __threadfence, store status); the same file's ReduceByKeyScanTileState<...,false> inherits this class
race_description: Producer tile publishes its partial/inclusive value with a plain ld/st.cg store, a __threadfence and then the status flag. The consumer (look-back of a later tile) polls the status flag and then loads the value from a different address with no fence between the two loads, so nothing orders the value load after the flag load (weak, unordered relaxed loads to different addresses) and the consumer can observe a stale value for a status that says PARTIAL/INCLUSIVE. This is the consumer-side half of the flag/value hand-off; the producer side already had its fence.
fix_summary: WaitForValid in the non-single-word variant now calls __threadfence() after each status load inside the polling loop, so the later value loads cannot be hoisted above the status load. The same commit also rewrites the polling loop of the single-word variants (ScanTileState<T,true> and ReduceByKeyScanTileState<...,true>) to add __threadfence_block() as a 'prevent hoisting loads from loop' compiler barrier; that change is about hoisting, not an inter-thread race, and is not part of the candidate.
evidence: Commit title 'add fence to single-pass lookback scan operator'; the added inline comment says the fence prevents hoisting loads from the loop or loads below being moved above the status load. No issue, no sanitizer report; whether the stale read ever occurred in practice is unverified. Modern cccl replaced these loads with explicit relaxed/acquire loads (details unverified).
driver: cub::DeviceScan::InclusiveScan (or ExclusiveScan) with a NON-primitive value type so that ScanTileState<T,false> is selected (SINGLE_WORD = Traits<T>::PRIMITIVE at the buggy commit), e.g. a user struct of three ints with a custom + functor, on about 1M items: 1M items / ~4K items per tile is a few hundred tiles, every tile's look-back polls once or a few times; far below 1e8 accesses. cub::DeviceReduce::ReduceByKey with a KeyValuePair also reaches the same tile-state class.
build_notes: Requires the archived Dec-2015 NVIDIA/cub checkout (CUB 1.5.x). That code predates Volta: the non-.sync shuffle/vote inline PTX and sm_20/sm_30 specializations are very unlikely to assemble for sm_89 under CUDA 13 without porting (unverified, not tried). The race can alternatively be studied by mutation on current cccl: delete the acquire in the corresponding look-back wait and run the scan.
dispute_points: The commit does not say a race was observed and mixes in an unrelated compiler-hoisting workaround; under the original author's mental model (volatile-like ld.cg plus producer-side fence) the stale-value outcome may have been a theoretical hazard only. Weak ld.cg flag polling is not a morally-strong access in the PTX model, so a detector must decide whether it counts the missing acquire as a race. Code is 2015-era and pre-Volta.

kernel: cub::BlockExchange::BlockedToWarpStriped and WarpStripedToBlocked (non-time-sliced and warp-time-sliced specializations)
location_buggy: cub/block/block_exchange.cuh:L281-L300 (BlockedToWarpStriped, no time slicing: write loop then read loop on temp_storage, no sync between), L305-L333 (time-sliced variant, same pattern inside 'if (warp_id == SLICE)'), L426-L445 and L451-L479 (WarpStripedToBlocked, same two shapes) at buggy_commit
race_description: In a warp-striped exchange each lane writes ITEMS_PER_THREAD items into the warp's slice of shared memory at lane*ITEMS_PER_THREAD+ITEM and then reads items written by other lanes of the same warp at ITEM*32+lane. The write loop and read loop use plain (non-volatile) shared memory accesses with no intervening warp barrier, relying on lockstep execution; nothing orders a lane's read after the other lanes' writes (a compiler or the hardware under independent thread scheduling can reorder them).
fix_summary: Inserted __threadfence_block() between the write loop and the read loop in all four warp-level exchange paths (two in BlockedToWarpStriped, two in WarpStripedToBlocked). The other parts of the commit (block scan raking WAW-hazard cleanup, warp scan prefix-callback removal) are unrelated. Current cccl uses __syncwarp(0xffffffff) at the same point (cub/cub/block/block_exchange.cuh L302 at cccl HEAD, in BlockedToWarpStriped).
evidence: Commit message first bullet: 'Fix race in warp-blocked/strided exchange' (author dumerrill, 2014-05-29). A fence rather than a barrier was added, so the original concern appears to be memory ordering of warp-synchronous accesses; no sanitizer output or issue found.
driver: A tiny kernel using cub::BlockExchange<int,128,4> BlockedToWarpStriped on one block of 128 threads with the archived cub checkout; trivial size. On current cccl the corresponding code already has __syncwarp, so the buggy form can only be reproduced from the archive or by mutation (delete the __syncwarp in block_exchange.cuh L302 and run).
build_notes: Archived May-2014 cub (CUB 1.2.x era) predates Volta and CUDA 9; building it for sm_89 with CUDA 13 is probably impossible without porting (unverified, not tried). Mutating current cccl is the cheap route.
dispute_points: A __threadfence_block in the fix suggests the issue was compiler/hardware reordering of non-volatile shared accesses within a warp under pre-Volta lockstep, not necessarily an actual race on contemporary GPUs; under Volta ITS the proper repair is a warp barrier, which is what cccl later used. Evidence is the commit title alone.

kernel: cuco::detail::find_all<block_size,tile_size,buffer_size,...> (static_multimap::find_all) with shared-memory output_buffer + block_counter and flush_output_buffer
location_buggy: include/cuco/detail/static_multimap_kernels.cuh:L561 (per-thread outer loop condition `while (first + key_idx < last)`), L568-L630 (inner loop with __syncthreads_or/__syncthreads/flush), L634-L637 (final remainder flush reading block_counter/output_buffer), flush_output_buffer L41-L55, at buggy_commit
race_description: In the last (partially populated) thread block, some tiles have first+key_idx >= last and leave the outer while loop immediately, while other tiles of the same block are still probing and appending matches to the shared output_buffer (atomicAdd_block on block_counter, then plain writes into output_buffer). The early-exited threads proceed to the 'final remainder flush' which reads block_counter and output_buffer[...] and calls flush_output_buffer, whose __syncthreads() pairs with a barrier the other threads execute at a different program point (the __syncthreads_or/__syncthreads in the inner loop). The exited threads therefore read and copy the shared buffer before the producing threads have finished/ordered their writes, and the buffer contents/count get flushed twice or truncated.
fix_summary: Two commits on 2021-05-12: d67b14560 makes the outer loop block-uniform (`while (__syncthreads_or(first+key_idx < last))`, `running` initialised from the bounds check, key/slot only read when running); the follow-up e806f2698 hoists key/current_slot out of the inner loop (the first commit left current_slot out of scope at the next_slot call) and guards next_slot with `if (running)`. Use e806f2698 as the compilable fixed tree, e7bf44b as the buggy tree.
evidence: Commit messages: 'Fix sync bug in the very last block in find_all' and 'Fix the last block sync bug in find_all'. No issue, no sanitizer output; judged from the code diff. Likely found when find_all returned wrong results for sizes where the last block is partial.
driver: tests/static_multimap/static_multimap_test.cu (find_all cases) or a ~40-line program: cuco::static_multimap<int,int> with ~1e4 inserted pairs, find_all over a number of keys that is not a multiple of the block size so the last block has idle tiles. Tiny input.
build_notes: This is a 2021 tree: needs libcudacxx (cuda::atomic) fetched via CPM/CMake at that era's version, which may not compile against CUDA 13's bundled libcu++ and C++17-era headers; budget some porting time (drop CMake, use -I to a recent libcudacxx may or may not work). Not compiled here.
dispute_points: This is a barrier-divergence bug: the hardware bar.sync pairs the mismatched barriers by count, so a happens-before-based detector that treats every bar.sync 0 as a global barrier will NOT see unordered accesses; it may only be caught by a divergence/synccheck-style check or by the effect of the real schedule. No sanitizer evidence and the commit message does not call it a race. Keep as a low-priority 'detector fidelity' case.

kernel: nvf::scan::blockScan, nvf::argsort::blockArgsort, nvf::topk::blockTopK (device functions in nvFuser's NVRTC runtime, called from generated kernels)
location_buggy: runtime/scan.cu:L92 (static __shared__ BlockScan::TempStorage temp_storage), L95 (InclusiveScan), function ends L106 with no barrier; runtime/argsort.cu:L76 (temp_storage), L93/L95 (SortDescending/Sort); runtime/topk.cu:L91 (temp_storage), L110/L113 (SortDescending/Sort) at buggy_commit
race_description: Each runtime helper declares a function-scope __shared__ cub TempStorage (one instance per template instantiation, so every call of the same helper in one generated kernel reuses it) and returns without a trailing __syncthreads(). When the generated kernel calls the same helper repeatedly (e.g. chained scans, or argsort/topk in a loop), warps that finish reading the first call's TempStorage race with fast warps that already write it for the next call. This is the documented CUB requirement of a barrier between reuse of a collective's TempStorage.
fix_summary: Append __syncthreads() ('make sure the work buffer can be freely used again') at the end of blockScan, blockArgsort and blockTopK; adds C++ tests ScanTest.BufferSync (three chained scans of 4096 floats, 1024 threads), and analogous argsort/topk tests.
evidence: PR 5252 (Naoya Maruyama): CUB routines do not sync on the shared work buffer at the end; repeated calls to the same routine may cause a write-after-read hazard; fix inserts a syncthreads at the end of each CUB-based function.
driver: nvFuser C++ gtests added by the fix: tests/cpp/test_scan.cpp ScanTest.BufferSync (3 chained scans over 4096 floats, TIDx=1024 with group 4), tests/cpp/test_argsort.cpp and tests/cpp/test_topk.cpp analogues (names unverified). Alternatively a stand-alone nvcc harness: include runtime/cub_utils.cu + runtime/scan.cu from the buggy checkout and call nvf::scan::blockScan three times in one 1024-thread kernel with matching template parameters (BlockDimT can be a dummy type).
build_notes: The nvFuser test binary needs PyTorch/libtorch and a full nvFuser build (high). The stand-alone harness only needs nvcc with CCCL/CUB from the CUDA 13 toolkit and the three runtime/*.cu files (they are plain device code in namespace nvf, with a small cub_utils helper); expect to adapt includes. Because nvFuser itself compiles these through NVRTC at runtime the in-product path is JIT, hence jit=true.
dispute_points: The author says repeated calls 'may' hazard and that single-use cases are safe; so the race only exists in kernels that call the same helper more than once (the added test does). Which instruction pair racecheck flags depends on the CUB algorithm (BLOCK_SCAN_RAKING warp storage vs raking segments; radix sort exchange buffers). The hazard follows the documented CUB reuse rule rather than a sanitizer log.

kernel: warp::warpReduceTIDX<SINGLE_WARP,Aligned,T,Func> (nvFuser runtime, called from generated reduction kernels)
location_buggy: runtime/warp.cu:L24-L86 at buggy_commit: warp 0 reads shared_mem[smem_offset + lane_idx] at L71 inside 'if (warp_idx == 0)'; the function returns after L80-L82 with no barrier, while warps 1..n-1 fall through immediately
race_description: After the per-warp partial results are written to shared_mem (L61, barrier L64), only warp 0 reads them back (L71). Warps other than warp 0 leave warpReduceTIDX without waiting, and the generated kernel can continue to code that reuses the same shared-memory workspace (the next reduction or broadcast using the same buffer) and write it while warp 0 is still reading the partial sums.
fix_summary: Add block_sync::sync<Aligned>() at the end of the !SINGLE_WARP branch, with the comment that otherwise other warps may access shared memory before this reduction is done.
evidence: PR 489 (Liqiang Lu, 2023-06-13): 'add sync to warp reduction runtime avoid smem data race', solves issue 271 (issue page not read). Added comment: needs sync, otherwise other warps may access shared memory before this reduction is done.
driver: Issue 271 (not read) holds the original failing fusion; any nvFuser reduction over threadIdx.x with more than one warp that is followed by generated code reusing the same shared workspace. A stand-alone harness on runtime/warp.cu (stub block_sync) must follow the call with a non-barrier consumer of shared_mem, because a second call to warpReduceTIDX itself starts with a barrier (L58) and would not race.
build_notes: nvFuser at mid-2023 requires PyTorch and NVRTC; not buildable with a CUDA 13 toolchain without effort. Treat as a stand-alone extraction target only.
dispute_points: Mechanism is generic: the function itself is internally consistent because a repeated call to warpReduceTIDX begins with its own barrier (L58); the race requires generated code that reuses the buffer outside this helper, which I could not verify (issue 271 unread). 2023 code, runtime is NVRTC-compiled.

kernel: grid_sync::blockSerializeWait / blockSerializeRelease (split-K serial reduction via semaphore)
location_buggy: runtime/grid_sync.cu:L193-L225 at buggy_commit: blockSerializeRelease does '__syncthreads(); semaphoreRelease(semaphore, ...)' (L223-L224) where semaphoreRelease is a thread-0 'st.global.release.gpu.b64' (L164-L173) and semaphoreWait spins with 'ld.global.acquire.gpu.b64' on thread 0 (L175-L191)
race_description: In serial split-K, block k+1 must observe the global-memory writes (tensor T3 partials) made by all threads of block k after it acquires the semaphore. The release path only issues __syncthreads() (CTA-scope) before thread 0 stores the semaphore, with no gpu-scope __threadfence; the maintainers state that writes from threads other than thread 0 are then not guaranteed visible to the next block, so block k+1 can read stale T3 and compute an invalid update.
fix_summary: Add __threadfence() before the __syncthreads() in blockSerializeRelease (with a long explanatory comment).
evidence: PR 2391 (Jacob Hinkle, 2024-06-12): prior to this there could be a data race during split-K reduction; cites the similar missing fence reported in pytorch PR 128455; gridReduce already has the fence inside grid_sync::sync, so only split-K was affected.
driver: nvFuser split-K matmul tests (tests/cpp/test_matmul.cpp with splitk serial reduction; exact test name unverified) or a stand-alone harness: runtime/grid_sync.cu (needs index_utils/block_sync stubs) with a kernel where blocks serialise via blockSerializeWait/Release and each does T[i] += x for all threads over a few hundred elements.
build_notes: Full nvFuser needs PyTorch + NVRTC. The stand-alone harness is easier: compile runtime/grid_sync.cu pieces with nvcc -arch=sm_89 and 2-8 blocks.
dispute_points: Under the PTX memory model a bar.sync followed by a thread-0 st.release.gpu is cumulative, so a model-precise checker may call the buggy version correct; the maintainers (and PyTorch PR 128455) treat the missing __threadfence as a real race. A detector that only credits per-thread fences will flag it. The race is also not observable on typical hardware.

location_buggy: megatron/core/fusions/fused_mla_yarn_rope_apply.py:L139-L159 (fwd: loads at interleaved offsets L144-L147, stores at split offsets L156-L159) and L235-L256 (bwd: loads at split offsets L245-L248, stores at interleaved offsets L255-L256) at ef8cd10b
race_description: The in-place Q-RoPE kernels load a [BLOCK_H, emb_dim/2] tile of x1/x2 in one layout (interleaved in fwd, split halves in bwd) and store the rotated result into the SAME Q/DO buffer in the other layout. The source and destination element sets overlap, but with several warps (num_warps>1, e.g. BLOCK_H=1 with num_warps=8, or BLOCK_H=2 with num_warps=4) the elements are distributed over different warps, so a warp's store can hit an address that another warp has not loaded yet (global-memory WAR across warps of one program/CTA). Triton emits no barrier between the loads and the stores.
fix_summary: Inserts tl.debug_barrier() (a CTA-wide bar.sync) between the loads and the aliasing stores in both kernels; also moves triton.autotune outside the jit function so the test can launch the raw kernel with a fixed BLOCK_H/num_warps.
evidence: Commit title 'Fix fused MLA Q-RoPE in-place load/store races (#5963)'; added comments say the interleaved and split layouts alias and all loads must finish before any warp stores. New test test_rotary_q_inplace_conversion_loads_before_stores launches the kernel 100-200 times with a multi-warp config and requires bit-exact equality with a single-warp control. No sanitizer log.
driver: tests/unit_tests/fusions/test_mla_yarn_rope_apply.py::test_rotary_q_inplace_conversion_loads_before_stores (added by the fix; at the buggy commit use the public wrapper megatron.core.fusions.fused_mla_yarn_rope_apply.fused_apply_mla_rope_for_q / fused_mla_rope_inplace, whose autotune picks BLOCK_H, or copy the test and call _mla_rope_fwd_inplace_kernel.fn). Input: total_seqlen=128 tokens, 32 heads, nope dim 128, emb_dim 128 (fwd) or 64 (bwd), bf16; about 1e6 element accesses.
build_notes: Needs only Python, torch (CUDA) and triton (pip), plus the Megatron-LM source tree at the buggy commit (pip install -e . is not required for the single module if megatron.core imports resolve; the test imports megatron.core.utils and tests.unit_tests.test_utilities, so the repo checkout with its dependencies such as transformer_engine may be needed (unverified): a standalone script that imports only fused_mla_yarn_rope_apply.py is simpler). Triton JIT compiles to PTX/SASS at run time, so the detector must attach to the JIT-compiled cubin (jit: true). Runs on sm_89.
dispute_points: Triton kernel, not nvcc; the race is a compiler-level one (Triton's layout conversion does not synchronise loads against later aliasing stores). Whether it triggers depends on the Triton version and chosen layout (the authors needed 100-200 repeats at specific BLOCK_H/num_warps), so the detector may see no race on a given build; the bug is 4 days old at the pin and tied to the layout Triton chooses, not to the Python source alone.

kernel: block_reduce_sum2_for<kReduceWarps> and block_reduce_sum2_active_for<kReduceWarps> (device helpers used by kda_decode_fusion_compact_heads_kernel and kda_decode_fusion_many_heads_kernel)
location_buggy: cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/kdaDecode/kdaDecodeLegacy.cu:L270-L283 (block_reduce_sum2_for) and L344-L357 (block_reduce_sum2_active_for) at af645b78
race_description: In the second stage of the block reduction warp 0 lanes read the per-warp partials scratch[lane] and scratch[kReduceWarps+lane] (lane < kReduceWarps, i.e. lanes 0..3 for kDimK=128), warp-reduce them, and then lane 0 writes the result to scratch[0] and scratch[1]. scratch[1] is read by lane 1 and written by lane 0 of the same warp with no __syncwarp between the read and the write, so on Volta+ (independent thread scheduling) the formal order of lane 0's store against lane 1's load is not guaranteed.
fix_summary: Adds __syncwarp() before the 'if (lane == 0)' stores in both helpers (comment: lane 0 overwrites partials that other lanes of this warp read above).
evidence: Commit title '[None][fix] kdaDecode legacy: __syncwarp before the lane-0 block-reduce stores (#19830)'; code comment added by the fix says lane 0 overwrites partials other lanes read. No sanitizer log, no linked issue.
driver: tests/unittest/_torch/modules/kimi_kda/test_kda_decode_op.py drives the Python op that dispatches kdaDecode (BATCH_SIZE=73, NUM_HEADS=96, HEAD_DIM=128, bf16), but the test is skipped unless is_kda_optimized_supported() (SM100/SM103), so on sm_89 a small standalone C++/CUDA harness calling the launcher in cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/kdaDecode/kdaDecodeDispatcher.cpp / kdaDecode.h is needed (signature unverified). One CTA of 256 threads per (batch, value head); a few 1e6 accesses at B*HV=100.
build_notes: Full TensorRT-LLM build is heavy; practical route is to compile kdaDecodeLegacy.cu on its own with nvcc -arch=sm_89 -I cpp -I <tensorrt_llm include/cuda deps> and a hand-written main() (unverified: the file includes tensorrt_llm common headers and launchWithPdlWhenEnabled, PDL launch attribute is a no-op unless enabled). The legacy kernel uses cp.async state prefetch.
dispute_points: Weak as a real race: both warp_reduce_sum() shuffles (full-mask __shfl_xor_sync) sit between lane 1's read and lane 0's write and consume the loaded values, so in hardware every lane has already completed its load before lane 0 can proceed; a detector that models shfl_sync as converging the warp will not flag it, and one that only credits __syncwarp will. The authors added the barrier for formal correctness. Dispatch to this kernel in the public Python path is Blackwell only.

links: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3630 (FlashInfer copy of the same fix, commit 0b727e676ad0d7504000813601d2ef88ae4881c7)
kernel: tinygemm_kernel (small-M bf16 GEMM, 384 threads/CTA, TMA cp.async.bulk.tensor producer warp + mbarrier-gated consumer warps)
location_buggy: cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/tinygemm2/tinygemm2_kernel.cuh:L341-L371 at d202244d (bar_ptr_wt/bar_ptr_act captured for `stage` at L341-L342; polling loop `while (!weight_ready || !act_ready)` L359-L363 re-polls those captured barriers, while L370-L371 pre-polls the next stage's barriers; consumers then read sh_weights/sh_activations of that stage L377-L378)
race_description: Producer warp fills each pipeline stage's shared-memory weight/activation tile with TMA bulk copies that signal an mbarrier. Consumer warps pre-poll the NEXT stage's barriers once (L370-L371) and, if that single try_wait failed, the spin loop at the next iteration re-polls the barrier pointers captured for the CURRENT stage instead of the next one, so the wait no longer guards the next stage's tile (barrier of the wrong stage, possibly with a mismatching parity) and the consumer may read the next stage's tile before the TMA write has landed (RAW between the async-proxy write and the consumer's shared-memory reads).
fix_summary: Recomputes the barrier addresses from the current stage inside the spin loop (`bar_try_wait(__cvta_generic_to_shared(&bar_wt_ready[stage]), phase)`) instead of reusing the stale captured pointers.
evidence: Commit title '[None][fix] fix tinygemm barrier bug (#15338)', a 2-line change; the FlashInfer mirror (#3630) thanks a user for a detailed reproduction script and says it fixes a barrier bug. The pre-poll/stale-pointer reading is mine from the code. Related earlier fix 6c2ecad2f is a PDL change and is not the same bug.
driver: tests/unittest/_torch/thop/parallel/test_tinygemm2.py (torch op tinygemm2; the kernel body is compiled only for __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900, so sm_90 hardware is required); small M (<= 16 tokens) with N,K of a router GEMM (e.g. K=7168, N=256, unverified), a few 1e6 accesses.
build_notes: Needs a TensorRT-LLM python build (or the FlashInfer JIT copy csrc/tinygemm2.cu at flashinfer 0b727e67^; `pip install flashinfer` at a commit before #3630 and call the tinygemm2 op through its JIT module, op name unverified). Hopper/Blackwell only; cannot run on the RTX 4060 Ti.
dispute_points: Race is between the TMA engine (async proxy) and ordinary shared loads, mediated by mbarrier waits; a thread-level race detector that does not model cp.async.bulk completion cannot see it. The failure needs the next-stage barrier not to be complete at the pre-poll, which depends on timing, so it was intermittent. Earlier fix 6c2ecad2f touches the same kernel but only reorders the PDL trigger.

location_buggy: transformer_engine/common/cast/mxfp8/quantize_mxfp8.cuh at 0c2e7b09: dbias epilogue L497-L528: 'float *partial_dbias_rowwise = reinterpret_cast<float *>(dshmem)' reuses the dynamic shared buffer (in_sh) with generic stores at L519 and __syncthreads at L522, but the preceding TMA operations (cp.async.bulk shared->global stores issued L479-L490, and shared-buffer prefetch) may still be reading/writing dshmem; group_quantize_mxfp8.cuh:L713-L720 same pattern
race_description: After the main loop the kernel reuses the TMA staging buffer dshmem (also holding data that an outstanding cp.async.bulk tensor store is still reading) as the row-wise dbias reduction buffer and writes partial dbias values into it with ordinary stores. No wait on the bulk-async group and no barrier precedes the first store, so generic-proxy writes can overwrite shared bytes the async proxy has not finished reading (and other threads' dbias stores race with each other's earlier uses).
fix_summary: Inserts ptx::cp_async_bulk_wait_group_read<0>() followed by __syncthreads() before reusing dshmem as the dbias buffer (both kernels).
evidence: Commit title: 'Fix the race in the dbias computation in MXFP8 quantization and grouped quantization kernel (#2921)'; no body or sanitizer output.
driver: TransformerEngine C++ tests: tests/cpp/operator/test_cast_mxfp8.cu (dbias variants) and test_cast_mxfp8_grouped.cu; or PyTorch MXFP8 quantize with return of dbias (te.pytorch.tex.bgrad_quantize) on H100/B200. MXFP8 kernels need TMA (sm_90+); sm_89 cannot run them.
build_notes: TE C++ tests need CMake build of libtransformer_engine + tests (cuDNN, cuBLASLt deps), hours. H100 required (needs_sm90). The detector must model cp.async.bulk completion (async proxy) - probably unsupported, so rank low.
dispute_points: Async-proxy vs generic-proxy hazard; a thread-level detector without TMA modelling may see only a missing __syncthreads. The original may be a very rare race.

kernel: transformer_engine::quantize_fp8_kernel<...> (FP8 cast with TMA staging, FP8_BUFFERS_NUM ring) and the gated/MXFP8/NVFP4 siblings
location_buggy: transformer_engine/common/cast/fp8/quantize_fp8.cuh at 7e7898fa: out_sh[buff][...] written by all threads at L181 in iteration k+B; TMA store of out_sh[buff] issued by master thread only (L190-L195) and only the master waits with cp_async_bulk_wait_group_read<FP8_PREFETCH_BUFFERS_NUM>() (L201); no barrier after the wait, so other threads proceed to overwrite the ring slot
race_description: The output staging ring in shared memory is drained to global memory by TMA bulk stores issued (and waited for) only by the master thread. The wait only guarantees the master thread observed that the async-proxy stopped reading a given buffer; the other 100+ threads write the next iteration's results into that same ring slot without any barrier after the master's wait, so their generic stores can overwrite data the TMA engine is still reading.
fix_summary: After the master thread's wait, adds __syncthreads() (when the ring can be reused: next_iter >= BUFFERS_NUM) so all writers are ordered after the wait; changes the wait depth to BUFFERS_NUM-1; replaces the trailing cp_async_bulk_wait_group_read<0> by a master-thread cp_async_bulk_wait_group + __syncthreads; adds a 'memory' clobber on fence_acquire_tensormap. Same pattern fixed in 20 kernels.
evidence: PR 3417 'Fix TMA synchronization in quantization kernels' (commit messages 'Fix TMA shared-memory reuse synchronization', 'Fix remaining TMA synchronization gaps'); the added comment: 'The bulk async-group is owned by the issuing thread. Hand its completion off to all cooperative writers before the output ring can be reused.' No sanitizer output.
driver: TransformerEngine C++ tests tests/cpp/operator/test_cast_*.cu (FP8/MXFP8/NVFP4 cast, gated) or PyTorch Float8Quantizer on H100. Needs sm_90 (TMA); NVFP4 kernels need sm_100.
build_notes: Build libtransformer_engine + C++ tests (cuDNN/cuBLASLt/NVSHMEM-optional), hours; requires H100. Detector must understand cp.async.bulk async proxy completion to see this race, which is likely unsupported -> low rank.
dispute_points: Async-proxy (TMA) vs generic-proxy race; at thread level the missing relation is 'barrier after master's wait'. Hard to observe dynamically.

kernel: HadamardAmaxTmaKernel (RHT amax, ping-pong TMA-loaded shared buffers)
location_buggy: transformer_engine/common/hadamard_transform/hadamard_transform.cu:L251-L301 at buggy_commit: TMA prefetch of the next stage into in_shs[next_stage % 2] (L259-L266), ptx::fence_proxy_async_shared_cta() at L269 placed BEFORE mbarrier_wait_parity (L272), generic reads of in_shs[stage % 2] in the compute loops (L283-L299), __syncthreads at L300; kernel compiled only for __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 1000 (L188)
race_description: Two shared buffers are ping-ponged between TMA writes (async proxy) and generic-proxy reads by the compute warps. The proxy fence that must separate the generic reads of a buffer from the next TMA write into that buffer was issued before the mbarrier wait of the current stage instead of after the compute and __syncthreads, so a TMA write for a later stage can overtake still-pending generic reads of the same buffer (cross-proxy WAR).
fix_summary: Remove the fence_proxy_async_shared_cta() before the mbarrier wait and add it after the compute loop's __syncthreads ('ensure generic shared-memory accesses are visible before the next TMA write'), in all three Hadamard amax kernels.
evidence: Commit/PR 2695 (Kirthi Shankar Sivamani): 'Fix race condition in HadamardAmaxTmaKernel'; the diff moves the proxy fence. No racecheck output.
driver: TransformerEngine NVFP4 RHT amax path (python/tests for NVFP4 quantization with random Hadamard transform, or C++ tests/cpp/operator hadamard tests; exact test unverified) on a Blackwell GPU (sm_100+ only: the kernel body is guarded by __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 1000, so it cannot run on sm_89 or H100).
build_notes: Needs TransformerEngine build with CUDA >= 12.8 for sm_100; not runnable on the RTX 4060 Ti nor the H100.
dispute_points: Cross-proxy (TMA vs generic) hazard that a CUDA-core race detector may not model; sm_100-only; mechanism inferred from the diff (no sanitizer log).

kernel: wp::tile_register_t<T,M,N>::extract(i,j) - runtime header compiled into user @wp.kernel code by NVRTC (wp.tile_extract / tile[i,j])
location_buggy: warp/native/tile.h:L230-L249 at 1e039fd3 (WP_TILE_SHARED Type scratch; thread 'thread' writes scratch=data[reg] at L243; all threads read it after WP_TILE_SYNC at L246-L248; no sync before the write)
race_description: extract() writes one value into a single static shared slot 'scratch' by the owning thread, syncs, then every thread returns scratch. When extract() is called repeatedly (e.g. in a loop over elements), a thread racing ahead into the next call can overwrite scratch while slower threads of the previous call have not yet read it, because there is no barrier between the read at return and the next call's write.
fix_summary: Adds a WP_TILE_SYNC() before the owning thread writes scratch ('ensure any previously scheduled threads have finished reading from scratch').
evidence: Commit message: 'Fix for shared memory race condition when extracting elements from register tiles'; code comment in the fix: ensure any previously scheduled threads have finished reading from scratch.
driver: A Warp Python kernel launched with wp.launch_tiled that calls wp.tile_extract(t, i, j) repeatedly in a loop (see warp/tests/test_tile.py, test names unverified); block_dim 64-256.
build_notes: Kernels are JIT-compiled by NVRTC at first launch (jit:true). Build Warp from source at the parent commit: python build_lib.py --cuda_path <CUDA> (no LLVM needed with --no_standalone), pip install -e .; tile support in this snapshot was still pre-1.5 development.
dispute_points: JIT-generated cubin; the detector needs to instrument modules loaded at run time. Tile.h is a library header not a user kernel, so racy accesses are in the NVRTC-compiled module.

kernel: wp::tile_shared_t<T,M,N,...>::operator=(const T&) / assign(register tile) / copy_from_global (wp.tile_load(..., storage='shared') in a dynamic loop)
location_buggy: warp/native/tile.h at 13361320: tile_shared_t::assign L691-L712, operator=(const T&) L643-L650, copy_from_global L879-L970 - each re-initialises the tile's shared data then WP_TILE_SYNC; nothing syncs BEFORE the re-initialisation
race_description: A shared-memory tile that is (re)initialised inside a dynamic loop (e.g. 'for i in range(x): tile = wp.tile_load(arr, i, TILE, storage=shared); ... read tile ...') is overwritten in iteration i+1 by fast threads while slower threads are still reading it in iteration i. The tile helpers only synchronise after the write.
fix_summary: Tracks whether a shared tile is already initialised and issues WP_TILE_SYNC() before any re-initialisation (assign, operator=, copy_from_global) - at some performance cost (CHANGELOG notes lower perf).
evidence: Commit/CHANGELOG: 'Add an implicit tile synchronization whenever a shared memory tile's data is reinitialized (e.g. in dynamic loops). This could result in lower performance.'
driver: Warp Python kernel with tile_load(storage='shared') inside a runtime-bounded for loop launched via wp.launch_tiled with block_dim>=64. Releases: the fix's CHANGELOG entry sits in the unreleased section directly above '## [1.5.1] - 2025-01-02', so the first release containing it is the one after 1.5.1 (presumably 1.6.0; unverified) - warp-lang 1.5.1 should contain the bug.
build_notes: pip install warp-lang==1.5.1 (assumed buggy; prebuilt libwarp + NVRTC JIT at run time) vs the next release (assumed fixed) - verify by grepping warp/native/tile.h in the installed package for 'initialized'. Needs a CUDA 12.x driver; sm_89 supported by NVRTC.
dispute_points: JIT'd kernels; racy accesses exist only in the NVRTC output. Race requires dynamic loop re-using the same tile variable.

kernel: reduceValue() device helper used by computeCenterPosition/computeRg (rg.cc), computeRMSDPart1.. (rmsd.cc), orientation restraint kernels
location_buggy: platforms/common/src/kernels/rg.cc:L4-L20 (race between L9-L13 and L14-L18); rmsd.cc:L7-L23 (L12-L16 vs L17-L21); orientationRestraintForce.cc:L4-L19 (L9-L13 vs L14-L18) at buggy_commit
race_description: reduceValue does a tree reduction in shared 'temp'. The first loop (step<32) only uses SYNC_WARPS (__syncwarp), after which temp[0], temp[32], temp[64].. hold per-warp partial sums. The second loop (step>=32) immediately lets thread 0 read temp[32] (written by thread 32 in the warp-level loop's last step), i.e. a cross-warp read of data written by another warp with no __syncthreads in between.
fix_summary: Inserts SYNC_THREADS between the warp-level loop and the cross-warp loop in all three copies of reduceValue.
evidence: Commit title 'Fixed a GPU thread synchronization bug' (PR #5346), 3 files x 1 line. The code was introduced recently (rg.cc in 1b6236a8, 2025-08-14), so the buggy commit is recent and builds with current CUDA.
driver: OpenMM unit tests TestCudaRGForce, TestCudaRMSDForce, TestCudaOrientationRestraintForce (platforms/cuda/tests, shared bodies in tests/TestRGForce.h etc.): 20-50 particles, thread block 256 (blockSize=min(256,maxThreadBlockSize) in CommonKernels.cpp), a few dozen kernel launches; far below 1e8 accesses.
build_notes: Check out buggy_commit; cmake -DOPENMM_BUILD_CUDA_LIB=ON -DOPENMM_BUILD_OPENCL_LIB=OFF -DOPENMM_BUILD_CUDA_TESTS=ON -DOPENMM_BUILD_PYTHON_WRAPPERS=OFF (no swig needed), then build targets OpenMM, OpenMMCUDA, TestCudaRGForce, TestCudaRMSDForce, TestCudaOrientationRestraintForce. Kernels are compiled at run time with NVRTC (default CudaCompiler); the kernel source is embedded at build time, so edits to *.cc need a rebuild. Because kernels are JIT-compiled the detector must hook the NVRTC-produced module (jit:true).
dispute_points: Reduction result is numerically correct in practice because the hardware warp-level ordering usually makes the read late enough, and the test only compares to ~1e-6; only the sanitizer/detector sees it. temp is declared volatile, which does not give ordering across warps.

kernel: reduceValue() in rmsd.cu (called three times in a row: center.x/.y/.z in computeRMSDPart1)
location_buggy: platforms/cuda/src/kernels/rmsd.cu:L7-L21 (temp[thread]=value at L9, return temp[0] at L21; consecutive calls at L36-L38) at buggy_commit. In HEAD the same code lives in platforms/common/src/kernels/rmsd.cc:L7-L24 and the fix is the first SYNC_THREADS inside reduceValue.
race_description: reduceValue ends with 'return temp[0]' read by every thread. The next call (center.y after center.x, center.z after center.y) starts with 'temp[thread]=value' with no barrier first, so thread 0 (or any thread in a faster warp) can overwrite temp[0] with the next partial sum while slower threads/warps are still reading temp[0] from the previous call.
fix_summary: Adds __syncthreads() at the top of reduceValue, before overwriting the shared buffer.
evidence: Commit 'Fixed race condition' (peastman, 2018-02-07), one __syncthreads added in the CUDA kernel and one barrier(CLK_LOCAL_MEM_FENCE) in the OpenCL twin.
driver: TestCudaRMSDForce (platforms/cuda/tests, body tests/TestRMSDForce.h): 20 particles, single 256-thread work group, 3 back-to-back reduceValue calls per evaluation.

location_buggy: platforms/cuda/src/kernels/customNonbondedGroups.cu:L123-L178 (shared volatile flag declared L139; loop condition read L158; write L168; end-of-iteration SYNC_WARPS at L171) at buggy_commit. HEAD equivalent: platforms/common/src/kernels/customNonbondedGroups.cc:L155-L195, the fix is the SYNC_WARPS at L176.
race_description: Every lane evaluates the loop condition !anyInteraction[local_warp] (volatile shared flag, one per warp) at the top of each iteration, while any lane that finds an interacting pair in the loop body writes anyInteraction[local_warp]=true (L168). Nothing orders the condition reads of the slower lanes before the body write of the faster lane (the only __syncwarp is at the end of the iteration, L171), so a lane can observe true in the same iteration in which others observed false and lanes leave the loop in different iterations, after which the per-lane shared-memory accesses diverge.
fix_summary: Adds SYNC_WARPS (=__syncwarp) as the first statement of the loop body.
evidence: Commit 'Added missing synchronization' (2018-04-25), a follow-up to the Volta fix 9f92ae40 (openmm-5) in the same file.

location_buggy: platforms/cuda/src/kernels/customNonbondedGroups.cu:L26-L86 at buggy_commit (per-lane init of localData L37-L44; rotating loop L46-L77 with localData[localIndex].f* += at L70-L72). HEAD equivalent: platforms/common/src/kernels/customNonbondedGroups.cc:L76-L121 (reduceMax at L76, SYNC_WARPS at L77, L111, L121).
race_description: Each lane first writes its own localData[threadIdx.x] (positions/params, zeroed forces) and then loops j=rangeStart..rangeEnd reading and accumulating (+=) into localData[tbx+tj], an entry owned by another lane, with tj rotating so that in lockstep every lane touches a distinct entry. The per-lane trip count (rangeEnd-rangeStart) differs between lanes and there is no __syncwarp between the initialisation and the loop or between iterations, so under independent thread scheduling lanes drift apart: a lane can read another lane's entry before it is initialised and two lanes can += the same entry in different iterations (lost update).
fix_summary: Makes all lanes run the same number of iterations (rangeStop = rangeStart + warp-wide max via __shfl_xor reduceMax, guarded by 'if (j < rangeEnd)') and adds SYNC_WARPS before the loop and at the end of every iteration and after the final atomicAdds.
evidence: Commit 'Fixed incorrect synchronization on Volta' (2018-04-20); the diff adds reduceMax guarded by __CUDA_ARCH__>=700 and __syncwarp calls. Follow-up 'Added missing synchronization' f1bbb8e7 is openmm-4.
driver: TestCudaCustomNonbondedForce interaction group tests (testInteractionGroups, testLargeInteractionGroup; tests/TestCustomNonbondedForce.h) with ranges of unequal size per tile; hundreds of atoms.

kernel: computeParameters (CUDA/NVRTC kernel of CudaCalcNonbondedForceKernel; grid-stride over atoms, exceptions and exclusions)
location_buggy: platforms/cuda/src/kernels/nonbondedParameters.cu:L19-L46 (loop 1 writes posq[i].w / charge[i] and sigmaEpsilon[i]) vs L69-L88 (loop 3 reads posq[atoms.x].w, posq[atoms.y].w, charge[], sigmaEpsilon[]) at the buggy commit; HEAD equivalent platforms/common/src/kernels/nonbondedParameters.cc has the separate computeExclusionParameters kernel
race_description: One launch (grid-stride, threads = padded atoms) first stores the updated charge and sigma/epsilon of atom i, then, in a later loop of the same kernel, each thread handling exclusion k reads the charges and sigma/epsilon of atoms atoms.x and atoms.y. Those values are written by whichever thread owns the atom, usually in another block, with no grid-wide barrier, so the exclusion parameters may be computed from stale charges. Only matters when HAS_EXCLUSIONS (Ewald/PME/LJPME) and the kernel runs (parameters changed or offsets present).
fix_summary: Moves the exclusion loop into a new kernel computeExclusionParameters launched after computeParameters (kernel boundary = grid barrier); host code adds the second launch for CUDA and OpenCL.
evidence: Commit message is just 'Fixed race condition' (P. Eastman, 2019-06-11); the diff splits one kernel into two so the exclusion loop runs after all charges are stored.
driver: TestCudaNonbondedForce (platforms/cuda/tests/TestCudaNonbondedForce.cpp including tests/TestNonbondedForce.h) PME/Ewald tests with exclusions, e.g. testEwaldPME or testLargeSystem with a few thousand particles; computeParameters runs on the first execute because recomputeParams is true. The kernel is a 1-2 block launch for small systems, so use at least a few thousand atoms to get several blocks.
build_notes: cmake -DOPENMM_BUILD_CUDA_LIB=ON -DOPENMM_BUILD_OPENCL_LIB=OFF -DOPENMM_BUILD_CUDA_TESTS=ON -DOPENMM_BUILD_PYTHON_WRAPPERS=OFF, target TestCudaNonbondedForce. The 2019 buggy commit will not build with CUDA 13 as is; build HEAD (kernel sources are embedded and NVRTC-compiled at run time, jit:true) and re-merge the two kernels by hand (move the body of computeExclusionParameters back after the exceptions loop of computeParameters, drop the second launch in platforms/common/src/CommonKernels.cpp).
already_reported_check: Not searched on GitHub issues.
dispute_points: Commit message gives no evidence; the mechanism is inferred from the diff (it is the only data dependency between the two loops). Re-creating the buggy code on HEAD needs a hand edit in common code. The stale-read window is tiny on hardware, so the effect is mostly invisible; a happens-before detector should still flag it.

kernel: computeRange (single-block min/max reduction used by CudaSort)
location_buggy: platforms/cuda/src/kernels/sort.cu:L67-L83 at the buggy commit (L75 'minimum = rangeBuffer[0];' vs L76 'rangeBuffer[threadIdx.x] = maximum;')
race_description: After the min tree reduction every thread reads rangeBuffer[0]; the very next statement makes every thread overwrite rangeBuffer[threadIdx.x] with its max, including thread 0 writing rangeBuffer[0]. With no barrier between them a thread in another warp can still be reading rangeBuffer[0] when thread 0's warp overwrites it, so the minimum seen can be a max.
fix_summary: Adds one __syncthreads() between 'minimum = rangeBuffer[0]' and the reuse of rangeBuffer for the maximum.
evidence: Commit 'Fixes a race-condition in compute Range' (Y. Zhao, 2013-05-14), 1 line added.

Stock sizes give about 10^5 thread accesses (unverified count).

location_buggy: platforms/cuda/src/kernels/findInteractingBlocks.cu:L337-L347 at the buggy commit (L337-L338 'if (!bufferFull && valuesInBuffer == BUFFER_GROUPS) bufferFull = true;', L340 __syncthreads, L341 'if (bufferFull)', L344-L346 'if (threadIdx.x==0) bufferFull=false; __syncthreads();' inside the if)
race_description: bufferFull is a shared flag. In an iteration where the buffer is not full the barrier at L346 is skipped, so a fast thread can go on to the next iteration and write bufferFull = true (L338) while a slow thread has not yet executed the 'if (bufferFull)' test of the previous iteration (L341). The slow thread then sees true, enters the store branch (which contains __syncthreads) alone while its block-mates skip it: a read/write race on bufferFull that also causes barrier divergence.
fix_summary: Moves the __syncthreads() out of the 'if (bufferFull)' body so every thread executes it after the test in every iteration.
evidence: Commit 'Fixes a race condition in buffer status in findBlocksWithInteractions()' (Y. Zhao, 2013-04-15); same function got a further one-line barrier fix 81753737 nine days later (rejected: mechanism not demonstrable).
driver: OpenMM CUDA tests that use the cutoff neighbour list with enough blocks per row to fill the buffer, e.g. TestCudaNonbondedForce testLargeSystem / TestCudaCustomGBForce with a few thousand atoms (BUFFER_GROUPS tiles per thread must be reached, so a large dense system). The kernel runs once per neighbour-list rebuild.
build_notes: 2013 tree compiled by nvcc at run time; not buildable with CUDA 13. HEAD's findInteractingBlocks.cu was reworked, so revert is not possible there; would need the kernel extracted with its #defines (BUFFER_SIZE, GROUP_SIZE, TILE_SIZE, ...). Hence build_cost high.
already_reported_check: Not searched on GitHub issues.
dispute_points: Old, and the kernel has since been restructured. The race is on a one-word flag and the failure mode (barrier divergence) may deadlock or silently skip stores, so detectors may report it as a race on bufferFull. Mechanism derived from reading the code; commit message only names the race.

location_buggy: src/atomicCAS-cuda/kernels.h:L2-L85 (plain `ret = *address` seeds at L5, L19, L33, L45, L59, L73) at buggy_commit
race_description: Hand-written CAS-loop atomic (64-bit atomic min/add) starts from a plain (non-atomic) load of the target word and then loops on atomicCAS. The plain load races with atomicCAS/atomic stores performed by other threads on the same word (plain read vs atomic RMW; SuperCollider calls these 'clobbered reads'). Value-wise the idiom is benign (a stale seed only costs another CAS iteration).
fix_summary: Replaces the plain seed load with a relaxed atomic load (`__nv_atomic_load_n(..., __NV_ATOMIC_RELAXED)` when CUDA_VERSION >= 12080, else keeps the plain load), and uses a local pointer in the atomicCAS call.
evidence: Commit subject: 'try to address memory races' (atomicCAS-cuda/hip). SuperCollider Table 6 lists atomicCAS among HeCBench apps with detected races.
driver: src/atomicCAS-cuda: `./main <n>` (Makefile `./main 10000`).
build_notes: cd src/atomicCAS-cuda && make ARCH=sm_89 EXTRA_CFLAGS=-lineinfo (plain nvcc Makefile, no external deps unless noted).
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream). SuperCollider (PLDI 2026) lists HeCBench as a suite where it found races; the maintainer thanked a reporter and updated the programs.
dispute_points: Classic benign CAS-seed idiom: a strict-C++-memory-model race, not a functional bug. The fixed version only differs when built with CUDA >= 12.8 (CUDA_VERSION >= 12080), which is the case for CUDA 13.x on the cluster. A detector that models volatile/relaxed as atomic would stop reporting it after the fix.
