driver: src/scatter-cuda: `./main <n> <repeat>` (Makefile `./main 10000000 100`); use `./main 100000 1`.
build_notes: cd src/scatter-cuda && make ARCH=sm_89 EXTRA_CFLAGS=-lineinfo (plain nvcc Makefile, no external deps unless noted).
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream). SuperCollider (PLDI 2026) lists HeCBench as a suite where it found races; the maintainer thanked a reporter and updated the programs.
dispute_points: Classic benign CAS-seed idiom: a strict-C++-memory-model race, not a functional bug. The fixed version only differs when built with CUDA >= 12.8 (CUDA_VERSION >= 12080), which is the case for CUDA 13.x on the cluster. A detector that models volatile/relaxed as atomic would stop reporting it after the fix. The same idiom exists in pytorch_scatter (not examined here).

location_buggy: paddle/operators/conv_shift_op.cu:L38-L78 at 3dc88342 (early 'else { return; }' at ~L66 before __syncthreads at ~L68)
race_description: In the last x-block (num_x = x_width % blockDim.x < blockDim.x) threads with tx >= num_x take the 'else return' path before the __syncthreads(). Those same threads, however, have already executed the cooperative load loop (for j = tx; j < y_width; j += blockDim.x) that writes sy[j] and sx_pad[j] in shared memory, which the surviving threads read in the dot-product loop after the barrier. The barrier is therefore executed by only part of the block (divergent __syncthreads), so the hand-off of the exited threads' shared-memory writes is not guaranteed by the barrier.
fix_summary: Removed the early return; the shared-memory load stays under if (tx < num_x), every thread reaches __syncthreads(), and the compute+store is wrapped in if (tx < num_x).
evidence: Commit title 'conv shift: fix return before syncthreads' (no body, no PR link, no sanitizer output).
driver: Op unit test python/paddle/v2/framework/tests/test_conv_shift_op.py (path unverified at this commit) or a standalone launch: x_width not a multiple of 256 (e.g. 300 or 1000), y_width odd (e.g. 5), batch 2; grid (DivUp(x_width,256), batch), block 256, dynamic smem (256+2*y_width)*4. <10^6 accesses.
build_notes: Kernel is self-contained (no Paddle types except the op wrapper): copy ConvShiftForward<T> L38-L78 into a .cu harness, drop the Paddle includes, compile for sm_89. Do not build Paddle 2017.
dispute_points: Low confidence as a *hardware-observable* race. Real GPUs count exited threads as arrived at bar.sync, so results were most likely correct; this is barrier divergence (synccheck class) that a happens-before detector may or may not flag depending on how it treats exited threads. Treat as a test of the early-exit-before-barrier label rather than a ground-truth data race. Also at the buggy commit num_x evaluates to 0 for the last block when x_width % blockDim.x == 0 (separate logic issue, not touched by this fix). Op is from 2017; whether it still exists at HEAD is unverified.

kernel: inclusive_sum_scan_kernel (device helper) called from auc_kernel (metric_ops.cu) and index_select_scalar_cumsum_kernel / asynchronous_complete_cumsum (jagged_tensor_ops.cu)
location_buggy: fbgemm_gpu/include/fbgemm_gpu/fbgemm_cuda_utils.cuh:L3134-L3153 at buggy_commit: producer `block_sums[block_id] = ...; __threadfence(); atomicAdd(&block_flags[block_id],1)` L3149-L3152 vs consumer spin `while (atomicAdd(&block_flags[block_id-1],0) < signal)` L3140 followed by plain load `block_sums[block_id-1]` L3144
race_description: Single-pass (stream) scan across thread blocks: block b publishes its running sum to block_sums[b] and then raises block_flags[b]; block b+1 spins on the flag with an atomic read and afterwards reads block_sums[b] with an ordinary, non-volatile load and no acquire fence. The consumer-side load is therefore not ordered after the flag observation (it may be satisfied from a stale L1 line or hoisted by the compiler), so block b+1 can consume a stale partial sum.
fix_summary: Declares the block_sums parameter `volatile` so the consumer's loads are not cached or reordered by the compiler; no fence is added.
evidence: Commit message (PR #1739): block_sums has to be volatile 'to prevent the compiler from caching the results in registers' so sums are visible for inter-block consumption. No sanitizer output.
driver: fbgemm_gpu/test/metric_ops_test.py exercises auc_kernel (multi-block when num_entries exceeds MAX_ENTRIES_PER_BLOCK); the cumsum path is torch.ops.fbgemm.asynchronous_complete_cumsum on a long 1-D tensor (multi-block when grid_size>1, block_flags allocated at jagged_tensor_ops.cu L3282). Alternative: copy inclusive_sum_scan_kernel into a 30-line harness (cub::BlockScan, 8-64 blocks, 128 threads) - well under 1e8 accesses.
build_notes: Full FBGEMM-GPU build needs torch; prefer the standalone harness: the helper depends only on cub::BlockScan and __threadfence/atomicAdd. Cross-block spin requires all blocks of the grid to be co-resident or lower-indexed blocks to be scheduled first (true in practice; keep the grid below the number of SMs times occupancy).
already_reported_check: n/a (fixed upstream 2023-05-01).
dispute_points: Race existence rests on the CUDA memory model (no acquire on the consumer side); the producer already has __threadfence. The fix (volatile) does not add a fence either, so a strict release/acquire-based detector may still flag the fixed code; a detector that models L1 staleness or `volatile` as relaxed-atomic will treat the fixed version as clean. Observable failures need the consumer block to have previously cached block_sums[b] or the compiler to hoist the load.

kernel: plan_compress_prefill_kernel0 (DeepSeek-V4 c128/c4 compression plan, 1024-thread single-block kernel)
location_buggy: python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/c_plan.cuh:L157-L160 (`if (tx < kNumWarps) { warp_max[tx] = 0; warp_min[tx] = 0xFFFFFFFFu; }`) vs L166-L167 (`warp_max[warp_id] = warp::reduce_max(e_for_max); warp_min[warp_id] = warp::reduce_min(e_for_min);`) at d21eefc9; first __syncthreads is only at L168
race_description: Threads 0..31 (warp 0) initialise warp_max[0..31]/warp_min[0..31] to identity values, while every warp w writes its reduction result into warp_max[w]/warp_min[w]. There is no barrier between the init store (warp 0, lane w) and the result store (warp w), so when warp w is faster the init overwrites the result with 0 / 0xFFFFFFFF and the later max/min over warps (L170-L171) gives wrong s_max_extend / s_min_extend, flipping the is_mtp_extend decision.
fix_summary: Deletes the redundant initialisation (5 lines); every warp unconditionally writes its slot before the first __syncthreads anyway.
evidence: PR 32467 title 'Fix race in c128 prefill plan kernel on ragged extend'; diff only removes the init block. No sanitizer log. Derived race by reading the kernel.
driver: JIT kernel in sglang (python/sglang/kernels/jit); exercised by the DeepSeek-V4 compressed-attention planning path (sglang.srt.layers.attention.deepseek_v4_backend). Standalone test file unverified (python/sglang/test/kernels/deepseek_v4/ has helpers). A direct harness: compile c_plan.cuh's plan_compress_prefill_kernel0 with a small batch_size (<=1024), seq_lens/extend_lens arrays, and 1024 threads. Tiny.
build_notes: Kernel is built through sglang's JIT infrastructure (tvm-ffi / torch cpp extension with nvcc) and uses sgl_kernel device helpers (warp::reduce_max/min, SGL_DEVICE) from python/sglang/kernels/jit/include; extracting plan_compress_prefill_kernel0 into a stand-alone .cu requires copying those headers. Needs CUDA 13-capable nvcc.
dispute_points: Very small kernel; the WAW is genuine but its observable effect is limited to the is_mtp_extend heuristic. Driver is unverified; JIT.

location_buggy: csrc/persistent_topk.cuh:L890-L909 at bcf5cac9 (CTA 0 zero-inits state->histogram/arrival_counter/etc. with plain stores + __syncthreads) vs CTA 1..n-1 red_release(&state->arrival_counter, 1) at L706/L755/L839 and atomic histogram updates
race_description: The per-group RadixRowState lives in global memory. CTA 0 initialises it (plain stores) and only an intra-CTA __syncthreads orders that; the other CTAs of the group start their first red.release.gpu on arrival_counter (and atomicAdds into histograms) with no inter-CTA ordering to CTA 0's init. CTA 0's late zero store can overwrite an already incremented arrival_counter, making later wait_ge barriers return early or hang. (A second, cross-launch issue: the counter is never reset, so a stale large value from the previous call is also seen.)
fix_summary: Removed the in-kernel init; host code now does cudaMemsetAsync(workspace, 0, state_bytes, stream) before the launch when the cooperative radix path will run.
evidence: PR 41444 (zyongye): 'no inter-CTA synchronization between CTA-0's init writes and CTA-1+'s first red_release', 'two distinct races'; author notes the window is masked in practice by the ~1e4-cycle chunk-load stage. No sanitizer log.
driver: tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py::test_persistent_topk_correctness / test_persistent_topk_algorithm_paths / test_persistent_topk_stress (torch.ops._C.persistent_topk). Rows must exceed RADIX_THRESHOLD = 32768 elements to hit the cooperative radix path, with <= 32 rows. persistent_topk.cuh includes only cuda/cub, so a standalone main() launching persistent_topk_kernel<2048,1> (params per csrc/topk.cu launch_persistent_topk) is realistic and far cheaper than a full vLLM build. ~32k-64k elements x a few rows x ~4 radix passes ~ 1e6 accesses.
build_notes: Persistent path requires max opt-in shared memory >= 128 KB per block (kFixedSmemLarge + shared_ordered; per PR text 'devices with max_smem >= 128KB'), i.e. sm_80/sm_90/sm_100 -- NOT sm_89 (99 KB), so on this cluster only the H100 can run it (flag needs_sm90 although no sm_90 instruction is used). Standalone build: nvcc -arch=sm_90 -std=c++17 harness.cu (header-only kernel + cub).
dispute_points: Author concedes the in-launch race is 'masked' by timing in practice and that the dominant failure was cross-launch stale state (not a within-launch race, so out of detector scope). A race detector will only see the within-launch plain-store vs atomic conflict if its model treats CTA-0's init and CTA-1's red.release as unordered, which they are. Needs the H100.

kernel: _fwd_kernel_ep_scatter_1 (Triton; grid = num_experts programs, num_warps=8), called from ep_scatter()
location_buggy: vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/deep_gemm_utils.py:L69-L97 at cd32d6f5 (`tl.store(expert_start_loc + offset_cumsum, cumsum, mask=...)` L79 followed by `cur_expert_start = tl.load(expert_start_loc + cur_expert)` L81)
race_description: Every program (one per expert) computes the full cumulative-sum vector of aligned per-expert token counts, stores all of it to the global array expert_start_loc, and then immediately loads element cur_expert of the same array. In Triton the element is stored by whichever thread owns it in the vector layout and loaded by a different thread, with no barrier between the global store and the load (RAW across warps of the CTA); in addition all num_experts programs write identical values to the same addresses concurrently (cross-block WAW) while others read them.
fix_summary: Extracts the block's own offset from the register vector (tl.sum of tl.where(offset_cumsum == cur_expert, cumsum, 0)) and stores only expert_start_loc[cur_expert], so there is no store-then-load through global memory; also drops num_stages=4 on the loop and adds an assert on expert_start_loc.shape.
evidence: PR title '[Bugfix] ep_scatter kernel store-load race condition (#34991)'; the added code comment says the offset is taken from the register vector (warp shuffle), with no global memory round-trip. No sanitizer log.
driver: Call vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.deep_gemm_utils.ep_scatter directly with synthetic CUDA tensors (recv_x (T,H) fp8, recv_x_scale, recv_topk (T,topk) int, num_recv_tokens_per_expert (E,) int, expert_map=None, expert_start_loc (E,) int32, output_tensor, output_tensor_scale, m_indices filled with -1 of length multiple of 128, output_index); E=8..64, T=256, H=128. First kernel touches only E*(E+tokens) elements, well under 1e6. No existing unit test for ep_scatter found in the tree listing (tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_deepgemm.py is unrelated; could not grep the tree, so unverified).
build_notes: pip install a vLLM wheel that contains the buggy file (any release between the introduction of ep_scatter and 2026-03-12), or check out cd32d6f5 and `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 pip install -e .`; the module only needs torch + triton + vllm imports, so a stub that exec()s the single file after providing vllm.utils helpers also works (unverified). Triton compiles the kernel for sm_89; no DeepGEMM install needed to call ep_scatter itself.
dispute_points: Triton kernel (jit: true). Hardware effect is tiny: all writers store identical values, and a thread loading a not-yet-stored element would read the stale previous contents of expert_start_loc, which is why the bug is reported as a store-load race rather than a wrong-output issue; the detector must see the PTX/SASS of the Triton-compiled cubin. Whether Triton inserts a barrier between the store and the load depends on the Triton version (it does not for global memory).

kernel: sample_recovered_tokens_kernel (Triton; grid (batch_size, max_spec_len), NO_DRAFT_PROBS=True path used for n-gram draft)
location_buggy: vllm/v1/sample/rejection_sampler.py:L598-L636 at 04d1dd7f (orig_prob load L601, `tl.store(target_probs_ptr + ... + draft_token_id, 0)` L606-L608, full-row `tl.load(... + vocab_offset)` L609-L612, restore store L632-L636)
race_description: To exclude the draft token the kernel temporarily overwrites target_probs[row, draft_token_id] with 0 in global memory, then loads the whole row (PADDED_VOCAB_SIZE elements spread over the program's warps) and finally writes the saved value back. The scalar store, the vectorised row load and the restore store are executed by different threads of the program with no barrier between them, so some threads can load the old (unzeroed) value or the restored one, making the argmax pick the draft token itself. The write also mutates an input tensor in place.
fix_summary: Removes the store/restore pair and instead masks the draft token out of the load (`mask=(vocab_offset < vocab_size) & (vocab_offset != draft_token_id)`).
evidence: PR title '[bugfix] [spec-decoding] fix data race in sample_recovered_tokens_kernel (vLLM v1) (#23829)'; the diff deletes the temporary zero-out and restore.
driver: tests/v1/sample/test_rejection_sampler.py (exercises vllm.v1.sample.rejection_sampler.rejection_sample with draft_probs=None, which selects NO_DRAFT_PROBS=True; individual test names unverified), or call sample_recovered_tokens directly: batch 4-8, max_spec_len 4, vocab 32000-128000 so the row spans several warps (PADDED_VOCAB_SIZE=2^k >= vocab). A few 1e6 accesses.
build_notes: pip install a vLLM wheel older than 2025-08-29 (v0.10.1.x or earlier; check that it contains rejection_sampler.py with this kernel), or `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 pip install -e .` at 04d1dd7f. The Triton kernel itself needs only torch + triton; no custom CUDA op is involved in this path.
dispute_points: Triton kernel, so the detector must see the JIT-compiled cubin. Triton's own lowering decides which thread executes the scalar store and whether it inserts a barrier (it does not for global memory); the race only changes results when a thread loads the row element before the zero-store becomes visible, which is timing dependent, hence only a bug in principle until someone observes the wrong recovered token.

location_buggy: examples/93_blackwell_low_latency_gqa/tgv_gqa.cuh:L444-L446 (lane 0 of each warp writes smem(warp_idx,i)), L450 (named barrier), L453-L463 (lane 0 reads smem(j,i) of all warps); call at L1352 inside the `for kv_tile` loop L1310-L1438 with no further epilog_barrier in the loop; pinned HEAD 56ca28ad (2026-10-13)
race_description: cta_reduce has a single named barrier between the partial-result writes and the cross-warp reads and none afterwards. The caller invokes it once per KV tile reusing the same sFmaxPartial scratch; a fast epilog warp can enter the next tile's cta_reduce and overwrite smem(warp_idx,i) while another warp's lane 0 is still reading the previous tile's partials (L458).

verify.notes: I traced the barrier chain. BMM1(n+1) waits only on the epilog warps' arrive at L1329 (before cta_reduce) and on the K tile, so it can complete while warp A is still reading; the warps' arrives on tmasoftmax_bmm2_full_barrier (L1436, after the reads) gate BMM2(n), which in the MMA warp is issued after BMM1(n+1), and the epilog's wait on bmm2_epilog_full_barrier (L1390) is after cta_reduce in the same iteration. kernel: cv::cudev::block_reduce_detail::Generic<N>::reduce (instantiated via cv::cudev::blockReduce<N> with non-power-of-2 N or N>1024)
location_buggy: modules/cudev/include/opencv2/cudev/block/detail/reduce.hpp:L254-L315 (warp-synchronous tail: 'if (tid < 32) merge(...,32)' then 'if (tid < 16) { merge 16,8,4,2,1 }') at opencv_contrib HEAD eca97a4adb2fa32afc82478947d7f049fce57ee1
race_description: The generic block reduction ends with a legacy warp-synchronous tail on a volatile shared buffer: lanes tid<16 execute merge(smem,val,tid,16), merge(...,8), merge(...,4), merge(...,2), merge(...,1) back to back; each step reads smem[tid+k] written by lane tid+k in the previous step, with no __syncwarp (the file has none) and no __syncthreads. Under Volta+ independent thread scheduling lanes of the divergent 'if (tid<16)' region are not guaranteed to advance in lock-step, so step j+1 may read smem written by a lane that has not yet performed step j.
evidence: No issue found. Sibling code in the same library (warp/scan.hpp) was already ported to shfl_up_sync for CUDA>=9, and Dispatcher routes power-of-2 sizes <=1024 to WarpOptimized/GenericOptimized32 that use shfl for CV_CUDEV_ARCH>=300, so only the Generic path is left.
driver: Any cudev kernel calling cv::cudev::blockReduce<N>(smem, val, tid, op) with N not a power of two or >1024 (e.g. a small test kernel with N=96, 160 or 2048); otherwise OpenCV tests rarely reach Generic. Unverified which in-tree kernel instantiates it; a custom 100-line driver is needed.
build_notes: cudev is header-only: include opencv2/cudev/block/reduce.hpp from a standalone .cu compiled with nvcc and -I pointing at opencv_contrib/modules/cudev/include plus a minimal OpenCV core include path (needs opencv2/core/cvdef.hpp, cuda_types); no full OpenCV build required beyond cmake-generated cvconfig/opencv_modules headers, so copy the needed headers or build only core+cudev.
already_reported_check: git log on the clone for race/sync/volatile in cudev: no commit found touching this tail; no web search.
dispute_points: A skeptic will say: dead/rarely used code (Dispatcher picks shfl-based variants for the common sizes), the pattern is the textbook volatile warp-synchronous idiom, and nobody has observed wrong results. Instantiation with the right N is contrived, so impact is low; it is mainly a cheap synthetic target for ITS-aware race detection.
